pages.name: Home
pages.description: Home is the first screen after signing in.
pages.summary:
Home is the first screen after signing in. The band across the top greets you, shows the time in your profile timezone, and lists what needs you right now as clickable chips: unassigned and at-risk shipments (when you can read shipments), plus counts from the billing queue, pending approvals, reconciliation exceptions, service failures, EDI problems and decisions waiting on the desk. Each chip opens the page that holds those items. When nothing is flagged it says you're clear.

Below the band is a grid of widgets: queues, metrics, report tiles, dashboards, insights and announcements. Your administrator can give each role a preset home screen; you can customize your own copy unless the administrator has locked it.

tasks.title: Jump to what needs attention
steps: Open [Home](/).
Select a chip in the top band (for example unassigned, at risk or service failures) to open the page with those items.

tasks.title: Customize your home screen
steps: Open [Home](/) and select **Customize**.
Select **Add widget**, search or pick a category, and select a widget card to add it. Some widgets ask what to show before they land.
Drag widgets to rearrange them. Open a widget's menu to change its **Width** and **Height**, **Configure** what it shows, or **Remove** it.
Select **Save** in the floating bar, or **Done** in the top band. **Discard** throws the changes away.

tasks.title: Configure a widget
steps: Open [Home](/), select **Customize**, and open the widget's menu.

Select **Configure** and set what the widget offers, such as **Title**, **Metrics**, **Rows to show**, **Window (days)**, **Report** with **Shows as** (**Table**, **Chart** or **Single number**), **Dashboard** or **Announcement**.
Select **Save**, then save the layout.

tasks.title: Go back to the preset home screen
steps: Open [Home](/). A customized screen shows a small "Customized" chip above the widgets.
Select **Reset** on that chip to restore the preset (or the default home screen) and receive its future updates again.

pages.notes:
If **Customize** is disabled with a lock, your administrator manages this home screen and it cannot be changed from here. Home screen presets and role assignments are managed under [Home layouts](/admin/home-layouts).

A home screen holds a limited number of widgets; when it is full, remove one before adding another. Selecting **Done** without changing anything does not count as a customization, so you keep receiving preset updates.

pages.name: Accounting dashboard
pages.description: Receivables health, collections, and cash-flow at a glance.
pages.summary:
The accounting dashboard is the landing page of Accounting management. It shows the health of receivables at a glance: **AR outstanding**, **Days sales outstanding**, **Collection effectiveness**, **Unapplied cash** and the **Overdue** share, followed by a **DSO trend** chart, a **Cash-flow forecast — 90 days**, an **Aging** breakdown, **Collections performance**, the **Top overdue customers** and a **Collections worklist**.

Controllers, AR clerks and collections staff use it to decide where to spend the day: which customers to chase, how much cash is waiting to be applied, and how collections are trending. Until the first invoice posts from billing, the page shows **Nothing on the books yet** instead of the figures.

tasks.title: Check how receivables are doing
steps: Open [Accounting](/accounting).
Read the figures across the top: **AR outstanding**, **Days sales outstanding**, **Collection effectiveness**, **Unapplied cash** and **Overdue**.

Select **AR outstanding** to go to [AR aging](/accounting/ar/aging), **Unapplied cash** to go to [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments), or **Overdue** to go to [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items).

tasks.title: See which customers to chase
steps: Open [Accounting](/accounting).
Look at **Top overdue customers** and the **Collections worklist**. Worklist rows show how far past due an invoice is and flag **Disputed** and **Short-paid** invoices.
Select a customer or worklist row to open that customer in the [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger).
Select **View aging** to see every customer's balance by age, or **Open items** to see every outstanding invoice.

tasks.title: Switch the aging view
steps: Open [Accounting](/accounting).
In the **Aging** card, switch between the snapshot and trend views with the buttons in the card header.

tasks.title: Record a customer payment from the dashboard
steps: Open [Accounting](/accounting).
Select **Record payment** in the page header. This opens the record payment panel on [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments).

pages.notes:
Opening the dashboard needs read access to accounts receivable. **Record payment** only appears for people who can create customer payments.

The quick links at the bottom of the page jump to the other accounting pages, such as [Manual journals](/accounting/manual-journals), [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals), [Bank receipts](/accounting/reconciliation/bank-receipts), [Trial balance](/accounting/reports/trial-balance) and [Balance sheet](/accounting/reports/balance-sheet).

pages.name: AR aging
pages.description: Receivables aging by customer with drill-down to the ledger.
pages.summary: AR aging shows how much each customer owes, split by how late it is: **Current**, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days, with a **Total open** column and a totals row. Figures above the table give the **Total open**, **Current** and **Overdue** amounts, **Current DSO** and **CEI**, with a **Distribution** of the balance by age. Collections staff and controllers use it to see who owes what and how old it is, and to export the aging for month-end.

tasks.title: Review aging for all customers or one customer
steps: Open [AR aging](/accounting/ar/aging).
To narrow the list, pick a **Customer**. Leave it empty for all customers.
Select a column heading to sort by it.

tasks.title: Run aging as of an earlier date
steps: Open [AR aging](/accounting/ar/aging).
Set **As of date**. Leave it empty to age as of today.

tasks.title: Export the aging to a spreadsheet
steps: Open [AR aging](/accounting/ar/aging).
Set **Customer** and **As of date** if needed.
Select **Export CSV**. The file holds the rows currently shown.

tasks.title: Drill into a customer's ledger
steps: Open [AR aging](/accounting/ar/aging).
Select the customer's name in the **Customer** column. Their [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger) opens.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to accounts receivable.

pages.name: Customer ledger
pages.description: Statement-style transaction history with the customer's AR profile.
pages.summary:
The customer ledger shows one customer's receivables history as a running statement: every posting with its **Date**, **Document**, **Event**, **Source**, **Debit**, **Credit** and running **Balance**. Above it sits the customer's AR profile: **Open balance**, **Credit utilization**, **DSO / days to pay**, **Delinquency score**, a chart of **Payments — trailing 12 months** and **Account details** such as **Oldest open invoice**, **Last payment** and **Unapplied cash**.

AR clerks and collectors use it to answer a customer's balance questions, raise credit or debit memos, record payments and open a customer statement. The customer statement page shows an **Opening balance**, **Charges**, **Payments** and **Ending balance** for a date range, an **Aging summary**, the **Transaction history** and the customer's **Open items**.

tasks.title: Look up a customer's ledger
steps: Open [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger).
Pick the **Customer**. Their profile and ledger load below.

tasks.title: Export a customer's ledger
steps: Open [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger) and pick the **Customer**.
Select **Export**.

tasks.title: Open a customer statement
steps: Open [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger) and pick the **Customer**.
Select **Statement**. The customer statement opens.
Change **Statement date** or **Start date** to cover a different range.
Select **Back to open items** to go to [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items).

tasks.title: Raise a credit memo or debit memo for a customer
steps: Open [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger) and pick the **Customer**.
Select **Credit memo** or **Debit memo**.
Fill in **Reason**, and optionally **Memo date** and **Memo text**.
Under **Lines**, enter a **Description**, **Amount** and **Qty** for each line. Select **Add line** for more.
Turn on **Post immediately** to post the memo to the ledger in the same step.
Select **Create credit memo** or **Create debit memo**. The new memo opens in the invoice workspace.

tasks.title: Record a payment from the customer
steps: Open [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger) and pick the **Customer**.
Select **Record payment**. The record payment panel opens on [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments) with this customer filled in.

pages.notes: Opening the ledger or a customer statement needs read access to accounts receivable. **Credit memo** and **Debit memo** only appear for people who can create invoices, and **Record payment** only for people who can create customer payments.

pages.name: Invoice register
pages.description: Every invoice issued, with its bill-to, shipper, dates and settlement status.
pages.summary:
The invoice register lists every invoice your organization has issued, as a ledger rather than a work queue. Each row shows **Invoice #**, **Type**, **Status**, **Bill To**, **Shipper**, **Invoice date**, **Due date**, **Total**, **Open**, **Past due**, **Settlement**, **Dispute**, **EDI**, **Scope** and **Split**. The **Shipper** column is only filled in when the invoice bills someone other than the shipper.

Accounting and AR staff use it to look up any invoice, current or historical, check whether it has been paid, and jump to the invoice or the shipment behind it.

tasks.title: Find an invoice
steps: Open [Invoice register](/accounting/ar/invoices).
Type in the search box, or use **Filter** to add conditions on columns such as **Invoice #**, **Bill To**, **Status**, **Settlement**, **Dispute** or **Invoice date**.
Select a column heading to sort by it, for example **Due date** or **Open**.

tasks.title: Open an invoice
steps: Open [Invoice register](/accounting/ar/invoices).
Select the row or its **Invoice #**. The invoice opens in the [Invoices](/billing/invoices) workspace.
Or right-click the row and choose **Open in workspace**.

tasks.title: See the shipment an invoice billed
steps: Open [Invoice register](/accounting/ar/invoices).
Right-click the row and choose **View shipment**. The shipment opens in a new browser tab. The option only appears when the invoice is tied to a shipment.

tasks.title: Void an invoice
steps: Open [Invoice register](/accounting/ar/invoices).
Right-click the row and choose **Void**.
Enter the **Reason** and choose a **Freight disposition**: **Release freight for rebilling** sends the billing queue items back for a fresh invoice; **Do not rebill** cancels them.
Select **Void invoice**.

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to invoices. The register has no create button; invoices are created from the billing queue. - **Void** is unavailable once any payment has been applied to the invoice, and is hidden on invoices that are already voided. - A draft is voided at once. A posted invoice is voided through a full-reversal credit memo; when that reversal needs an approver, the dialog shows **Void requested; awaiting reversal approval** and the invoice reads voided only once the reversal is approved.

pages.name: Late charges
pages.description: Overdue invoices charged once per thirty-day period at each customer's rate, raised as one debit memo per customer.
pages.summary:
Late charges shows what the late-charge run would bill for overdue invoices, and lets you raise those charges now for the customers you choose. Each overdue invoice is charged once per thirty-day period at the customer's late charge rate, after their grace period, and each customer gets one debit memo per run.

The preview table groups lines by customer, with **Invoice**, **Period**, **Basis**, **Rate** and **Charge** for each overdue period and a total per customer. Customers the run would skip show the reason instead of a checkbox. AR staff use the page to check charges before they go out and to run them by hand.

tasks.title: Preview late charges
steps: Open [Late charges](/accounting/ar/late-charges).
Pick a **Customer** to see only that customer, or leave it on all customers.
Set **As of** to preview charges as of another date; it starts on today.
Select an invoice number to open the invoice.

tasks.title: Raise late charges now
steps: Open [Late charges](/accounting/ar/late-charges).
Tick the customers to charge, or tick the header box to select them all.
Select **Assess now**. The confirmation shows how many debit memos will be raised and their total.
Select **Assess late charges**. The table then shows each new debit memo number with **Posted** or **Draft**; select a memo number to open it.

tasks.title: Turn automatic late charges on or off
steps: Open **Billing controls** in the organization settings.
In the **Late charges** card, set **Assessment mode** to **Disabled**, **Preview only** or **Automatic**, and optionally a **Minimum late charge**.
Save the billing controls.

tasks.title: Set a customer's late charge rate
steps: Open [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers) and open the customer.
In their billing profile, turn on **Apply late charges** and fill in **Late charge rate** and **Grace period**.

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to accounts receivable. **Assess now** only appears for people who can create invoices. - A notice above the table says how the nightly run is set: **Automatic** raises and posts the memos each night, **Preview only** writes nothing, and **Disabled** means **Assess now** stays unavailable even though you can still preview. - Each invoice period is charged only once, so running again cannot double-charge a customer. - Customers whose charges for a run add up to less than the **Minimum late charge** are skipped.

pages.name: Open items
pages.description: Outstanding invoices and their payment status across all customers.
pages.summary:
Open items lists every invoice that still has money owing, across all customers: **Invoice**, **Customer**, **Type**, **PRO / BOL**, **Invoice date**, **Due date**, **Status**, **Total**, **Applied** and **Open**. Invoices under dispute show **Disputed** and short-paid invoices show **Short-paid**. Figures above the table give **Total open**, **Current**, **Overdue**, **Average age** and **Count**.

AR clerks use it to find what a customer owes, and to pick the invoices a payment should pay off.

tasks.title: Find open invoices
steps: Open [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items).
Pick a **Customer** to see only their invoices, or leave it on all customers.
Set **As of date** to see what was open on an earlier date.
Select a column heading to sort by it.

tasks.title: Apply a payment to selected invoices
steps: Open [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items).
Tick the invoices the payment covers. They must all belong to one customer.
Select **Apply payment**. The record payment panel opens on [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments) with the customer and invoices filled in.
Select **Clear** to drop the selection instead.

tasks.title: Record a payment
steps: Open [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items).
Select **Record payment** in the page header.

tasks.title: Open a customer's statement
steps: Open [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items).
Select the customer's name in the **Customer** column. Their customer statement opens.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to accounts receivable. **Record payment** and **Apply payment** only appear for people who can create customer payments.

pages.name: Customer payments
pages.description: Record, apply, and reverse customer payments with full GL traceability.
pages.summary:
Customer payments is where AR staff post money received from customers and apply it to their open invoices, all in one step, with the matching general ledger entries. Figures at the top show **Posted today**, **Unapplied cash** and **Reversed — 30 days**. The table lists each payment's **Status**, **Reference**, **Customer**, **Method**, **Payment date**, **Accounting date**, **Amount**, **Applied**, **Unapplied** and **Invoices**.

Selecting a payment opens its detail: the dates, method and reference, the invoices it was applied to, any short-pay written off, and the **GL postings** it created.

tasks.title: Record a customer payment
steps: Open [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments).
Select the New customer payment button in the table toolbar. The **Record payment** panel opens.

Pick the **Customer** and fill in **Payment amount**, **Payment method**, **Payment date** (when the funds arrived) and **Accounting date** (the GL date, which must fall in an open fiscal period). Add a **Reference number** such as the check number or ACH trace, and a **Memo** if needed.

Under **Apply to open invoices**, tick the invoices this payment pays and enter the **Applied** amount for each, or select **Auto-apply oldest first**. Enter a **Short-pay** amount on an invoice to write off the difference.
Select **Post payment**. Anything not applied stays on the payment as unapplied cash.

tasks.title: Apply unapplied cash later
steps: Open [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments) and select the payment.
Select **Apply unapplied**.
Set the **Accounting date**, tick the invoices and enter the amounts, then select **Apply cash**.

tasks.title: Reverse a payment
steps: Open [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments) and select the payment.
Select **Reverse**.
Enter the **Accounting date** and **Reason**, then select **Reverse payment**. The cash is backed out, the invoices it paid are reopened and a reversing GL entry is posted.

tasks.title: Check a payment's ledger entries
steps: Open [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments) and select the payment.
Look under **GL postings**, or select **Open full view** to see the entries on their own page.
Select the customer name under the amount to open their [Customer ledger](/accounting/ar/customer-ledger).

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to customer payments. **Apply unapplied** and **Reverse** need update access and only appear on posted payments; **Apply unapplied** only shows when the payment still has unapplied cash. - The payment cannot be posted if the applied total is more than the payment amount, or if any invoice would be paid past its open balance. - A reversal cannot be undone. - **Apply payment** on [Open items](/accounting/ar/open-items) opens this page's payment panel with the customer and chosen invoices already filled in.

pages.name: Account types
pages.description: Manage and configure account types for your organization
pages.summary:
Account types group your general ledger accounts under an accounting category. Each account type has a **Code**, a **Name**, a **Status**, a **Category** (**Asset**, **Liability**, **Equity**, **Revenue**, **Cost of Revenue** or **Expense**), and an optional **Description** and **Color**. The table shows **Status**, **Code**, **Name**, **Category**, **Description** and **Created At**.

Accounting administrators maintain the list when setting up or extending the chart of accounts.

tasks.title: Add an account type
steps: Open [Account types](/accounting/configuration-files/account-types).
Select **New account type**.
Fill in **Status**, **Code** (up to 10 characters), **Name** and **Category**. These are required.
Optionally add a **Description** and a **Color**.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** or **Save & add another** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit an account type
steps: Open [Account types](/accounting/configuration-files/account-types).
Find it with the search box or **Filter**, then select its row.
Change the fields and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate account types
steps: Open [Account types](/accounting/configuration-files/account-types).
To change one, select the status badge in its **Status** column and pick the new status.
To change several, tick the rows, choose **Update status** in the bar that appears and pick **Active** or **Inactive**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to account types. Adding needs create access; editing and changing status need update access.

pages.name: Fiscal years
pages.description: Manage and configure fiscal years for your organization
pages.summary:
Fiscal years set the accounting calendar that every ledger posting is dated into. Each year has a **Year**, a **Name**, a **Status** (**Draft**, **Open**, **Closed** or **Permanently closed**), its start and end dates, and twelve monthly fiscal periods that are created with it. One year is the current fiscal year, the one open for posting. The table shows **Status**, **Year**, **Name**, **Date range**, **Description** and **Created At**.

Controllers and accounting administrators use the page to set up new years, open and lock periods through month-end, and close the year.

tasks.title: Add a fiscal year
steps: Open [Fiscal years](/accounting/configuration-files/fiscal-years).
Select **New fiscal year**.
Fill in **Year** and **Name**, and optionally a **Description**.
Leave **Calendar year** on for January 1 to December 31, or turn it off and set the **Start date** and **End date**. The calendar cannot be changed after the year is created.
Turn on **Allow adjusting entries** if adjustments may be posted after year-end close.
Select **Save**. The year is created as a draft with its monthly periods.

tasks.title: Make a fiscal year current
steps: Open [Fiscal years](/accounting/configuration-files/fiscal-years).
Right-click the year and choose **Set as current**, or open the year and use **Set as current** at the top of its panel.
Confirm with **Set as current**. Any other current year stops being current.

tasks.title: Open, lock or close a fiscal period
steps: Open [Fiscal years](/accounting/configuration-files/fiscal-years) and select the year.
Under **Fiscal periods**, open the actions menu on the period's row.
Choose **Open period**, **Lock period**, **Unlock period**, **Close period** or **Reopen period**, and confirm. Reopening asks for a **Reason**, which is recorded on the period.

tasks.title: Close or reopen a fiscal year
steps: Open [Fiscal years](/accounting/configuration-files/fiscal-years).

Right-click an open year and choose **Close year**. The dialog previews the closing entry (revenue, cost of revenue, operating expense and net income) and the opening balances carried into the next year, and lists anything blocking the close.
Select **Post and close year**.
To undo a close, right-click a closed year, choose **Reopen year**, enter the **Reason**, and select **Reverse and reopen**.

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to fiscal years. Setting a year current, closing and reopening each need their own fiscal year permission, and period actions need fiscal period permissions; actions you are not allowed to take do not appear. - An open period accepts all postings. A locked period blocks invoices, receivables, payables and other subledger postings but still accepts manual journal entries. A closed period blocks every posting until it is reopened. Periods open and close in order, so an earlier period may need attention first. - Closing a year before its end date shows **Early close**: nothing more can be posted for the rest of that year. - Reopening a year posts reversing entries against its closing and opening entries; the year must be closed again afterwards. A permanently closed year or period cannot change.

pages.name: Journal reversals
pages.description: Request and manage journal entry reversals.
pages.summary:
Journal reversals are requests to back out a journal entry that has already been posted to the general ledger. The page lists every reversal request with its **Status**, **Original journal entry**, **Reason code**, **Reason** and **Created At**.

A reversal request starts as **Requested**, can go to pending approval, is **Approved** or **Rejected**, and an approved reversal is posted to the ledger (**Posted**). Accountants raise the requests; approvers review and post them.

The page also leads to the journal entry detail page, which shows an entry's number, type, status, accounting date, **Reference type**, **Reference**, whether it **Is reversal**, the entry it is a **Reversal Of** or is **Reversed By**, and its **Line items** with totals.

tasks.title: Request a journal entry reversal
steps: Open [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals).
Select **New journal reversal**.
Enter the **Original journal entry ID** of the posted entry and the **Requested accounting date** the reversal should post on.
Enter a **Reason code** (for example ERROR or DUPLICATE) and a detailed **Reason**.
Select **Create reversal**.

tasks.title: Approve or reject a reversal
steps: Open [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals).
Select a reversal whose **Status** is pending approval.
Under **Actions**, select **Approve**, or select **Reject**, type the reason and select **Confirm reject**.

tasks.title: Post an approved reversal
steps: Open [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals).
Select an **Approved** reversal.
Under **Actions**, select **Post**. The panel then shows the **Reversal entry** that was posted.

tasks.title: Cancel a reversal request
steps: Open [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals).
Select a reversal that is requested, pending approval or approved.
Select **Cancel reversal**, type the reason, then select **Confirm cancel**.

tasks.title: Look at the original journal entry
steps: Open [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals).
Select the ID in the **Original journal entry** column. The journal entry page opens with its details and **Line items**.
On the journal entry page, select the **Reference** link to open the record that produced the entry, or select **Back** to return.

pages.notes:
Opening the page needs read access to journal reversals. Opening a journal entry page needs read access to journal entries.

A reversal does not delete the original entry: posting it adds a reversing entry, and the original entry then shows who it was **Reversed By**.

pages.name: Manual journals
pages.description: Create and manage manual journal entries.
pages.summary:
Manual journals are general ledger entries that people key in by hand, such as accruals, reclassifications and other adjustments that do not come from billing or payments. The page lists every manual journal with its **Request #**, **Status**, **Description**, **Accounting date**, **Total debit** and **Total credit**.

A manual journal moves through a review flow before it reaches the ledger: it starts as a **Draft**, is submitted for approval (pending approval), is **Approved** or **Rejected**, and an approved journal is then posted to the general ledger (**Posted**). Accountants prepare the drafts; approvers review and post them.

tasks.title: Create a manual journal draft
steps: Open [Manual journals](/accounting/manual-journals).
Select the New button above the table. The **New manual journal** panel opens.
Under **Journal details**, fill in **Description** and **Accounting date**. Add a **Reason** for approvers if needed, check **Currency**, and optionally pick a **Fiscal year** and **Fiscal period**.
Under **Line items**, pick a **GL account** for each line and enter a **Debit** or **Credit** amount, with an optional **Memo**. Select **Add line** for more lines.
Make sure total debits equal total credits; the summary under the lines shows **Balanced** when they do.
Select **Create draft**.

tasks.title: Edit and submit a draft for approval
steps: Open [Manual journals](/accounting/manual-journals).
Select the journal's row to open it.
Change any fields or lines, then select **Save draft**.
Select **Submit** to send the journal for approval. Its status becomes pending approval.

tasks.title: Approve or reject a journal
steps: Open [Manual journals](/accounting/manual-journals).
Select the row of a journal whose **Status** is pending approval.
Under **Actions**, select **Approve**, or select **Reject**, type the rejection reason and select **Confirm reject**.

tasks.title: Post an approved journal to the general ledger
steps: Open [Manual journals](/accounting/manual-journals).
Select an **Approved** journal's row.
Under **Actions**, select **Post to GL**. The journal's status becomes **Posted**.

tasks.title: Cancel a journal
steps: Open [Manual journals](/accounting/manual-journals).
Select the journal's row. Only a draft, pending approval or approved journal can be cancelled.
Select **Cancel journal**, type the reason, then select **Confirm cancel**.

pages.notes:
Opening the page needs read access to manual journals.

The **Accounting date** must fall within an open fiscal period. Only a draft can be edited; once submitted, the journal's fields are read-only. A posted journal cannot be cancelled or edited; to undo its effect on the ledger, request a reversal on [Journal reversals](/accounting/journal-reversals).

pages.name: Bank receipts
pages.description: Match imported bank receipts to customer payments and resolve exceptions.
pages.summary:
Bank receipt reconciliation is where imported bank deposits are matched to the customer payments they paid for. The list on the left holds the receipts that could not be matched automatically when they were imported (exceptions), newest first. Selecting one shows its **Receipt details**, the **Exception reason**, and **Match suggestions**: posted customer payments that could be the same money, each with a **Score** and a **Reason**.

Figures at the top count receipts that are **Imported**, **Matched** and in **Exceptions**, plus **Active work items**. Accounting staff use the page to clear unmatched deposits.

tasks.title: Match a bank receipt to a customer payment
steps: Open [Bank receipt reconciliation](/accounting/reconciliation/bank-receipts).
Select the receipt in the list.
Check the **Exception reason** and look through **Match suggestions**.
Select **Match** on the right payment. The receipt shows **Matched payment** with the payment ID and time.

tasks.title: Handle a receipt with no suitable payment
steps: Open [Bank receipt reconciliation](/accounting/reconciliation/bank-receipts) and select the receipt. If it shows **No match suggestions available.**, the payment may not be posted yet.
Post the payment on [Customer payments](/accounting/ar/payments) for the same amount, then come back and match it.
Or work the receipt from the [Work queue](/accounting/reconciliation/work-queue), where it can be resolved or dismissed with a note.

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to bank receipts; matching needs update access to bank receipts. - Only a posted customer payment for exactly the receipt's amount can be matched, and a receipt that is already matched cannot be matched again. - Matching a receipt also resolves its open item in the [Work queue](/accounting/reconciliation/work-queue). - Receipts arrive here from [Import batches](/accounting/reconciliation/import-batches).

pages.name: Import batches
pages.description: View and create bank receipt import batches.
pages.summary:
Import batches is where bank receipts enter reconciliation. Each batch is a set of deposits from one bank, entered line by line, and the list shows its **Reference**, **Source**, **Status**, **Imported**, **Matched**, **Exceptions**, **Total amount** and **Created** time. Figures at the top give **Total batches**, **Processing** and **Completed**.

As a batch is saved, each receipt is checked against posted customer payments. A receipt with a reference number that points to exactly one payment of the same amount is matched on the spot; the rest become exceptions to work on [Bank receipts](/accounting/reconciliation/bank-receipts) and the [Work queue](/accounting/reconciliation/work-queue). Accounting staff use this page to bring deposits in and see how many matched.

tasks.title: Import a batch of bank receipts
steps: Open [Import batches](/accounting/reconciliation/import-batches).
Select **Import batch** (or **Import a batch** when there are none yet).
Fill in **Source** (the bank) and **Reference**, such as a statement number.

Under **Receipt lines**, enter each deposit's **Date**, **Amount ($)**, **Reference #** (the check number or transaction ID) and an optional **Memo**. Select **Add line** for more deposits, or the bin icon to remove one.
Select **Import batch**, or press Ctrl+Enter.

tasks.title: See what a batch matched
steps: Open [Import batches](/accounting/reconciliation/import-batches).
Select the batch row. Its page shows **Imported**, **Matched** and **Exceptions** totals, the **Batch info**, and every receipt under **Receipts** with its status.
Select **Back to batches** to return to the list.

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to bank receipts; importing needs create access to bank receipts. - A batch needs at least one receipt line. - Receipts with no **Reference #** cannot be matched automatically and always become exceptions. - Automatic matching only runs when reconciliation is turned on in the organization's accounting control settings. When it is off, receipts stay imported and unmatched.

pages.name: Summary
pages.description: Overview of bank receipt reconciliation status.
pages.summary:
The reconciliation summary is a read-only overview of bank receipt reconciliation. It shows how many receipts are **Imported**, **Matched** and in **Exceptions** with their amounts, and the **Match rate** (matched receipts as a share of imported ones). **Exception aging** counts exceptions as **Current**, **1-3 Days**, **4-7 Days** and **7+ Days** old, and **Work items** counts the **Active**, **Assigned** and **In review** items in the work queue.

Accounting managers use it to see at a glance whether deposits are being matched and how long exceptions have been waiting.

tasks.title: Check reconciliation status
steps: Open [Reconciliation summary](/accounting/reconciliation/summary).
Read the totals at the top and the **Exception aging** table.
Select **Bank receipts** to match receipts, or **Work queue** to work the open items.

tasks.title: Start reconciling for the first time
steps: Open [Reconciliation summary](/accounting/reconciliation/summary). Until anything has been imported it shows **Nothing to reconcile yet**.
Select **Import a batch** to go to [Import batches](/accounting/reconciliation/import-batches).

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to bank receipts. Nothing can be changed here.

pages.name: Work queue
pages.description: Review and resolve bank receipt exceptions requiring attention.
pages.summary:
The bank receipt work queue holds one work item for every bank receipt that became an exception on import, so someone owns it until it is settled. Each item moves from **Open** to **Assigned** to **In review**, and ends **Resolved** or **Dismissed**. Figures at the top count **Open**, **Assigned**, **In review** and **Exceptions**.

The list shows the items still being worked (open, assigned or in review), newest first, each marked assigned or unassigned. Selecting an item shows the **Bank receipt info** (date, amount, reference, memo, status and exception reason), the **Assignment**, and the **Actions** available at its current step. Accounting staff use it to divide up and close out reconciliation exceptions.

tasks.title: Take and review a work item
steps: Open [Bank receipt work queue](/accounting/reconciliation/work-queue) and select an **Open** item.
Select **Assign to me**.
When you are ready to work it, select **Start review**.

tasks.title: Resolve or dismiss a work item
steps: Open [Bank receipt work queue](/accounting/reconciliation/work-queue) and select an item that is **In review**.

To resolve it, select **Resolve**, pick a resolution type (**Matched to payment**, **Marked false positive**, **Requires external follow-up** or **Superseded**), add notes, and select **Confirm resolution**.
To dismiss it instead, select **Dismiss**, give the reason, and select **Confirm dismiss**.

pages.notes: - Opening the page needs read access to bank receipt work items; assigning, reviewing, resolving and dismissing need update access. - Resolving or dismissing a work item does not match the bank receipt. To match it to a customer payment, use [Bank receipt reconciliation](/accounting/reconciliation/bank-receipts); matching there resolves the work item automatically. - Resolved and dismissed items leave the list and have no further actions.

pages.name: Balance sheet
pages.description: Assets, liabilities, and equity as of a fiscal period.
pages.summary: The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and equity as they stood at the close of a fiscal period, with **Total assets**, **Total liabilities** and **Total equity**, plus **Current year earnings** when there are any. A check at the bottom compares assets with liabilities plus equity and reads **Balance sheet is balanced** or **Balance sheet is NOT balanced**.

tasks.title: View the balance sheet for a period
steps: Open [Balance sheet](/accounting/reports/balance-sheet).
Pick a **Fiscal year**, then a **Fiscal period**.
Read the asset, liability and equity sections and check the balance line at the bottom.

pages.notes: The report needs read access to accounting reports. If the check reads **Balance sheet is NOT balanced**, the [Trial balance](/accounting/reports/trial-balance) for the same period is a good place to start looking.

pages.name: Income Statement
pages.description: Revenue, expenses, and net income for a fiscal period.
pages.summary: The income statement shows revenue, cost of revenue and operating expenses for a fiscal period, with **Gross profit** and **Net Income** totals. Controllers and owners use it to see whether the business made money in a period.

tasks.title: View the income statement for a period
steps: Open [Income Statement](/accounting/reports/income-statement).
Pick a **Fiscal year**, then a **Fiscal period**.
Read the revenue, cost of revenue and operating expense sections, then **Gross profit** and **Net Income**.

pages.notes: The report needs read access to accounting reports.

pages.name: Trial balance
pages.description: View account balances for a fiscal period.
pages.summary: The trial balance lists every general ledger account that had activity in a fiscal period, with its **Account code**, **Account name**, **Category**, **Debit**, **Credit** and **Net change**, and a **Totals** row at the bottom. Accountants use it to check that the books balance before closing a period and to spot unusual account movements.

tasks.title: Run the trial balance for a period
steps: Open [Trial balance](/accounting/reports/trial-balance).
Pick a **Fiscal year**, then a **Fiscal period**.
Read the account rows and compare the **Debit** and **Credit** totals in the **Totals** row.

pages.notes: The report needs read access to accounting reports. If nothing was posted in the chosen period, the page shows **Nothing posted**.

pages.name: Accounting controls
pages.description: Configure and manage your accounting control settings
pages.summary:
Accounting control holds the organization's accounting rules and default general ledger accounts. The page is one settings form in five cards: **Recognition policy** (accounting basis and when revenue and expenses are recognized), **Journal policy** (automatic journal posting, manual journals, reversals and default accounts), **Driver settlement posting** (accounts used when driver settlements post), **Period and reconciliation** (period close and posting into locked or closed periods) and **Currency settings**.

Controllers and accounting administrators use it when setting up the ledger and when changing how postings flow.

tasks.title: Set the accounting basis and recognition policies
steps: Open [Accounting controls](/admin/accounting-control).
In **Recognition policy**, choose the **Accounting basis** (**Accrual** or **Cash**).
Set the **Revenue recognition policy** and **Expense recognition policy**; they must be compatible with the basis.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Post journals automatically from business events
steps: Open [Accounting controls](/admin/accounting-control).
In **Journal policy**, set **Journal posting mode** to **Automatic**.
Under **Auto-post source events**, tick the events that may create journal entries, such as **Invoice posted** or **Customer payment posted**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set the default GL accounts
steps: Open [Accounting controls](/admin/accounting-control).
In **Journal policy**, pick accounts such as **Default Revenue account**, **Default cash account**, **Default AR account**, **Default AP account** and **Default write-off account**.
In **Driver settlement posting**, pick the **Driver pay expense account**, **Settlements payable account** and the other settlement accounts.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Control manual journals and period close
steps: Open [Accounting controls](/admin/accounting-control).
In **Journal policy**, set the **Manual journal entry policy** (**Allow all**, **Adjustment only** or **Disallow**), **Require manual JE approval** and the **Journal reversal policy**.
In **Period and reconciliation**, set the **Period close mode**, **Require period close approval**, **Locked period posting policy** and **Closed period posting policy**.
Set the **Reconciliation mode**; when it is not **Disabled**, also set the **Reconciliation tolerance amount**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Turn on multi-currency
steps: Open [Accounting controls](/admin/accounting-control).
In **Currency settings**, set **Currency mode** to **Multi currency** and choose the **Functional currency**.
If the OANDA panel says OANDA is required, select **Configure** to connect it.
Once OANDA is connected, set the **Exchange rate date policy**, **Exchange rate override policy**, **Realized FX gain account** and **Realized FX loss account**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to accounting control; saving needs update access. The currency policy fields only appear once OANDA is connected, and **Configure** needs read access to integrations. Switching back to **Single currency** clears the FX accounts.

pages.name: AI control
pages.description: Providers say where AI work goes, agents say what it may do, extensions add what they can reach, quality says how well they do it, and activity shows what it did.
pages.summary:
AI control is the one place for everything AI in the organization. A rail down the left side holds eight sections: **Overview**, **Agents**, **Providers**, **Extensions**, **Memory**, **Safety**, **Quality** and **Activity**. Providers say where AI work goes (the model endpoints Trenova calls and which AI tasks each one handles), agents say what AI may do (their instructions, tools, autonomy and trigger), extensions add abilities that work only for agents, such as searching the web, using the organization's own account with the vendor, memory holds the standing instructions and facts agents read, safety shows what each tool and agent can do without a person, quality says how well each agent does its work, and activity shows what agents did: their runs, the changes they proposed, multi-step plans, replays and exceptions.

**Overview** shows whether AI can work at all (a banner warns when no provider is connected or a task has no provider), a strip of figures for providers and agents that are on, proposals awaiting a decision, runs in the last 24 hours, model calls, spend, response time and tokens, the **Organization-wide** switches, and every agent at a glance. Administrators use this page to set up providers and agents; reviewers use **Activity** to approve or reject what agents propose.

tasks.title: Connect an AI provider
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Providers** in the rail.
Select **New provider**.
Optionally pick a **Deployment** under **Start from a preset** to fill in the endpoint and output settings for a known deployment.
Under **Endpoint**, fill in **Name**, **Protocol**, **Model**, **Base URL** and the API key if the provider needs one.

Under **Routing**, choose the AI tasks in **Handles these tasks** and set **Priority** (lower runs first; providers behind it act as fallbacks). Turn on **Trusted for financial work** only for a provider that may take tasks that read sensitive records.
Leave **Enabled** on and select **Save**.
Back on the provider's card, select **Test** to check the endpoint answers and honours JSON schemas.

tasks.title: Set up an embedding provider
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Providers** in the rail.

Select **New provider** and, under **Start from a preset**, pick one of the embedding presets: Voyage AI, Gemini, OpenAI, or Ollama for a model on your own hardware. The preset fills in the endpoint, the model, and the embedding task.

Under **Routing**, **Handles these tasks** shows **Embedding** ticked. An embedding model serves nothing else, so leave the other tasks for a separate provider. Anthropic has no embedding endpoint, so the task cannot be ticked on an Anthropic provider.
Under **Embedding**, check **Dimensions** matches the vector size the model returns and set **Input style** to how the endpoint tells a stored document from a search query.
Enter the API key, optionally the **Input price, USD per million tokens**, and select **Save**.
Select **Test** on the provider's card. The test asks for one embedding and fails when the model returns a different size than **Dimensions**.

tasks.title: Let agents search the web
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Extensions** in the rail.
On the web search card, select **Set up**.
Paste the organization's Exa API key and select **Save changes**. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again; leave the field blank later to keep it.
Select **Test connection** to check the key works.

Turn the extension on, and under **Available to** choose **Every agent** to give all agents, the assistant included, the web search tools, or **Agents you choose** to add them only to the agents you pick under **Choose tools** on the **Agents** section. Then select **Save changes**.
Optionally change the search depth, the results per search, the daily request limit and the sites agents never receive results from.

tasks.title: Create an agent
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Agents** in the rail.
Select **New agent**.
Optionally choose a starter in **Start from** to fill in instructions, tools and a trigger you can change freely.
Fill in **Name**, **Description** and **System instructions**. Add hard lines the agent must not cross under **Never**, pressing Enter after each.
Under **Tools**, select **Choose tools**, pick what the agent may look up and change, then select **Done**.
Under **Autonomy**, set the **Ceiling**: **Propose only**, **Act with approval** or **Act automatically**. Turn on **Shadow mode** or **Simulation** to try the agent without it changing anything.
Under **When it runs**, pick **Chat**, **Scheduled**, **Event** or **Continuous** and fill in the schedule or events it asks for.
Optionally set a **Monthly budget**, **Runs per day** and a **Preferred provider**, leave **Enabled** on, and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Let an agent hand work to another agent
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Agents** in the rail.
Select the pencil button on the agent that should be able to ask for help.
In **Can ask**, select **Add an agent** and pick each agent it may hand a task to, such as the Report Builder for an agent that builds dashboards. An agent can ask up to eight others.
Select **Save**. From its next reply the agent can hand those agents a task, and shows their work step by step in the conversation.

tasks.title: Choose who can use an agent
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Agents** in the rail. Each agent's row shows who can use it: **Everyone**, or how many roles it is limited to.
Select the pencil button on the agent, or select **New agent** to set it while creating one.
In **Who can use it**, choose **Everyone who can use the assistant** or **Specific roles**.

For **Specific roles**, pick the roles in **Roles**. **Suggested roles** lists every role with what it could make of the agent with the tools chosen on the form, saved or not: "Can use all of its tools", the resources it is missing, or "Can't use the assistant". Select **Add** beside one to choose it.

Select **Save**. The agent and who can use it are saved together, so a new agent limited to roles is limited from the moment it exists. From then on only people holding one of the chosen roles, or a role that inherits one, see the agent in the Desk and the assistant, and only they see and decide what it proposes.

tasks.title: Turn an agent on or off, run it now, or remove it
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Agents** in the rail.
Use the switch at the end of an agent's row to enable or disable it.
To start a run without waiting for its trigger, select the play button on the row. It is shown for agents that are not chat agents, and only works while the agent is enabled.
To change an agent, select the pencil button and edit it, then **Save**.
To delete one, select the trash button and confirm with **Remove agent**. System agents cannot be removed.

tasks.title: Approve or reject what an agent proposed
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control), select **Activity** in the rail and then **Proposals**.
Right-click a pending proposal and choose **Approve**, **Approve with changes** or **Reject**.
Give a **Reason** (required when rejecting) and confirm with **Approve and run** or **Reject**.
For a multi-step plan, select **Plans** instead and use **Approve all** or **Reject all**.

tasks.title: Pause every agent at once
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) on **Overview**.
In **Organization-wide**, turn on **Pause all agents**. Agents keep running and recording what they would do, but nothing they propose is offered for a decision or executed.
In the same panel, turn **Earned autonomy** on or off and choose the **Promotion threshold** (clean approvals in a row before a tool moves up a tier on that agent).

tasks.title: See what agents can do without a person
keywords: what can the AI do on its own
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Safety** in the rail. Safety has two tables under it in the rail, **Tool rules** and **By agent**.

Read the figures at the top: **Tools that run without a person** (tools that change records and, on at least one agent, can run without anyone approving), **Tools that send outside the organization**, and **Open agents with sensitive tools** (agents everyone can use that hold tools reaching restricted data or leaving the organization).

Select **Tool rules**. Every tool is listed with **Who sees it**, its **Max tier**, what it **Needs** of the person using it, whether it **Reads outside content**, and whether it **Runs without a person** on at least one agent. Use the search box to find a tool by name, or select **Filter** to narrow by **Who sees it**, **Max tier**, **Needs**, **Kind**, **Reads outside content** or **Runs without a person**, and **Sort** to order by any of them. **Display** shows hidden columns such as **Name** and **Kind** and changes the row density.
Select a row to open its rule: the **Rationale**, **How far it may go** and any **Record condition**. A tool marked **Depends on the call** goes further for some calls than others; its rule says why.

Select **By agent**, then **Add an agent** and choose one; add up to ten to compare them in one table. Nothing is read until you add an agent. Each agent shows **Who can use it** and its **Ceiling**, and the table lists every tool the agents hold with what happens **Before outside text** and **After outside text**: **Runs on its own**, **Depends on the call**, **Needs approval**, **Proposes only** or **Simulated**. Select **Filter** to narrow to one **Agent**, an answer, or a **Held by** reason. Select the cross beside an agent's name to take it out of the comparison.

The **Held by** chips say which limit stops a tool going further, such as the agent's ceiling, where the work goes, or that the run has read outside text. A tool whose tier was earned shows **Tier earned**, and one still earning shows how many clean approvals it needs for the next tier. Select a row to read both answers beside the tool's rule.

tasks.title: Check how well an agent is doing
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Quality** in the rail. Quality lists its tables under it in the rail: **Agents**, **Suite runs**, **Worst-rated answers**, **Golden set** and **Settings**.

Read the figures at the top: **Satisfaction** (the share of rated answers that were thumbs up), **Ratings**, **Quality score** (how the agents score against their golden sets), **Regressions**, and **Eval spend this month** against the monthly budget.

In **Agents**, each agent is listed with its satisfaction against the window before, a line of its recent suite scores, and how its **Last run** went: **Completed**, **Skipped** (nothing about the agent or its cases changed), **Budget stopped** or **Failed**. An agent whose score fell shows **Regressed**. Select **Filter** to narrow by **Last run** or **Regressed**, and **Sort** to order by **Satisfaction** or **Quality score**.

Select an agent's row to open it. **Quality over time** shows its scores. To score it now instead of waiting for the nightly sweep, select **Run suite now**. Select **Its suite runs** or **Its worst-rated answers** to open those tables narrowed to the agent; **Show every agent** widens them again.

In **Suite runs**, each run shows its **Status**, **Quality score**, **Cases** and **What changed** about the agent since the run before, such as its instructions, tools or model. Select a run to read it, then **See the cases** to list what each case scored; select a case to read the reply and the judge's note. **Back to suite runs** returns to the runs.

**Worst-rated answers** lists the answers people rated down in the last 30 days, most disliked first. Select one to read the question, the answer and **Why**. Select **Open the conversation** to read one you were part of.

Keep the cases the agents are scored against in **Golden set**: **Activate** a candidate captured from a decided proposal, **Add case** to write one by hand, or **Quarantine** a case that is no longer fair.

In **Settings**, turn **Run the nightly sweep** on or off, choose the **Hour it starts**, set **Most cases per agent**, the **Nightly budget (USD)** and **Monthly budget (USD)**, the **Regression threshold (points)**, and whether to **Have a judge read a sample**. Then select **Save settings**.

tasks.title: Record something every agent should know
steps: Open [AI control](/admin/agent-control) and select **Memory** in the rail.
Select **New memory**.
Choose the **Kind** (**Instruction**, **Fact** or **Correction**), write the **Memory**, and optionally set **Until**.
To make it about one record, pick a **Kind of record** and the record; leave it empty for something every agent should know. Then select **Save**.
To stop agents reading an entry, right-click it and choose **Retire**; **Restore** brings it back.

pages.notes:
An embedding provider turns memories, documents and mail into vectors so agents can find them by what they mean rather than by the exact words; until one is set up, agents search by keywords only. Social security, card and bank account numbers are masked before a document is sent. Changing the embedding model or its size re-indexes everything that was embedded. Providers with the same model and size back each other up; a provider with a different model is never used in their place.

An agent that has read content written outside the organization (an inbound email, an extracted document, an EDI file, a bank receipt, a file attached in chat, or a memory such a run wrote) never sends anything to a customer, driver or outside address, or moves money, on its own: that change waits for a person's approval whatever tier the tool has, and the proposal is marked as having read outside content. A suggested memory drawn from ratings of one agent is kept for that agent alone once approved.

A memory holds up to 4,000 characters. Each prompt carries only as much memory as the agent's **Memory in the prompt** setting allows (6,000 tokens unless changed), starting with what is recorded about the record the conversation is about. When the organization keeps close to 5,000 active memories, the Memory section warns that fewer of them reach each prompt; retire what no longer holds.

Opening the page needs read access to AI control. Each section in the rail appears only for people who may read it (agents, AI providers, agent runs, agent proposals, agent exceptions, agent memory); a section someone cannot open is left out. **Safety** appears for people who may read agents, and **Quality** for people who may read the evaluation suite. **Worst-rated answers** and satisfaction need read access to agent feedback, **Run suite now** needs create access to the evaluation suite, and changing **Settings** needs update access to both the evaluation suite and AI control, because the budgets are spend. The organization-wide switches need update access to AI control, deciding proposals needs update access to agent proposals, and **Test** on a provider needs manage access to AI providers. Viewing **Extensions** needs read access to agent extensions, and turning one on, changing its settings or testing it needs update access. An agent searches the web for someone only when their role has the web research permission.

Search queries and the addresses of pages agents read are sent to the extension's vendor. Queries that contain Trenova record IDs, email addresses or phone numbers are refused before they leave Trenova. Once an agent has read web content, every change it asks for in the rest of that reply waits for a person's approval, whatever the agent's autonomy. Each extension counts its requests against the daily limit, which resets at midnight UTC, and the card shows today's requests and this month's cost.

An agent asks only the agents listed under **Can ask**; with none listed it works with its own tools alone. Only agents people talk to can ask or be asked, and an agent that was asked cannot hand the task on. The agent asked works as the person in the conversation, with its own tools and approvals, so it can never do more than that person could.

Who can use an agent is set under **Who can use it**. An agent open to everyone that holds tools reaching restricted or confidential data, or whose work leaves the organization, shows a warning there as soon as the form says so, before it is saved; each person can still only do what their own permissions allow. An agent limited to specific roles with none chosen can be used by nobody. Roles chosen while an agent is open to everyone are kept for when it is limited again. A system agent is always open to everyone and cannot be limited to roles. Someone who loses access to an agent keeps their conversations with it, read-only. Setting who can use an agent needs update access to both agents and roles; someone without update access to roles can still save the rest of an agent as long as they leave who can use it as it was. The same grants can be managed from a role's page on [Roles](/admin/roles), under **Agents**.

Every night, at the hour chosen in **Settings** (in the organization's timezone unless another is chosen there), each agent with active cases is replayed against a sample of its golden set with every write simulated. The sample always includes the cases the agent failed most recently and is otherwise spread across where the cases came from; it is the same sample for the same run. An agent is skipped when nothing about it (its instructions, tools, model or provider) or its cases changed since its last run, unless that run is older than the rerun limit. A run stops when the nightly or monthly budget is spent, and says so. When an agent's score falls below the median of its recent runs by more than the threshold, the run is marked **Regressed**, a Watchtower item is raised (critical when a case failed a hard check), and the people who can update AI control are told once, with what changed.

Removing a provider stops any task routed only to it until another provider is assigned. Removing an agent keeps its existing conversations but they cannot be continued, and its schedule stops. On **Runs**, right-clicking a finished run offers **Replay against the current agent**; the comparison appears under **Evaluations**, where **Open comparison** shows what the replay would have done beside the original.

pages.name: API keys
pages.description: Provision bearer credentials for third-party systems with direct, tenant-scoped permissions.
pages.summary:
API keys are bearer credentials that let a third-party system (a warehouse connector, a customer portal, a reporting tool) call Trenova's API directly. Each key has its own permissions, granted resource by resource, and is scoped to your organization. Figures at the top show **Total keys**, **Active keys**, **Revoked keys** and **Requests (30d)**.

The table lists each key's **Name**, **Description**, **Status**, **Permissions**, **Last used**, **Expires** and **Updated**. Administrators and developers create keys here, hand the token to the system that needs it, and revoke keys that are no longer used.

tasks.title: Create an API key
steps: Open [API keys](/admin/api-keys).
Select **New API key**.
Under **Key details**, enter a **Display name** and optional **Description**, and set an **Expiration** if the key should stop working on a date (leave it blank to keep it active until revoked).

Under **Permissions**, apply a preset (**All read**, **All write** or **Full access**) or use **Search resources...** and grant each resource **View only** or **Full access**. **Clear all** removes every grant.
Select **Create API key**.
Select **Copy API key** and store the token securely, then **Close**. The token is shown only once.

tasks.title: Change a key's details or permissions
steps: Open [API keys](/admin/api-keys) and select the key's row.
Change the **Display name**, **Description**, **Expiration** or permissions.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Rotate a key's secret
steps: Open [API keys](/admin/api-keys) and select the key's row.
Select the rotate button at the top of the panel (**Rotate secret**). It runs straight away.
Select **Copy API key**, update the system that uses the key, and **Close**. The new token is shown only once.

tasks.title: Revoke a key
steps: Open [API keys](/admin/api-keys).
Right-click the key and choose **Revoke** (or open it and select the revoke button, **Revoke key**).
Confirm with **Revoke key**. Any system using the key starts failing authentication immediately. A revoked key stays in the list, read-only.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to API keys. Creating a key needs create access to API keys, and editing, rotating or revoking one needs update access. Requests made with a key are limited to the permissions granted to that key.

pages.name: Audit entries
pages.description: Monitor and review system activity across your organization
pages.summary:
Audit entries is the record of activity across your organization: who created, changed or deleted what, and when. Each entry shows the **Resource ID**, a **Description**, the kind of **Resource** (shipment, customer, user and so on), the **Action**, the **Timestamp** and the **User** who did it.

Opening an entry shows its **Entry details** (event ID, operation, IP address, category, correlation ID, user agent and whether it was critical), the **Changes** made field by field with the previous and current value, and the **Metadata**, **Previous state**, **Current state** and **Full event data** behind it. Administrators and auditors use it to answer "who changed this record, and what did it say before?". The page is read-only.

tasks.title: Find who changed a record
steps: Open [Audit entries](/admin/audit-logs).
Select **Filter** and filter **Resource ID** (contains) with the record's ID, or filter **Resource** to the kind of record.
Narrow further by **Action** or **Timestamp** if needed, and sort by **Timestamp**.

tasks.title: Read the details of an entry
steps: Open [Audit entries](/admin/audit-logs).
Select an entry's row to open its details.
Read **Changes** for each field's **Previous value** and **Current value**. A value marked **Sensitive** was left out of the log.
For a list or object value, select **View JSON** to expand it, or scroll to **Full event data** for the complete payload.

tasks.title: Review what a person did
steps: Open [Audit entries](/admin/audit-logs).
Use the search box or **Filter** on **Description**, **Resource** and **Action**, and sort by **Timestamp** to see activity in order. The **User** column shows who did each action.

tasks.title: Export audit entries
steps: Open [Audit entries](/admin/audit-logs) and filter to the entries you need.
Select **Export to CSV** in the toolbar.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to audit logs; exporting needs export access. Audit logs are processed in batches, so a change you just made may take a few moments to appear; refresh the page after a brief wait if it is missing.

pages.name: Billing controls
pages.description: Configure and manage your billing control settings
pages.summary:
Billing control holds the organization-wide rules for billing. The page is one settings form in five cards: **Invoice defaults** (what invoices show and the fallback payment term, terms and footer), **Automation policy** (how shipments move into billing and whether invoices are drafted and posted automatically), **Exception policy** (how missing billing requirements and rate variances are handled), **Rating policy** (what happens to a shipment no rate agreement covers) and **Late charges** (whether the nightly late-charge run raises debit memos).

Billing managers and finance leads use it. A warning at the top of the page notes that these settings affect revenue processing and invoicing, and should change only after review.

tasks.title: Set invoice defaults
steps: Open [Billing controls](/admin/billing-controls).
In **Invoice defaults**, turn **Show due date on invoice** and **Show balance due on invoice** on or off.
Choose the **Default payment term** and fill in **Default invoice terms** and **Default invoice footer**. These apply when a customer's billing profile does not set its own.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Automate the billing queue and invoice drafts
steps: Open [Billing controls](/admin/billing-controls).

In **Automation policy**, set **Ready-to-bill assignment mode** and **Billing queue transfer mode**. With **Automatic when ready**, also set the **Billing queue transfer schedule** and **Billing queue transfer batch size**.
Set **Invoice draft creation mode**. With **Automatic when transferred**, also set the **Auto invoice batch size** and whether to **Notify on auto invoice creation**.
Set **Invoice posting mode** to **Manual review required** or **Automatic when no blocking exceptions**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Decide how billing exceptions are handled
steps: Open [Billing controls](/admin/billing-controls).
In **Exception policy**, set **Shipment billing requirement enforcement** and **Rate validation enforcement** to **Ignore**, **Warn**, **Require review** or **Block**.
If either uses **Require review**, choose the **Billing exception disposition**: **Route to billing review** or **Return to operations**.
Set the **Rate variance tolerance percent** and the **Rate variance auto resolution mode**, and turn on **Notify on billing exceptions** if wanted.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Handle shipments with no rate agreement
steps: Open [Billing controls](/admin/billing-controls).
In **Rating policy**, choose the **Unrated shipment disposition**: **Fall back to formula template**, **Zero the rate and flag for review** or **Block the save**.
For the fallback, optionally pick a **Fallback formula template**.
Turn on **Require rate override reason** and **Enforce margin floor** as needed.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Turn on automatic late charges
steps: Open [Billing controls](/admin/billing-controls).
In **Late charges**, set **Assessment mode** to **Disabled**, **Preview only** or **Automatic**.
Set the **Minimum late charge**; customers whose charges for a run add up to less are skipped.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to billing control; saving needs update access. Late charge rates and grace periods are set on each customer's billing profile, not here. In **Preview only** the nightly run writes nothing, and memos are raised by hand on [Late charges](/accounting/ar/late-charges).

pages.name: Carrier settlement control
pages.description: Configure carrier pay periods, cost accrual triggers, batch automation, invoice-match tolerance, and AP posting accounts
pages.summary:
Carrier settlement control holds the organization's rules for paying carriers on brokered freight. The page is one settings form in four cards: **Pay period** (how often carriers are settled and when carrier cost accrues), **Workflow automation** (automatic batches and posting), **Invoice matching** (how carrier invoices are compared to the buy rate) and **Posting accounts** (the GL accounts settlements post to).

Carrier payables and brokerage finance staff use it.

tasks.title: Set the carrier pay period
steps: Open [Carrier settlement control](/admin/carrier-settlement-control).
In **Pay period**, choose the **Frequency** and **Period end day**, and enter the **Pay Delay (days)**.
Choose the **Pay trigger**, the shipment milestone at which carrier cost accrues.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Automate batches and posting
steps: Open [Carrier settlement control](/admin/carrier-settlement-control).

In **Workflow automation**, turn on **Auto-generate batches** to create a batch when each pay period closes, and **Auto-post on approval** to post a settlement to the ledger as soon as it is approved.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Match carrier invoices automatically
steps: Open [Carrier settlement control](/admin/carrier-settlement-control).
In **Invoice matching**, enter the **Variance tolerance** in USD.
Turn on **Auto-match inbound invoices** to match inbound EDI 210 invoices to their carrier assignment.
Turn on **Auto-accept within tolerance** to resolve matched invoices within the tolerance without review. It requires auto-match.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set the posting accounts
steps: Open [Carrier settlement control](/admin/carrier-settlement-control).
In **Posting accounts**, choose the **Accounts payable account** and the **Purchased transportation account**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: The page is only available to organizations with brokerage features turned on. Opening it needs read access to carrier settlement control; saving needs update access. A blank posting account falls back to the defaults on [Accounting controls](/admin/accounting-control). Invoices outside the tolerance still land in the review workspace.

pages.name: Cost control
pages.description: Configure the cost-per-mile model that powers shipment profitability estimates
pages.summary:
Cost control sets up the cost-per-mile model behind shipment profitability estimates. The page is one settings form in four cards: **Cost basis** (fuel pricing, fleet miles per gallon, deadhead and the target margin), **Variable costs** and **Fixed costs** (one row per cost category, each with an industry benchmark rate) and **GL actuals** (deriving category rates from posted expenses).

Finance and operations managers use it to make the cost and margin figures on shipments reflect the fleet's real costs.

tasks.title: Set the cost basis
steps: Open [Cost control](/admin/cost-control).
In **Cost basis**, enter the **Fleet miles per gallon**.
Turn on **Use live fuel price** to price fuel from a diesel index instead of the benchmark, and choose the **Fuel index**.
Turn **Include Deadhead Miles** on or off, and enter a **Target margin percent**. Margins below it show as thin; it defaults to 10% when left empty.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Override a cost category's rate
steps: Open [Cost control](/admin/cost-control).
In **Variable costs** or **Fixed costs**, find the category. Its benchmark rate is shown on the right.
Turn on **Override rate** and enter the **Override rate per mile**.
To leave a category out of the total, turn off **Active**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Derive rates from the general ledger
steps: Open [Cost control](/admin/cost-control).
In **GL actuals**, turn on **Enable GL actuals** and set the **Rolling window (months)**. Optionally set **Planned monthly miles** as a floor for fixed categories.
For each category, choose its **Mapped GL accounts** and turn on **Use GL actuals**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to costing control; saving needs update access. Each category uses one rate source at a time: the benchmark, an override or GL actuals. Saving refreshes the cost estimates shown on shipments.

pages.name: Custom fields
pages.description: Define custom fields for trailers, workers, and other resources
pages.summary:
Custom field definitions add your own fields to Trenova records when the built-in fields are not enough, for example a lease number on trailers or a badge ID on workers. Custom fields can be added to trailers, tractors, workers, shipments, customers and locations. Each definition names the **Resource type** it applies to, its **Field type** (**Text**, **Number**, **Date**, **Boolean**, **Select** or **Multi-select**), an internal **Name** and the **Label** people see, and whether it is **Required** and **Active**.

The table lists each definition's **Label**, **Name**, **Resource type**, **Field type**, **Required**, **Active** and **Created At**. Administrators maintain it; the fields then appear on the forms for that kind of record.

tasks.title: Add a custom field
steps: Open [Custom field definitions](/admin/custom-fields).
Select **New custom field definition**.
Choose the **Resource type** and **Field type**.
Enter the **Name** (lowercase letters and underscores only) and the **Label** shown to users, and optionally a **Description** as help text.
Turn on **Required** if users must provide a value, and leave **Active** on so the field is visible and usable. Optionally set a **Display order** and a **Color**.
For **Select** or **Multi-select**, under **Options** select **Add option** for each choice and fill in its **Value**, **Label** and optional **Color**. At least one option is needed.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change a custom field
steps: Open [Custom field definitions](/admin/custom-fields).
Select the field's row (or right-click it and choose **Edit**).
Change the fields and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Deactivate or reactivate a custom field
steps: Open [Custom field definitions](/admin/custom-fields).
Right-click an active field and choose **Deactivate**. The field is hidden from forms and the values already entered are kept.
To bring it back, right-click it and choose **Activate**.

tasks.title: Delete a custom field
steps: Open [Custom field definitions](/admin/custom-fields).
Right-click the field and choose **Delete**, then confirm with **Delete**. This cannot be undone.
If the field already holds values on any record, it cannot be deleted; the dialog shows how many values exist and asks you to deactivate it instead.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to custom field definitions; **New custom field definition** appears only for people who can create them.

pages.name: Dash control
pages.description: Choose what drivers can see and do in the Dash driver portal
pages.summary:
Dash control decides what drivers can see and do in the Dash driver portal. The page is one settings form in five cards: **Load workflow** (accepting loads, arrive and depart, paperwork and messaging), **Pay visibility** (per-load pay before settlement), **Expenses & disputes**, **Profile self-Service** (what drivers can update on their own record) and **Reminders & alerts** (credential reminders and detention alerts).

Operations, safety and payroll managers use it. Changes reach drivers as soon as they are saved.

tasks.title: Choose what drivers can do on their loads
steps: Open [Dash control](/admin/dash-control).
In **Load workflow**, turn on **Load acceptance** so drivers accept or decline new assignments, and **Allow declines** if they may decline with a reason.
Turn **Self-Service arrive / depart**, **POD / BOL upload** and **Load messaging** on or off.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Show or hide pay before settlement
steps: Open [Dash control](/admin/dash-control).
In **Pay visibility**, turn on **Per-load pay** to show what each load pays, and **Pay estimates** to show an estimated payout on active loads.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Let drivers submit expenses and disputes
steps: Open [Dash control](/admin/dash-control).
In **Expenses & disputes**, turn on **Expense submission** and, if receipts are needed, **Require receipts**.
Turn on **Settlement disputes** to let drivers flag a statement or line for review.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Control driver profile self-service
steps: Open [Dash control](/admin/dash-control).
In **Profile self-Service**, turn on **Qualification document upload**, **Contact info edits** and **Time-off requests** as needed.
Turn on **Approve contact edits** to hold contact changes for office approval.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set up credential reminders and detention alerts
steps: Open [Dash control](/admin/dash-control).

In **Reminders & alerts**, turn on **Credential expiry reminders** and choose **How drivers are told**: one notice per obligation, a daily round-up or a weekly round-up. For the weekly round-up, pick the **Weekly round-up day**.
Turn on **Detention alerts** and enter the **Detention Threshold (minutes)**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: The page is only available to organizations with asset operations turned on. Opening it needs read access to Dash control; saving needs update access. Settlement statements are always visible to drivers, and compliance dates such as CDL and medical expiry are always set by the office. **Allow declines** needs **Load acceptance**, **Pay estimates** needs **Per-load pay**, and **Require receipts** needs **Expense submission**.

pages.name: Data entry controls
pages.description: Configure case formatting rules for data entry across the system
pages.summary:
