Data entry control sets how text is formatted automatically when people enter data, so codes, names, email addresses and cities look the same everywhere. The page has one card, **Case formatting rules**, with four settings.

Administrators use it once when setting up the organization and whenever they want to change the house style for entered text.

tasks.title: Change how entered text is capitalized
steps: Open [Data entry controls](/admin/data-entry-controls).

In **Case formatting rules**, choose a format for each field type: - **Code case** for code fields such as equipment and fleet codes. - **Name case** for name fields such as commodity and hazmat names. - **Email case** for email addresses. - **City case** for city names.
The formats are **As entered**, UPPER, lower and **Title case**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to data entry control; saving needs update access. The rules apply system-wide.

pages.name: DB sessions
pages.description: Inspect lock contention and manually terminate blocking database sessions
pages.summary:
Database sessions shows lock contention in the Trenova database: each card is one session that is waiting on another. The card title reads "PID {blocked} blocked by PID {blocking}" and shows the wait type and database, then both sides of the pair with their application, database user, state, **Tx age** (how long the transaction has been open) and **Query age**. Ages over two minutes are highlighted. Expanding **Queries** shows the **Blocked query** and the **Blocking query**.

The status bar at the top counts the blocked sessions; the list refreshes itself every 15 seconds. When nothing is waiting, the page reads "All database sessions are running clean". Technical administrators use this page when screens hang or saves time out because something is holding a lock.

tasks.title: Check for blocked database sessions
steps: Open [Database sessions](/admin/database-sessions).
Read the count in the status bar. Select the refresh button (**Refresh**) to check again straight away.
On a card, compare **Tx age** and **Query age** on both sides, and expand **Queries** to see what each session is running.

tasks.title: Terminate a blocking session
steps: Open [Database sessions](/admin/database-sessions) and find the card for the blocked pair.
Select **Terminate** on the card.

Read the confirmation, then select the confirm button (it reads "Terminate PID" followed by the blocking process number) to end the blocking session. Its in-flight transaction is cancelled and the blocked session is released.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to database sessions; terminating one needs delete access to database sessions. Terminating cancels whatever the blocking session was in the middle of, so any unsaved work in that transaction is lost. Check the **Blocking query** first.

pages.name: Dispatch controls
pages.description: Configure and manage your dispatch control settings
pages.summary:
Dispatch control holds the organization-wide rules for assigning and dispatching work. The page is one settings form in up to four cards: **Automated resource assignment** (letting the system assign drivers and equipment), **Candidate scoring weights** (how drivers are ranked), **Service failure monitoring** (which late pickups and deliveries are recorded as service failures) and **DOT compliance enforcement** (checks that run before an assignment goes ahead).

Dispatch managers and safety or compliance leads use it.

tasks.title: Turn on automated assignment
steps: Open [Dispatch controls](/admin/dispatch-controls).
In **Automated resource assignment**, turn on **Enable automated assignment**.
Choose the **Assignment optimization strategy**: **Proximity**, **Availability**, **Load balancing** or **Performance**.
Set the **Auto-execute confidence threshold** (0 to 1), **Maximum deadhead miles**, **Planning horizon (hours)** and **Coverage risk window (hours)**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Tune how drivers are ranked
steps: Open [Dispatch controls](/admin/dispatch-controls).
In **Candidate scoring weights**, enter a weight from 0 to 10 for each factor. A factor set to 0 is ignored; leave a field empty to use the strategy's preset, shown as the placeholder.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Record service failures
steps: Open [Dispatch controls](/admin/dispatch-controls).
In **Service failure monitoring**, choose which incidents to capture in **Record Service failures**, for example **Pickup**, **Delivery** or **Pickup/delivery**. **Never** turns it off.
Set the **Service failure grace period** in minutes and, optionally, a **Service failure target** percentage.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Enforce DOT compliance at dispatch
steps: Open [Dispatch controls](/admin/dispatch-controls).
In **DOT compliance enforcement**, turn on **Enable DOT compliance enforcement**.
Turn on the checks to run: **Medical certification validation**, **Driver qualification verification**, **Hazardous materials compliance** and **Drug and alcohol testing compliance**.
Set the **Compliance enforcement level** to **Warning**, **Block** or **Audit**.
Turn on any assignment rules needed: **Require worker assignment**, **Require trailer continuity**, **Enforce worker PTA restrictions** and **Enforce worker tractor fleet continuity**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to dispatch control; saving needs update access. The automated assignment, scoring weights and DOT compliance cards only appear for organizations with asset operations turned on; a brokerage-only organization sees just **Service failure monitoring**. Turning off **Enable DOT compliance enforcement** turns off the four individual checks.

pages.name: Distance controls
pages.description: Configure mileage storage behavior and distance profile assignments
pages.summary:
Distance controls decide how Trenova calculates and reuses mileage for your business unit. The page is one settings form in three cards: **Stored mileage policy** (whether lane mileage is reused before calling PC*Miler and how new mileage records are captured), **Jurisdiction mileage** (whether each move's routed distance is broken down by state or province for IFTA returns), and **Distance profile assignments** (which distance profile is used for each mileage purpose).

Administrators set this up once and revisit it when routing policy, billing mileage or fuel tax reporting needs change.

tasks.title: Reuse stored lane mileage
steps: Open [Distance controls](/admin/distance-controls).
In **Stored mileage policy**, turn on **Use stored mileage** so calculations check stored lane mileage before calling PC*Miler.

Turn on **Auto-create Stored Mileage** to buffer successful PC*Miler results for the scheduled job that saves them as stored mileage, and **Postal code fallback** to fall back to city and state lane keys when postal-code matching is unavailable.
Choose the **Stored distance units**.
Select **Save changes** in the bar that appears at the bottom.

tasks.title: Capture state-by-state miles for IFTA
steps: Open [Distance controls](/admin/distance-controls).
In **Jurisdiction mileage**, turn on **Capture jurisdiction miles**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Choose which distance profile each workflow uses
steps: Open [Distance controls](/admin/distance-controls).

In **Distance profile assignments**, pick a profile for each purpose: **Loaded move**, **Empty move**, **Pay**, **Billing**, **Fuel**, **ETA out-of-route**, **Calculator practical** and **Calculator shortest**. Every one is required.
Select **Save changes**. Use **Reset** instead to discard your edits.

pages.notes:
Opening the page needs read access to distance control. The profiles offered in the assignments come from [Distance profiles](/admin/distance-profiles), so create a profile there first if the one you need is missing.

Capturing jurisdiction miles asks PC*Miler for a state-by-state report on every move route, which PC*Miler may bill as an additional transaction per route. Routes calculated before it is turned on have no jurisdiction breakdown until they are recalculated.

pages.name: Distance overrides
pages.description: Override calculated distances between location pairs for routing and billing adjustments
pages.summary: Distance overrides replace the calculated distance between two locations with a figure you set, for routing and billing adjustments. An override names an origin and destination location, the distance, optionally a customer it applies to, and optionally intermediate stops in travel order. The table lists each override with its origin, destination, distance, customer and stops.

tasks.title: Add a distance override
steps: Open [Distance overrides](/admin/distance-overrides).
Select **New distance override**.
Choose the **Origin location** and **Destination location** and enter the **Distance**.
Optionally choose a **Customer** to limit the override to that customer.
Under **Intermediate stops**, select **Add stop** for each stop between origin and destination, in travel order.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change or delete an override
steps: Open [Distance overrides](/admin/distance-overrides).
Select a row to edit it, change the fields and select **Save**.
To delete one, right-click the row, choose **Delete** and confirm with **Delete**. This cannot be undone.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to distance overrides; **New distance override** appears only for people who can create them.

pages.name: Distance profiles
pages.description: Manage business-unit routing policy used by distance calculations
pages.summary:
Distance profiles hold the routing policy Trenova sends to PC*Miler when it calculates distance: the data version, region, routing type, distance units, how much of each stop's address is used, and route behavior such as toll roads and cross-border routes. The table lists each profile with its status, provider, routing type, units and data version, and marks the business unit's default profile.

Administrators create profiles here, then assign them to mileage purposes (loaded moves, pay, billing, fuel and so on) on [Distance controls](/admin/distance-controls).

tasks.title: Create a distance profile
steps: Open [Distance profiles](/admin/distance-profiles).
Select **New distance profile**.
Under **Profile details**, fill in **Name**, **Status** and **Description**, and turn on **Default profile** if this should be the business unit's default.
Under **Provider policy**, set **Provider**, **Data version**, **Region**, **Routing type**, **Distance units** and **Location granularity**, and optionally a PC*Miler vehicle profile name.
Under **Route behavior**, choose **Highway only**, **Allow toll roads**, **Borders open** and **Include toll data** as needed.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a distance profile
steps: Open [Distance profiles](/admin/distance-profiles).
Select the profile's row (or right-click it and choose **Edit**).
Change the fields you need and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Make a profile the default
steps: Open [Distance profiles](/admin/distance-profiles).
Right-click an active profile and choose **Set default**.

tasks.title: Delete a distance profile
steps: Open [Distance profiles](/admin/distance-profiles).
Right-click the profile and choose **Delete**, then confirm with **Delete**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to distance profiles; **New distance profile** appears only for people who can create them. Inactive profiles cannot be set as the default, and the default profile cannot be deleted.

pages.name: Document intelligence
pages.description: Configure OCR, classification, extraction, and shipment draft behavior
pages.summary:
Document intelligence decides what Trenova does with uploaded documents: whether it reads them with OCR, classifies them into document kinds and types, extracts structured data (optionally with an AI provider), turns documents such as rate confirmations into reviewable shipment drafts, and indexes their text for search. The page is one settings form in four cards: **Platform availability**, **Classification and extraction**, **Shipment draft extraction** and **Search and retrieval**.

Administrators use it to switch document processing on and choose how much of it is automatic.

tasks.title: Turn document intelligence on
steps: Open [Document intelligence](/admin/document-intelligence).
In **Platform availability**, turn on **Enable document intelligence**. This is the master switch; every other option on the page stays unavailable while it is off.
Turn on **Enable OCR** to read scanned documents when native text extraction is not enough.
Select **Save changes** in the bar that appears at the bottom.

tasks.title: Choose how documents are classified and extracted
steps: Open [Document intelligence](/admin/document-intelligence).

In **Classification and extraction**, turn on the options you want: **Enable automatic classification**, **Enable AI-assisted classification**, **Enable automatic document type association**, **Enable automatic document type creation** and **Enable AI-assisted extraction**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Create shipment drafts from documents
steps: Open [Document intelligence](/admin/document-intelligence).
In **Shipment draft extraction**, turn on **Enable shipment draft extraction**.
Tick the records whose documents may produce drafts: **Shipment**, **Trailer**, **Tractor** or **Worker**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Make document text searchable
steps: Open [Document intelligence](/admin/document-intelligence).
In **Search and retrieval**, turn on **Enable full-text indexing**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to document control. The AI-assisted options depend on an enabled AI provider that serves document work, which is set up on [AI control](/admin/agent-control). Provider-specific parsing rules live on [Parsing rules](/admin/document-parsing-rules).

pages.name: Document operations
pages.description: Inspect document lifecycle state and trigger recovery actions
pages.summary:
Document operations is a support tool for one uploaded document at a time. Paste a document's ID and the page shows where it is in its lifecycle: a pipeline of **Upload**, **Preview**, **Extraction** and **Draft** with each step's status, the file's details (the record it belongs to under **Resource**, **Version**, **Created**, **Updated**, **Preview status**, **Content status**, **Draft status** and **Detected kind**), whether **Extracted content** and a **Shipment draft** exist, and any errors detected.

Below that it lists the document's **Version history**, its **Upload sessions** and the **Workflow references** behind its background processing, and offers **Recovery actions** to restart the steps that failed. Administrators and support staff use it when a document has no preview, its text was never extracted, or it does not show up in search.

tasks.title: Inspect a document
steps: Open [Document operations](/admin/document-operations).
Paste the document's ID into **Paste a document ID to inspect...** and select **Inspect**.
Read the pipeline and statuses to see which step stopped, and the error count if any errors were detected.
Check **Version history**, **Upload sessions** and **Workflow references** for more detail.

tasks.title: Re-run a failed step
steps: Inspect the document in [Document operations](/admin/document-operations).

Under **Recovery actions**, choose the step to restart: - **Reextract content** re-processes the document's text and structured data. - **Regenerate preview** starts a new thumbnail workflow. - **Resync search** updates the document's search index entry with its latest data.
Select **Confirm**. The action starts in the background; inspect the document again after a short wait to see the result.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to document operations; the recovery actions need update access to document operations. If the ID is wrong or the document no longer exists, the page shows "Failed to load diagnostics" with **Retry**.

pages.name: Parsing rules
pages.description: Define provider-specific parsing rules, test with fixtures, and simulate extraction results
pages.summary:
Document parsing rules teach Trenova how to read documents from a particular provider or format, such as one broker's rate confirmation. Each rule set is listed in the sidebar on the left; selecting one opens it with four tabs: **Metadata** (name, document kind, priority and the published version), **Versions** (draft and published versions of the rules), **Fixtures** (saved sample documents with expected results) and **Simulation** (run a version against pasted document text and see what it extracts).

A version says which documents it matches (**Match config**) and what to pull out of them (**Rule builder**: sections, fields and stops). Drafts can be edited; publishing a draft makes it the version used in production.

tasks.title: Create a rule set
steps: Open [Parsing rules](/admin/document-parsing-rules).
Select **New** at the top of the sidebar (or **Create rule set** when there are none).
Enter a **Name** that identifies the provider or document format and select **Create**.
On the **Metadata** tab, set the **Document kind**, **Priority** and **Description**, then select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Write and publish a version of the rules
steps: Open [Parsing rules](/admin/document-parsing-rules) and select the rule set in the sidebar.
Open the **Versions** tab and select **New draft**. The new draft opens.
Under **Version settings**, give it a **Label** and choose the **Parser mode**.
On **Match config**, fill in **Provider fingerprints**, **File name contains**, **Requires all**, **Requires any** and **Section anchors** so the rules match the right documents.
On **Rule builder**, use **Add section**, **Add field** and **Add stop** to define what to extract, then select **Save changes**.
When it is ready, select **Publish** and confirm with **Publish version**. The previously published version is archived and this version becomes read-only.

tasks.title: Test rules against sample documents
steps: Open [Parsing rules](/admin/document-parsing-rules) and select the rule set.

To keep a sample, open **Fixtures** and select **New fixture**. In the fixture that opens, paste the **Full document text**, describe the expected results under **Assertions**, and select **Save fixture**.
To try a version, open **Simulation**, choose the **Version**, paste the **Document text**, optionally fill in **File name** and **Provider fingerprint**, and select **Run simulation**.

tasks.title: Delete a rule set
steps: Open [Parsing rules](/admin/document-parsing-rules) and select the rule set.
Select the delete button in its header and confirm with **Delete**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to document parsing rules. Creating rule sets, drafts and fixtures needs create access, deleting needs delete access, and **Publish** appears only for people who may activate parsing rules. Only draft and published versions can be simulated, and published or archived versions cannot be edited.

pages.name: GraphQL explorer
pages.description: Browse, search, and run every persisted GraphQL operation in the client
pages.summary:
GraphQL explorer is a developer tool that lists every persisted GraphQL operation the Trenova web client uses, with the fragments they share. The header shows how many operations and fragments exist. The left side is a searchable list grouped into **Operations** and **Fragments**; the right side shows the selected item.

For an operation, the **Definition** tab shows its **Variables**, **Input types**, **Root fields**, the fragments it uses and the full definition; the **Run** tab lets you execute it with your own variables and see the **Response**; the usages tab lists the source files that reference it. Developers and technical administrators use it to understand what the app asks the server for and to try an operation directly.

tasks.title: Find an operation or fragment
steps: Open [GraphQL explorer](/admin/graphql-explorer).
Type in **Search operations…** to search by name, field or domain.
Narrow the list with **All**, **Queries**, **Mutations** or **Fragments**, then select an item.
Use **Copy name**, **Copy hash** or **Copy definition** to copy what you need.

tasks.title: Run an operation
steps: Open [GraphQL explorer](/admin/graphql-explorer) and select an operation.
Select the **Run** tab.
Edit the JSON under **Variables** (**Reset** puts back the starting template).
Select **Run** (or press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter). The **Response** appears with its status; use **Copy response** to copy it.
Select **History** to see the last runs of this operation and replay their variables, or **Clear** to empty the list.

tasks.title: See where an operation is used
steps: Open [GraphQL explorer](/admin/graphql-explorer) and select an operation or fragment.
Select the usages tab to see the source files that reference it. For a fragment, the **Definition** tab also lists the operations that use it and any **Nested fragments**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to the organization. Runs go to the live server under your own account, so they only return what your permissions allow. A mutation shows "Mutation — executes against live data": running it really changes records, with no extra confirmation. An operation with no persisted hash cannot be run.

pages.name: Hazmat seg. rules
pages.description: Manage and configure hazmat segregation rules for your organization
pages.summary:
Hazmat segregation rules say which hazardous material classes may not travel together, or may only travel together with separation. Each rule pairs a **Class A** with a **Class B** (and can narrow the pair to a specific **Hazardous material A** and **Hazardous material B**) and sets the **Segregation type**: **Prohibited**, **Separated**, **Distance** (with a minimum distance) or **Barrier**. Rules can record exceptions and the regulation they come from, such as a 49 CFR reference.

The table lists **Status**, **Name**, **Description**, **Class A**, **Class B**, **Segregation type**, **Min distance**, **Has exceptions** and **Updated At**. Safety and compliance staff maintain it; the rules are used when shipments are checked for hazmat segregation.

tasks.title: Add a segregation rule
steps: Open [Hazmat segregation rules](/admin/hazmat-segregation-rules).
Select **New hazmat segregation rule**.
Set **Status**, and enter a **Name** and optional **Description**.
Choose **Class A** and **Class B**. To apply the rule to specific materials only, also pick **Hazardous material A** and **Hazardous material B**.
Choose the **Segregation type**. For **Distance**, also enter the **Minimum distance** and choose the **Distance unit** (**Feet**, **Meters**, **Inches** or **Centimeters**).
If the rule has exceptions, turn on **Has exceptions** and describe them in **Exception notes** (required once the switch is on).
Optionally record the **Reference code** (for example 49 CFR 177.848) and **Regulation source**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change or deactivate a rule
steps: Open [Hazmat segregation rules](/admin/hazmat-segregation-rules).
Select the rule's row (or right-click it and choose **Edit**).
Change the fields, or set **Status** to **Inactive** to stop using the rule, and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Find rules for a hazard class
steps: Open [Hazmat segregation rules](/admin/hazmat-segregation-rules).
Use the search box, or select **Filter** to narrow by **Status**, **Class A**, **Class B**, **Segregation type** or **Has exceptions**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to hazmat segregation rules; **New hazmat segregation rule** appears only for people who can create them. Whether shipments are checked against these rules is turned on with **Check Hazmat segregation** on [Shipment controls](/admin/shipment-controls). The hazardous material records themselves are kept on [Hazardous materials](/shipment-management/configuration-files/hazardous-materials).

pages.name: Hold reasons
pages.description: Manage and configure hold reasons for your organization
pages.summary:
Hold reasons are the reasons people choose when putting a shipment on hold. Each reason has a **Hold type** (Operational, Compliance, Customer or Finance), a **Reason code**, a **Display name**, a **Default severity** and gating rules that decide what the hold blocks by default: dispatch, delivery and/or billing.

The table lists each reason with its **Active**, **Type**, **Code**, **Label**, **Description**, **Default severity**, **Blocks dispatch**, **Blocks delivery** and **Blocks billing** columns. Administrators maintain the list so holds are applied and reported consistently.

tasks.title: Add a hold reason
steps: Open [Hold reasons](/admin/hold-reasons).
Select **New hold reason**.
Choose the **Hold type**, enter a **Reason code** (for example ELD_OOS) and a **Display name**, and optionally **Details**.
Choose the **Default severity**: **Informational**, **Advisory** or **Blocking**.
Under **Gating rules**, turn on **Block dispatch**, **Block delivery** and/or **Block billing**, and **Visible to customer** if customers may see this reason.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit or retire a hold reason
steps: Open [Hold reasons](/admin/hold-reasons).
Select the row to open it.
Change the fields, or turn off **Active** so the reason is no longer offered.
Select **Save**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to hold reasons; **New hold reason** appears only for people who can create them, and editing needs update access. The severity and gating rules are defaults applied when someone picks the reason; they can be adjusted on each hold.

pages.name: Home screens
pages.description: Author a home screen once and assign it to the roles that should land on it.
pages.summary:
Home screens lets administrators author a home screen once (the widgets people land on when they open Trenova) and assign it to the roles that should see it. Each home screen in the list shows its name, an **Org default** or **Locked** badge where they apply, how many widgets it has, who it reaches (its roles, a job function, or everyone without another assignment) and how many people it reaches today.

Until an administrator authors one, everyone lands on the home screen Trenova ships for their role. When someone matches more than one home screen, the one with the highest **Priority** wins.

tasks.title: Create a home screen for a role
steps: Open [Home screens](/admin/home-layouts).
Select **New home screen** (or **Create one** when the list is empty).
Enter a **Name** and optional **Description**.
Select **Add widget** (or **Add your first widget**), pick widgets from **Add a widget**, and select **Done**. Some widgets ask you to choose what they show before they land.
Drag widgets to rearrange them. Use a widget's options menu to change its **Width** and **Height**, **Configure** it, or **Remove** it.
Under **Assign to roles**, tick the roles that should land on it, or choose a function in **Or assign by job function** to reach every role tagged with that function, including roles added later.
Select **Create**. The editor stays open on the new home screen.

tasks.title: Edit a home screen
steps: Open [Home screens](/admin/home-layouts) and select **Edit** on the home screen (or select its name).
Change the widgets, name, roles or settings, then select **Save**. **Discard** throws away unsaved changes.

tasks.title: Set the organization default or lock a home screen
steps: Open the home screen from [Home screens](/admin/home-layouts).
Turn on **Organization default** to make it where anyone without a role assignment lands. Only one home screen can hold this.
Turn on **Lock this home screen** so the people assigned it cannot rearrange it. Anything they saved earlier is kept and returns if you unlock it.
Set **Priority** (0 to 1000) to decide which home screen wins when someone matches more than one, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Preview what a role will see
steps: Open a saved home screen from [Home screens](/admin/home-layouts).
Choose a role in **Preview as**. The canvas shows what a member of that role resolves to today, read-only and drawn with your own permissions. Unsaved edits are not included.
Select **Stop** to go back to editing.

tasks.title: Delete a home screen
steps: Open [Home screens](/admin/home-layouts).
Select the trash button on the home screen's row and confirm with **Delete**. The people it reached fall back to the next home screen that matches them. This cannot be undone.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to home layout presets. **New home screen** appears only for people who can create them, and the trash button only for people who can delete them.

pages.name: Inbound mailboxes
pages.description: Addresses the system listens on, where each provider posts, and how much each is trusted to do without a person
pages.summary:
Inbound mailboxes are the email addresses Trenova listens on, such as one for tenders, one for PODs and one for carrier invoices. Each mailbox has an **Address**, the **Provider** that receives the mail and posts it to Trenova (Resend or Postmark), a webhook URL the provider posts to, a signing secret that proves each delivery really came from the provider, and a trust level saying how much the desk may do with its mail without a person.

Each mailbox card shows whether it is **Listening** or **Not listening**, what it is **Trusted to** do, its **Purpose** and when it was **Created**. A mailbox without a signing secret refuses every delivery. Administrators set mailboxes up here; the mail itself is read in the [Inbox](/inbox).

tasks.title: Create a mailbox
steps: Open [Inbound mailboxes](/admin/inbound-mailboxes).
Select **New mailbox**.
Enter a **Name** and the **Address**, choose the **Provider**, and set **Status** to **Listening**. Optionally describe its **Purpose**.

Choose **How much it may do alone**: **A person reviews everything**, **The desk acts when it is sure enough** (then set the **Confidence bar**, between 0.5 and 1) or **The desk acts on everything it can**.
For Resend, optionally paste the **Signing secret (optional)** now. Select **Create mailbox**.
Copy the webhook URL shown in the next dialog and set it as the provider's inbound webhook, then select **I have copied it**. The URL cannot be shown again.

tasks.title: Set or replace the signing secret
steps: Open [Inbound mailboxes](/admin/inbound-mailboxes) and find the mailbox.
Select **Set signing secret** (or **Replace secret**).
For Resend, paste the webhook's signing secret (it starts with whsec_) into **Signing secret** and select **Save secret**.
For Postmark, select **Generate credentials** (or **Replace the credentials**), copy the user and password into the webhook URL in Postmark, and select **I have copied them**.

tasks.title: Rotate a mailbox's webhook URL
steps: Open [Inbound mailboxes](/admin/inbound-mailboxes) and select **Rotate URL** on the mailbox.
Confirm with **Rotate**. The old URL stops working immediately and mail is refused until the provider is pointed at the new one.
Copy the new URL into the provider and select **I have copied it**.

tasks.title: Change a mailbox or stop it listening
steps: Open [Inbound mailboxes](/admin/inbound-mailboxes) and select **Edit** on the mailbox.
Change the fields, for example set **Status** to **Not listening**, and select **Save changes**. Changing the provider means setting the new provider's signing secret before mail is accepted again.

tasks.title: Read a mailbox's mail
steps: Open [Inbound mailboxes](/admin/inbound-mailboxes).
Select **Open its mail** on the mailbox to open the [Inbox](/inbox) filtered to it.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to inbound mailboxes. **New mailbox** needs create access, and **Edit**, **Rotate URL** and the secret buttons need update access. The webhook URL carries the mailbox's token, which is stored only as a hash; if it is lost, rotate for a new one.

pages.name: Integrations
pages.description: Connect the outside services Trenova works with: mileage, telematics, email, fuel prices and carrier data.
pages.summary: Integrations is where administrators connect the outside services Trenova works with. Each service is a card grouped by category (such as Email, Telematics, Mapping & Routing, Weather, Financial Data, Fuel Cards and Carrier Compliance) with its description, links to its docs, a button to open its settings and a switch showing whether it is connected. Services include Resend and Postmark (email), Samsara (telematics), Google Maps and PC*Miler (mileage and routing), OpenWeatherMap, OANDA Exchange Rates, EIA Fuel Prices, the WEX, Comdata and Ramp fuel card feeds, and CarrierOk and FMCSA QCMobile (carrier intelligence). Some cards describe planned providers that cannot be configured yet.

tasks.title: Find an integration
steps: Open [Integrations](/admin/integrations).
Type in **Search integrations**, or narrow the list with the category filter (**All categories** or one category) and the status filter (**All statuses**, **Connected** or **Disconnected**).
Change **Sort By** to **Name (A-Z)** or **Name (Z-A)** if needed.

tasks.title: Connect a service
steps: Open [Integrations](/admin/integrations) and find the service's card.
Select the card's button (or its switch) to open the service's settings.

Turn on the service's enable switch (for example **Enable Google maps** or **Enable Samsara**) and enter its credentials, such as the API key. When a key is already saved, leave the field blank to keep it.
Where offered, select **Test connection** to check the credentials work.
Select **Save changes** (or **Save configuration** for Samsara).

tasks.title: Set up Samsara telematics
steps: Open [Integrations](/admin/integrations) and open the Samsara card.
On **Configuration**, turn on **Enable Samsara**, enter the token, and select **Save configuration**. A token is required before Samsara can be enabled.
Copy the URL under **Webhook endpoint** and point Samsara's webhook at it. It is unique to your organization and appears after the configuration is saved.
Select **Worker sync** and choose **Start sync** to push Trenova worker records into Samsara. **Detect drift** and **Repair drift** find and fix workers that no longer match.

tasks.title: Configure carrier intelligence
steps: Open [Integrations](/admin/integrations) and open the CarrierOk or FMCSA QCMobile card.
On **Connection**, turn on the provider, enter its credentials and save. Select **Make primary** to make it the primary carrier intelligence provider; another enabled provider acts as the fallback.
On **Rules**, set the **Vetting rules** and **Enforcement** (for example **Refresh before tender** and **Disqualify on block**).
On **Monitoring**, choose which carriers are enrolled for continuous monitoring and the **Refresh cadence**.
On **Spend**, set a **Monthly spend cap** and how long raw data is kept, then select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to integrations; saving or testing a connection needs update access to integrations. Starting a Samsara worker sync needs update access to workers. The carrier intelligence tabs need read access to carrier intelligence, and changing them needs manage access.

pages.name: Invoice adjustment controls
pages.description: Configure organization policy for credits, rebills, write-offs, and invoice adjustment review.
pages.summary:
Invoice adjustment controls set the organization's policy for credits, rebills and write-offs on invoices. The page is one settings form in four cards: **Eligibility policy** (which invoices may be adjusted and which accounting date adjustments use), **Documentation requirements**, **Approval policy** (when adjustments and write-offs need approval) and **Credit and visibility** (customer credit balances and what customers see after an invoice is replaced).

Billing and finance managers use it to decide how much control to put around changing invoices that have already gone out.

tasks.title: Decide which invoices can be adjusted
steps: Open [Invoice adjustment controls](/admin/invoice-adjustment-controls).

In **Eligibility policy**, set the **Partially paid invoice adjustment policy**, **Paid invoice adjustment policy** and **Disputed invoice adjustment policy** to **Disallow**, **Allow with approval** or **Allow without approval**.
Set the **Adjustment accounting date policy** and **Closed period adjustment policy**.
Set the **Rerate variance tolerance percent** and **Replacement invoice review policy** for credit-and-rebill work.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Require approval for adjustments and write-offs
steps: Open [Invoice adjustment controls](/admin/invoice-adjustment-controls).

In **Approval policy**, set the **Standard adjustment approval policy** to **None**, **Always** or **Amount threshold**. With **Amount threshold**, enter the **Standard adjustment approval threshold**.
Set the **Write-off approval policy** to **Disallow**, **Always require approval** or **Require approval above threshold**, and enter the **Write-off approval threshold** if asked.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Require a reason on every adjustment
steps: Open [Invoice adjustment controls](/admin/invoice-adjustment-controls).
In **Documentation requirements**, set **Adjustment reason requirement** to **Required**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Control customer credits and superseded invoices
steps: Open [Invoice adjustment controls](/admin/invoice-adjustment-controls).
In **Credit and visibility**, set the **Customer credit balance policy** and **Over-credit policy**.
Set the **Superseded invoice visibility policy** to decide whether customer-facing views show only the current invoice or also the ones it replaced.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to invoice adjustment control; saving needs update access. Adjustments that need approval wait on [Pending approvals](/billing/pending-approvals).

pages.name: Carrier overrides
pages.description: Hold your fleet to stricter limits than a state requires. An override can only tighten a limit, never loosen one, and applies to your organization alone.
pages.summary:
Carrier overrides hold your own fleet to stricter oversize limits than a state requires. Each override names one state and can narrow its maximum width, height, length and weight, require more permit lead time, or add daylight-only and holiday restrictions the state does not impose. An override can only tighten a limit, never loosen one, and applies to your organization alone; any field left blank defers to the state's own rule.

The table lists each override with its **State**, a **Narrows** column showing which limits it tightens, and the **Reason** it exists. Safety, compliance and permitting staff maintain it.

tasks.title: Add a carrier override
steps: Open [Carrier overrides](/admin/jurisdiction-rule-overrides).
Select **New carrier override**.
Under **Jurisdiction**, choose the **State**.

Under **Tighter limits**, enter only the limits you want to narrow: **Max width**, **Max height**, **Max length** (feet) or **Max weight** (pounds). Leave the rest blank to defer to the state. A value above the state's limit is rejected.
Under **Lead time**, optionally enter a **Permit lead time** in days. It may require more notice than the state, never less.
Under **Added restrictions**, tick **Daylight only** or **Holiday restricted** if your fleet does not run oversize at night or on holidays in that state.
Under **Reason**, explain why you run tighter than the statute (at least 10 characters).
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change an override
steps: Open [Carrier overrides](/admin/jurisdiction-rule-overrides).
Select the override's row (or right-click it and choose **Edit**).
Change the limits, restrictions or **Reason** and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Remove an override
steps: Open [Carrier overrides](/admin/jurisdiction-rule-overrides) and select the override's row.
Select **Remove override** at the bottom of the panel. The state reverts to its statutory limits for your organization.

tasks.title: Find overrides
steps: Open [Carrier overrides](/admin/jurisdiction-rule-overrides).
Use the search box, or select **Filter** to filter on **Reason**. The **State** column can be sorted.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to carrier overrides; **New carrier override** appears only for people who can create them. A restriction the state already imposes cannot be lifted here. The statutory limits themselves live on [Jurisdiction rules](/admin/jurisdiction-rules).

pages.name: Jurisdiction rules
pages.description: Oversize and overweight limits per state. These limits are shared across every organization; record a carrier override to hold your own fleet to something stricter.
pages.summary:
Jurisdiction rules hold each state's oversize and overweight limits: the legal width, height, length and weight above which a load needs a permit, superload thresholds, permit lead time, validity and fees, and travel restrictions such as daylight-only movement. The permit engine uses active rules.

These rules are shared by every organization on the platform, not just yours. To hold your own fleet to a stricter limit, record a carrier override on [Jurisdiction rule overrides](/admin/jurisdiction-rule-overrides) instead. The table lists each rule's **State**, **Verification**, **Status**, **Max width**, **Max height**, **Max length**, **Max weight**, **Lead time** and **Verified** date.

tasks.title: Add a state's limits
steps: Open [Jurisdiction rules](/admin/jurisdiction-rules).
Select **New jurisdiction rule**.
Under **Jurisdiction**, choose the **State** and **Status**. Only **Active** rules are used.
Under **Legal limits**, enter **Max width**, **Max height**, **Max length** and **Max weight**.
Optionally fill in **Superload thresholds**, **Permit terms** (**Lead time**, **Validity**, **Base fee**, **Per mile fee**) and **Travel restrictions**.
Under **Source**, record the **Source note** and **Source URL** the figures came from.
Select **Save**. A new rule starts unverified.

tasks.title: Correct a state's limits
steps: Open [Jurisdiction rules](/admin/jurisdiction-rules).
Select the state's row.
Change the values and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Verify a rule against the state
steps: Open [Jurisdiction rules](/admin/jurisdiction-rules) and select the state's row.
Select **Verify**.
Choose the **Outcome**: verified if it matches the issuing state, or disputed if the state contradicts it.
Describe **What you checked** (at least 10 characters) and optionally add a **Source URL**.
Select **Record verification**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to jurisdiction rules. Creating needs create access, editing needs update access, and recording a verification needs approve access. Changing any limit clears the rule's verification; editing only the **Source** section keeps it. Verifying does not change the limits, so fix wrong numbers by editing the rule.

pages.name: Organization settings
pages.description: Manage your organization profile, compliance, and security settings
pages.summary:
Organization settings holds the organization's profile, sign-in security and subscription details, in three tabs: - **General**: the logo (**Organization branding**), **Organization details** (name, timezone and tenant login slug), the **Operating model**, **Regulatory compliance** identifiers (SCAC, DOT number and tax ID) and the **Registered address**. - **Security**: four sub-tabs. **Sign-in** manages OIDC identity providers for single sign-on, **Provisioning** manages SCIM directories, tokens and group-to-role mappings, **Policies** holds priority-ordered access policies, and **Activity** shows authentication events, risk decisions, external identities and MFA authenticators. - **Billing & usage**: the access state, plan, enabled features and metered usage for the period.

Administrators use it to keep the company's details current and to set up single sign-on and user provisioning.

tasks.title: Update the company profile
steps: Open [Organization settings](/admin/organization-settings) on the **General** tab.
Edit **Organization details** (**Name**, **Timezone**, **Tenant login slug**), **Regulatory compliance** (**SCAC code**, **DOT number**, **Tax ID**) and the **Registered address**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Change the organization logo
steps: Open [Organization settings](/admin/organization-settings) on the **General** tab.
In **Organization branding**, select **Upload logo** and choose an image.
Adjust the crop and select **Upload logo**. Use **Remove logo** to take it off.

tasks.title: Set the operating model
steps: Open [Organization settings](/admin/organization-settings) on the **General** tab.
In **Operating model**, pick a **Preset**: Asset, Brokerage or Hybrid. The preset sets the **Brokerage features** and **Asset operations** switches, which can also be changed one at a time.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set up single sign-on
steps: Open [Organization settings](/admin/organization-settings) and select the **Security** tab, then **Sign-in**.
Select **Add provider**. Under **Quick start**, pick a provider such as Entra ID or Okta to fill in common defaults.
Fill in the **OIDC application** values: **Issuer URL**, **Redirect URI**, **Client ID**, **Client secret** and **OIDC scopes**.
Under **Access boundaries**, enter **Allowed domains** and turn on **Enabled**, and optionally **Enforce SSO**, **Auto-provision users** and **Trust federated MFA**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Provision users from a directory with SCIM
steps: Open [Organization settings](/admin/organization-settings) and select the **Security** tab, then **Provisioning**.
Under **SCIM directories**, select **Add**, enter the **Tenant slug**, turn on **Enabled** and select **Save**.
With the directory selected, enter a token name under **SCIM tokens** and select **Create token**. Copy the token straight away; it is only shown once.
Under **Group role mappings**, select **Add mapping** and map an **External group ID** to a **Role**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Check plan and usage
steps: Open [Organization settings](/admin/organization-settings) and select the **Billing & usage** tab.
Review the **Access state**, **Plan**, **Usage this period** and **Enabled features**. Select **Refresh** to reload usage.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to the organization; saving the **General** tab needs update access. The operating model only changes what appears in menus and navigation; it does not change permissions, API access or existing records. Revoke a SCIM token with **Revoke** in its row once it is no longer used.

pages.name: Roles
pages.description: Manage roles and permissions for your organization
pages.summary:
Roles decide what people in your organization can see and do. Each role holds a set of permissions: for every resource (shipments, customers, invoices and so on) which operations the role may perform, such as read, create or update, and how much data it reaches (**Own data only**, **Organization** or **All data**). A role also sets a **Max sensitivity** level (**Public**, **Internal**, **Restricted** or **Confidential**) that caps which sensitive fields its members can see.

The table lists each role's **Name**, **Description**, **Max sensitivity** and **Created At**. Administrators build roles here and then assign them to people on [Users](/admin/users).

tasks.title: Create a role
steps: Open [Roles](/admin/roles).
Select **New role**. The **Create role** page opens.
Under **Role details**, enter a **Name**, choose the **Max sensitivity level**, optionally pick a **Core responsibility**, and add a **Description**.

Under **Permissions**, optionally start from a template button at the top right: Viewer (read-only access to all resources), Editor (read and update), Manager (read, create and update on all resources) or Custom (start empty).
Adjust the permissions (see below), then select **Create role** at the top of the page.

tasks.title: Set a role's permissions
steps: On the create or edit page for a role, go to **Permissions**.
Use **Search resources...** to find a resource, or expand a category.

Select an operation chip on a resource's row to grant or remove that operation. The box at the start of the row toggles **Grant all** or **Remove all** for that resource, and **All** or **None** on a category header does the same for every resource in the category.
For a granted resource, choose how much data it reaches in the scope selector: **Own data only**, **Organization** or **All data**.

tasks.title: Edit a role
steps: Open [Roles](/admin/roles) and select the role's row. The edit page opens.
Change the **Name**, **Max sensitivity**, **Description** or the permissions.
Select **Save changes**. **Cancel** returns to the list without saving.

tasks.title: Give a role access to an agent
keywords: which agents a role can use
steps: Open [Roles](/admin/roles) and select the role's row. The edit page opens.
Go to **Agents**. It lists the agents this role is granted.
Select **Add an agent** and pick the agent. It is saved at once, without **Save changes**.
To take one away, select the remove button at the end of its row; that is saved at once too.

tasks.title: Find a role
steps: Open [Roles](/admin/roles).
Use the search box, or select **Filter** to narrow the list.

pages.notes:
Viewing the page needs read access to roles; **New role** needs create access. System roles show the banner "This is a system role. Some properties may be restricted." and their name, sensitivity and description cannot be changed. Changes to a role apply to everyone who holds it. A role's job function (**Core responsibility**) is also what [Home screens](/admin/home-layouts) can assign by.

A role's agents matter for agents limited to specific roles in [AI control](/admin/agent-control): people holding the role, or a role that inherits it, can use those agents and decide what they propose. Agents open to everyone who can use the assistant are included for every role automatically and need not be added; one that is granted anyway shows **Open to everyone**, and the grant applies once it is limited to specific roles. System agents cannot be granted to a role. Changing a role's agents needs update access to roles.

pages.name: Sequence configuration
pages.description: Configure sequence generation formats for shipments and billing workflows
pages.summary:
Sequence configuration sets the format of the numbers the system generates: PRO numbers, consolidation, order and work order numbers, invoice numbers, journal batch and journal entry numbers, manual journal requests, driver settlement numbers and location codes.

A list on the left groups the sequences under Operations, Billing, Accounting, Payroll and Locations. Selecting one shows its settings and a **Live preview** of a sample value. Administrators use it when setting up the organization or changing a numbering scheme.

tasks.title: Change a number format
steps: Open [Sequence configuration](/admin/sequence-configs).
Select the sequence in the list on the left, for example the invoice number.
Under **Core structure**, set the **Prefix** and **Sequence digits**, and turn on **Use separators** to pick a **Separator character**.
Under **Date components**, turn on **Include Year** (choose the **Year digits**), **Include Month**, **Include ISO Week Number** or **Include Day**.
Under **Context components**, turn on **Include Location Code** or **Include Business Unit Code** if wanted.
Check the **Live preview**, then select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Use a custom format or add check digits
steps: Open [Sequence configuration](/admin/sequence-configs) and select the sequence.
Expand **Advanced**.
Turn on **Include Random Digits** and set the **Random digits count**, or turn on **Include Check Digit**.
To write the layout yourself, turn on **Allow custom format** and enter a **Custom format template** using tokens such as {P} for prefix, {Y} for year and {S} for the sequence.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set how location codes are generated
steps: Open [Sequence configuration](/admin/sequence-configs) and select the location code in the list.
Under **Code strategy**, choose the **Components** to build the code from (name, city, state or postal code), in order.
Set the **Component width**, **Sequence digits**, **Separator**, **Casing** and **Fallback prefix**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Go back to the default format
steps: Open [Sequence configuration](/admin/sequence-configs) and select the sequence.
Select **Reset to default**, then **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to sequence configuration; saving needs update access. A dot next to a sequence in the list marks unsaved changes. Changes affect numbers generated from then on.

pages.name: Service failure reasons
pages.description: Manage operational exception reasons and EDI 214 defaults
pages.summary:
Service failure reason codes are the list of reasons people and the system pick from when a pickup or delivery goes wrong (a late delivery, a missed appointment, a weather delay). Each code has a stable **Reason code** identifier used for reporting and integrations, a **Display name** shown to operations and billing users, a **Category** (such as **Carrier**, **Customer**, **Facility**, **Weather** or **Driver**), and which stops it **Applies To**. Each code can also carry EDI defaults: the X12 status, reason and exception codes and a default note used when a service failure is sent on an EDI 214.

The table shows **Active**, **Code**, **Label**, **Category**, **Applies To**, **Description**, **X12 status**, **X12 reason**, **Sort** and **Created**. Administrators and operations managers maintain it.

tasks.title: Add a reason code
steps: Open [Service failure reason codes](/admin/service-failure-reason-codes).
Select **New service failure reason code**.
Leave **Active** on so the reason can be used for detected and manual service failures.
Enter the **Reason code** (for example LATE_DELIVERY) and the **Display name**.
Choose a **Category** and what the code **Applies To**: **Pickup**, **Delivery**, **Pickup & delivery** or **All stops**. Optionally describe when to use it in **Details**.
Under **EDI defaults**, optionally enter the **Status code**, **Reason code** and **Exception code** (up to 3 characters each) and a **Default note** for EDI 214 messages.
Under **Ordering**, set the **Sort order** (lower values appear first) and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change a reason code
steps: Open [Service failure reason codes](/admin/service-failure-reason-codes).
Select the code's row (or right-click it and choose **Edit**).
Change the fields and select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Archive or reactivate a reason code
steps: Open [Service failure reason codes](/admin/service-failure-reason-codes).
Right-click an active code and choose **Archive** to stop it being offered.
To bring an archived code back, right-click it and choose **Reactivate**.

tasks.title: Find a reason code
steps: Open [Service failure reason codes](/admin/service-failure-reason-codes).
Use the search box, or select **Filter** to narrow by columns such as **Active**, **Category** or **Applies To**. Most columns can be sorted.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to service failure reason codes; **New service failure reason code** appears only for people who can create them. Archiving makes a code inactive rather than deleting it; an inactive code is not available for detected or manual service failures.

pages.name: Settlement control
pages.description: Configure pay periods, accrual triggers, exception policies, and escrow interest
pages.summary:
Settlement control holds the organization's rules for driver settlements. The page is one settings form in four cards: **Pay period** (how often drivers are settled and when pay accrues), **Workflow automation** (automatic batches, approval and posting), **Exception detection** (flagging settlements that differ from a driver's recent history) and **Escrow interest** (interest on owner-operator escrow).

Payroll and settlement managers use it to set the settlement cycle and decide how much of it runs without manual review.

tasks.title: Set the pay period and pay trigger
steps: Open [Settlement control](/admin/settlement-control).
In **Pay period**, choose the **Frequency** (**Weekly**, **Biweekly** or **Monthly**) and the **Period end day**.
Enter the **Pay Delay (days)** between the period end and the pay date.
Choose the **Pay trigger**, the milestone at which driver pay accrues: **Move completed**, **Shipment delivered**, **POD received (ready to invoice)** or **Shipment invoiced**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Automate settlement batches and approval
steps: Open [Settlement control](/admin/settlement-control).
In **Workflow automation**, turn on the steps to automate: **Auto-generate batches**, **Auto-approve clean settlements**, **Auto-attach new pay to open drafts** and **Auto-post on approval**.
Turn on **Allow negative net (carry forward)** to carry a negative balance to the next settlement instead of capping deductions.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Flag unusual settlements
steps: Open [Settlement control](/admin/settlement-control).
In **Exception detection**, set the **Variance threshold** percentage and the **Lookback (settlements)** count used for the driver's trailing average.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set escrow interest
steps: Open [Settlement control](/admin/settlement-control).
In **Escrow interest**, enter the **Default annual interest rate** and the **Accrual Frequency (months)** (1 to 3).
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: The page is only available to organizations with asset operations turned on. Opening it needs read access to settlement control; saving needs update access. The default interest rate applies to new escrow accounts unless an account overrides it; see [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts).

pages.name: Shipment controls
pages.description: Configure and manage your shipment control settings
pages.summary:
Shipment control holds the organization-wide rules for shipments. The page is one settings form in five cards: **Performance metrics configuration** (tracking customer rejections), **Shipment processing configuration** (weight limit, duplicate bill of lading check, move removals and hazmat segregation checks), **Shipment delay management** (automatically marking shipments delayed), **Auto cancel shipments** (cancelling shipments left in New status) and **Detention management** (how detention time is tracked and charged).

Administrators and operations managers use it to set how strict shipment entry is and what the system does automatically.

tasks.title: Set shipment entry checks
steps: Open [Shipment controls](/admin/shipment-controls).
In **Shipment processing configuration**, set the **Max shipment weight limit** in pounds.
Turn on **Check for duplicate bills of lading** to require a unique BOL number on each new shipment, and **Check Hazmat segregation** to verify hazmat shipments are properly segregated.
Turn on **Allow move removals** only if users may permanently remove moves from shipments instead of cancelling them.
Select **Save changes** in the bar that appears at the bottom.

tasks.title: Mark late shipments as delayed automatically
steps: Open [Shipment controls](/admin/shipment-controls).
In **Shipment delay management**, turn on **Automatic delay status updates**.
Enter the **Delay status threshold** in minutes.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Cancel stale new shipments automatically
steps: Open [Shipment controls](/admin/shipment-controls).
In **Auto cancel shipments**, turn on **Automatic cancel shipments**.
Enter the **Auto cancel shipments threshold** in days a shipment may stay in New status.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set up detention tracking and charges
steps: Open [Shipment controls](/admin/shipment-controls).
In **Detention management**, turn on **Use detention policy engine** to compute detention with detention policies, and optionally pick a **Default detention policy**.

Or, for the flat threshold, turn on **Track detention time**, then set **Detention charge** and **Detention threshold** (free time in minutes), and turn on **Auto generate detention charges** to add detention lines to invoices automatically.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to shipment control. The detention policy engine needs at least one active detention policy or a default policy; set those up on [Detention policies](/detention/configuration-files/detention-policies). **Track customer rejections** in **Performance metrics configuration** records when customers refuse shipments.

pages.name: Stored mileages
pages.description: Review reusable mileage records captured from PC*Miler calculations
pages.summary:
Stored mileages are reusable mileage records captured from PC*Miler calculations. When stored mileage is turned on in [Distance controls](/admin/distance-controls), calculations check these records before calling PC*Miler. The table shows each record's lane (with any intermediate stops), distance, routing type, method, status, how many times it has been used (**Hits**) and when it was calculated.

The page is for review: records are created by the mileage calculations, not typed in here.

tasks.title: Review stored lane mileage
steps: Open [Stored mileages](/admin/stored-mileages).
Search, or use **Filter** to narrow by route, distance, routing, method or status.
Sort by **Hits** to see the lanes reused most, or by **Calculated** to see the newest records.

tasks.title: Stop a stored mileage from being reused
steps: Open [Stored mileages](/admin/stored-mileages).
Right-click an active record and choose **Deactivate**.
Confirm with **Deactivate**. The record is kept for audit and history but is no longer used in future mileage lookups.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to stored mileage. To fix the distance for a lane rather than stop reusing it, add a [distance override](/admin/distance-overrides).

pages.name: Table change alerts
pages.description: Monitor and review system activity across your organization
pages.summary:
Table change alerts notify people when records change. A subscription watches one table (optionally one record) for inserts, updates or deletes, can narrow the match with conditions, and sends a notification with a chosen priority and an optional custom title and message.

The page has two tabs. **Subscriptions** lists subscriptions with their **Name**, **Table**, **Events**, **Status**, **Priority** and **Conditions**. **Notifications** shows your recent notifications, newest first, with unread ones highlighted. Administrators and operations leads use it to keep an eye on changes that matter to them, such as a shipment's status changing.

tasks.title: Create a subscription
steps: Open [Table change alerts](/admin/table-change-alerts).
On the **Subscriptions** tab, select **New subscription**.
Enter a **Name** and choose the **Table** to monitor.
Optionally enter a **Record ID** to watch a single record, and set the **Priority**.
Under the event types, tick Insert, Update and/or Delete. At least one is required.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Only alert on specific changes
steps: Open the subscription from the **Subscriptions** tab, or start a new one.
Under **Conditions**, select **Add condition**, then enter the field, choose an operator (such as **Equals** or **Changed to**) and enter the value.
Set **Condition matching** to **Match ALL conditions** or **Match ANY condition**.
Optionally list **Watched columns** (comma-separated) so updates only trigger when those columns change.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Customize the notification text
steps: Open the subscription from the **Subscriptions** tab.
Under **Notification**, enter a **Topic**, a **Custom title** and a **Custom message**. The title can use placeholders such as {{table}}, {{operation}}, {{new.field}} and {{old.field}}.
Leave **Custom message** empty to use the auto-generated summary.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Review and clear notifications
steps: Open [Table change alerts](/admin/table-change-alerts).
Select the **Notifications** tab.
Hover over an unread notification and select the check mark to mark it read, or select **Mark all read**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to table change alerts; **New subscription** appears only for people who can create them. Only tables the system allows for alerts appear in **Table**.

pages.name: Users & roles
pages.description: Manage users and their role assignments
pages.summary:
Users is where administrators manage the people who can sign in to Trenova and the roles they hold. It has two tabs: **Users**, the list of accounts, and **Roles & permissions**, the same role list as [Roles](/admin/roles). The **Users** table shows each person's name (with a dot showing whether they are online now), **Status**, **Username**, **Last login** and **Created At**.

Opening a user shows their details, the roles assigned to them, and which organizations in the business unit they can access.

tasks.title: Add a user
steps: Open [Users](/admin/users) on the **Users** tab.
Select **New user**.
Set **Status**, and enter the **Full name**, **Username**, **Email address** and **Timezone**.
Leave **Require password change on first login** on if the person should set a new password after signing in.
Choose one or more **Roles**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change a user's roles
steps: Open [Users](/admin/users) and select the user's row (or right-click an active user and choose **Manage memberships**).
Under **Assigned roles**, select **Assign role**, choose the **Role**, and optionally set **Expires At** (leave it empty for a permanent assignment). Select **Assign role** to confirm.
To take a role away, select the remove button beside it in **Assigned roles**.

tasks.title: Give a user access to other organizations
steps: Open [Users](/admin/users) and select the user's row.
Under **Organization access**, tick each organization the user may open in the current business unit.
Select **Save organization access**.

tasks.title: Edit or deactivate a user
steps: Open [Users](/admin/users) and select the user's row.
Change **Status**, **Full name**, **Email address** or **Timezone** and select **Save**. The **Username** cannot be changed.
To change several users at once, tick their rows, then use **Update status** in the bar that appears and pick **Active** or **Inactive**.

tasks.title: Manage roles from this page
steps: Open [Users](/admin/users) and select the **Roles & permissions** tab.
Select **New role** to build one, or select a role's row to edit its permissions. See [Roles](/admin/roles) for the steps.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to users; **New user** needs create access and editing needs update access. **Manage memberships** is not offered for inactive users. Role assignments and organization access are saved as soon as you confirm them, separately from the panel's **Save**.

pages.name: Batch monitor
pages.description: Track bulk adjustment submission progress, failures, and created artifacts.
pages.summary:
Batch monitor tracks bulk invoice adjustment submissions: how far each batch has got, which items failed and why, and what each item created. The list shows every batch with its submitter and counts of total, done, failed and pending items; a strip across the top counts batches in flight, failed items, approvals pending and write-offs.

Selecting a batch shows its totals, status, submission time, last failure count and idempotency key, and an **Item results** table with each invoice's outcome, failure reason and links to the invoice and adjustment it produced. Finance and billing staff use it to follow up on bulk corrections that did not fully succeed.

tasks.title: Check how a batch ran
steps: Open [Batch monitor](/billing/adjustment-batches).
Select a batch in the list.
Read the totals for succeeded, failed and pending items, then scan **Item results** for the failure reason on each failed invoice.

tasks.title: Find a batch
steps: Open [Batch monitor](/billing/adjustment-batches).
Search by batch ID, submitter or idempotency key in the box above the list.
Filter by status: **Queued**, **Submitted**, **Running**, **Completed**, **Failed** or **Partial**.

tasks.title: Open what a batch item created
steps: Open [Batch monitor](/billing/adjustment-batches) and select the batch.
In **Item results**, select **Invoice** to open the invoice on [Invoices](/billing/invoices), or **Adjustment** to open the adjustment on [Pending approvals](/billing/pending-approvals).

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to invoices. The page only monitors batches; it does not submit or retry them.

pages.name: Accessorial charges
pages.description: Manage and configure accessorial charges for your organization
pages.summary:
Accessorial charges is the list of extra services your organization bills on top of line haul, each with a code, a description and how it is priced. Billing and rating staff set them up here once; they are then picked by name when a charge is added to a shipment or to an item in the billing queue.

The table shows each charge's **Status**, **Code**, **Method**, **Description** and **Rate**.

tasks.title: Add an accessorial charge
steps: Open [Accessorial charges](/billing/configuration-files/accessorial-charges).
Select **New accessorial charge**.
Fill in **Status**, **Code** (for example LUM for a lumper fee) and **Description**.
Pick a **Method**: **Flat** for a fixed dollar amount, **Per unit** for a rate per mile, hour, day or stop (then choose the **Rate unit**), or **Percentage** for a share of the line haul.
Enter the **Amount** and select **Save** (or **Save & close**).

tasks.title: Change or retire an accessorial charge
steps: Open [Accessorial charges](/billing/configuration-files/accessorial-charges).
Select the charge's row to open it.
Change the fields you need, or set **Status** to **Inactive** to stop using it, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Find an accessorial charge
steps: Open [Accessorial charges](/billing/configuration-files/accessorial-charges).
Type in the search box, or use **Filter** and **Sort** in the table toolbar to narrow the list, for example by **Method** or **Status**.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to accessorial charges; **New accessorial charge** only appears for people who can create them.

pages.name: Charge types
pages.description: Charge types is a reserved page that has not been built yet.
pages.summary:
Charge types is a reserved page that has not been built yet. It is not in the navigation, and opening it shows only a notice that the page is under construction; nothing can be viewed or set up here.

Extra charges billed on shipments are set up on [Accessorial charges](/billing/configuration-files/accessorial-charges).

tasks.title: Set up a charge that is billed on shipments
steps: Open [Accessorial charges](/billing/configuration-files/accessorial-charges) instead; [Charge types](/billing/configuration-files/charge-types) only shows **This page is under construction**.
Select **New accessorial charge** and fill in the charge.

pages.notes: Opening the page needs read access to charge types.

pages.name: Customers
pages.description: Manage and configure customers for your organization
pages.summary:
Customers is the master list of the companies you bill. Each customer record holds its code, name and address, and three settings tabs that decide how it is billed: **Billing profile** (payment terms, credit, invoice format, billing schedule, automation and requirements), **Email profile** (who receives invoices by email and what the email says) and, on an existing customer, **Broker vetting**.

Billing and customer-service staff use it to add new customers and to change how an existing customer is invoiced, for example switching them to a monthly statement or requiring a PO number before billing.

tasks.title: Add a customer
steps: Open [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers).
Select **New customer**.
On the **General** tab, fill in **Status**, **Code** and **Name**, then the address (**Address Line 1**, **City**, **State**, **Postal code**).
Set up the **Billing profile** and **Email profile** tabs as needed, then select **Save** (or **Save & close**).

tasks.title: Change how a customer is invoiced
steps: Open [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers) and select the customer's row.
Open the **Billing profile** tab.

Under billing schedule, set **Invoice delivery** to **Per shipment**, **Per order** or **Statement (consolidated)**. For a statement, choose **Bill every** (the cycle) and how the period is split with **Separate invoice for each**.

Adjust **Payment term**, **Credit limit**, **Required document types** or the billing automation switches (such as **Auto-approve clean shipments** and **Auto-generate invoices**) as needed, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Set who receives the customer's invoices
steps: Open [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers) and select the customer's row.
Open the **Email profile** tab.
Fill in **To recipients**, and optionally the **Subject line**, CC and BCC recipients and the attachment filename, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Vet a customer as a broker
steps: Open [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers) and select the customer's row.
On the **General** tab, enter the **DOT number** and turn on **Vet as a broker**, then save.
Open the **Broker vetting** tab and select **Vet broker** to pull a vetting snapshot.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate several customers at once
steps: Open [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers).
Tick the rows you want to change.
Use **Update status** in the action bar that appears and pick **Active** or **Inactive**.

pages.notes:
Viewing the page needs read access to customers; adding one needs create access and changing one needs update access. The **Broker vetting** tab needs a carrier intelligence provider connected under integrations.

A statement customer's shipments collect in the **Statements** view of the [Billing queue](/billing/queue) until their period is billed.

pages.name: Packet rules
pages.description: Configure which document types are required for each resource type
pages.summary:
Document packet rules decide which document types each kind of record must carry. A rule pairs a **Resource type** (**Shipment**, **Trailer**, **Tractor** or **Worker**) with a **Document type**, and says whether that document is **Required**, whether more than one is allowed, where it sits in the packet, and whether it must have an expiration date with an early warning.

Compliance, safety and billing leads use it to set up the document packet for shipments, equipment and workers, including documents that expire and should be flagged before they do.

tasks.title: Add a packet rule
steps: Open [Packet rules](/billing/configuration-files/document-packet-rules).
Select **New document packet rule**.
Choose the **Resource type** and the **Document type** it requires.
Turn on **Required** if the document is mandatory, and **Allow multiple** if more than one may be attached. Set **Display order** (lower numbers appear first in the packet).
To track expiry, turn on **Expiration required** and set **Warning days**. Then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change a packet rule
steps: Open [Packet rules](/billing/configuration-files/document-packet-rules).
Select the rule's row, change the settings and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Delete a packet rule
steps: Open [Packet rules](/billing/configuration-files/document-packet-rules).
Right-click the rule's row and choose **Delete**, then confirm with **Delete**. This cannot be undone.

pages.notes:
The page is governed by document type permissions: viewing needs read access to document types, and adding or changing rules needs create or update access to them.

The document types a rule can use are managed on [Document types](/billing/configuration-files/document-types). Documents a customer requires before invoicing are set separately, in the customer's **Required document types** on [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers).

pages.name: Document types
pages.description: Manage and configure document types for your organization
pages.summary:
Document types is the list of kinds of document your organization stores, such as a signed BOL or proof of delivery. Each type has a code, name, classification, category, color and description. Uploads are tagged with a type, and other settings refer to types by name: a customer's required documents for billing, and the packet rules that say which documents a shipment, worker or other record must carry.

Admins and billing leads maintain this list. Some types are built into the system and cannot be changed.

tasks.title: Add a document type
steps: Open [Document types](/billing/configuration-files/document-types).
Select **New document type**.
Fill in **Code**, **Name**, **Classification** (**Public**, **Private**, **Sensitive** or **Regulatory**) and **Category** (for example **Shipment**, **Worker** or **Invoice**).
Optionally choose a **Color** and add a **Description**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Change a document type
steps: Open [Document types](/billing/configuration-files/document-types).
Select the type's row to open it.
Change the fields and select **Save**. A type marked **System document type** cannot be modified.

tasks.title: Find a document type
steps: Open [Document types](/billing/configuration-files/document-types).
Type in the search box, or use **Filter** and **Sort** in the table toolbar, for example to show one **Category** or **Classification**.

pages.notes:
Viewing the page needs read access to document types; adding and changing them need create and update access.

To make a type required before a customer's shipments can be invoiced, add it to the customer's **Required document types** on [Customers](/billing/configuration-files/customers). To require it on a kind of record, add a rule on [Packet rules](/billing/configuration-files/document-packet-rules).

pages.name: Formula templates
pages.description: Manage and configure formula templates for your organization
pages.summary:
Formula templates are the rating methods that turn shipment facts (distance, weight, stops, hazmat and so on) into a charge, for example a per-mile rate or a per-hundredweight rate. Each template is a formula (its **Expression**), plus a charge policy (minimum, maximum and rounding) and an optional charge breakdown. Rate agreement lanes and rate matrices name a template as their **Rating method**.

Pricing staff build and test templates in the Formula Studio, which opens when you create a template or select one in the list. The studio shows a **Live preview** of the charge as you type, pinned test **Scenarios**, and a **Reference** of the variables and functions you can use.
