pages.name: Inbound files
pages.description: Inbound files are the files Trenova has picked up from partner mailboxes, with their processing state: received, parsed, processed, partial, quarantined or duplicate.
pages.summary:
Inbound files are the files Trenova has picked up from partner mailboxes, with their processing state: received, parsed, processed, partial, quarantined or duplicate. Opening a file shows where it came from (partner, method, remote path, ISA sender and receiver), what processing produced, the transactions inside it with their acknowledgment status, and the raw content.

EDI support staff use it to find files that failed processing, fix the cause, and run them again. The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds.

tasks.title: Find out why a file failed
steps: Open [Inbound files](/edi/inbound-files).
Look for rows whose **Status** is Quarantined or Partial.
Select the row and read **Processing notes** under **Processing**, then check the **Source** details and **Raw content**.

tasks.title: Reprocess a file
steps: Open [Inbound files](/edi/inbound-files) and select the file's row.
After fixing the cause (for example a missing partner, mapping or communication profile), select **Reprocess file**. It is offered for quarantined and partially processed files.

tasks.title: Reprocess several files at once
steps: Open [Inbound files](/edi/inbound-files).
Tick the rows you want. A bar appears at the bottom of the screen.
Select **Reprocess**. Files that are not quarantined or partially processed are skipped.

pages.notes: Viewing inbound files needs read access to EDI; reprocessing needs update access to EDI. How long raw EDI payloads are kept is set on [Data retention](/organization/data-retention).

pages.name: Mapping profiles
pages.description: Mapping profiles translate a trading partner's values into your own records.
pages.summary:
Mapping profiles translate a trading partner's values into your own records. When a partner tenders a load, it refers to customers, locations, commodities, service types, shipment types, rating templates and accessorial charges by its own codes; a mapping profile says which of your records each code means. Service failure reasons map the other way, to the partner's X12 code. Each partner has one mapping profile, created when its first mapping is saved.

EDI coordinators maintain these so inbound load tenders can be approved without stopping for unmapped values.

tasks.title: Create a mapping profile for a partner
steps: Open [Mapping profiles](/edi/mapping-profiles).
Select New EDI mapping profile at the top of the table. The **New mapping profile** panel opens.
Under **Partner**, choose the trading partner.
Pick the tab for the kind of record you are mapping, such as **Customer**.
Enter the partner's value in **Source value key** and optionally a **Source label**, choose your record in **Select local record**, and optionally add a **Target label**.
Select **Save**. Saving the first mapping creates the partner's mapping profile.

tasks.title: Add or remove mappings on an existing profile
steps: Open [Mapping profiles](/edi/mapping-profiles) and select the profile's row.
Pick the tab for the kind of record.
To add a mapping, fill in **Source value key** and **Select local record**, then select **Save**. For failure reasons, choose the reason and type the **Partner X12 code** instead.
To remove a mapping, select the delete icon on its row.

pages.notes: Viewing mapping profiles needs read access to EDI; adding or deleting mappings needs update access to EDI. The same mappings can be edited from a partner's **Mappings** tab on [Partners](/edi/partners). Inbound transfers with values that have no mapping wait in Mapping required status on [Inbound transfers](/edi/transfers/inbound).

pages.name: Messages
pages.description: The EDI Messages page lists every X12 document Trenova has generated or received, with its transaction set, partner, direction, delivery status, acknowledgment status and control numbers.
pages.summary:
The EDI Messages page lists every X12 document Trenova has generated or received, with its transaction set, partner, direction, delivery status, acknowledgment status and control numbers. Opening a message shows its delivery attempts and last error, the acknowledgment details and the raw X12.

EDI support staff use it to confirm a document reached a partner, chase missing acknowledgments, and resend deliveries that failed. The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds.

tasks.title: Check whether a document was delivered and acknowledged
steps: Open [Messages](/edi/messages).
Search or filter by **Partner**, **Transaction** or **Control number**, and read the **Delivery** and **Acknowledgment** columns.
Select the row to see **Delivery** (status, **Attempts**, **Remote path**, **Last error**), **Acknowledgment** and the **Raw X12**.

tasks.title: Retry a failed delivery
steps: Open [Messages](/edi/messages) and select the message's row.
Select **Retry delivery**. It is offered for outbound messages that are queued, failed or dead-lettered.

tasks.title: Retry deliveries for several messages
steps: Open [Messages](/edi/messages).
Tick the rows you want. A bar appears at the bottom of the screen.
Select **Retry delivery**. Messages that cannot be retried are skipped.

tasks.title: Send a delivered document again
steps: Open [Messages](/edi/messages) and select the message's row.
Select **Replay delivery** to queue the already-delivered document for another delivery to the partner. It is offered for outbound messages with status Sent whose raw content is still kept.

pages.notes: Viewing messages needs read access to EDI; retrying and replaying need update access to EDI. How many attempts a delivery gets before it is dead-lettered is set on the partner's [communication profile](/edi/communication-profiles). How long raw payloads are kept is set on [Data retention](/organization/data-retention); once a payload is purged the message can no longer be replayed.

pages.name: Overview
pages.description: The EDI operations page is the live health view of electronic data interchange for your organization.
pages.summary:
The EDI operations page is the live health view of electronic data interchange for your organization. It counts documents that need attention (dead-lettered messages, quarantined files, stuck transfers, overdue acknowledgments), shows pipeline state, charts document volume and delivery success over time, scores each trading partner, and lists the most recent failures.

EDI coordinators and support teams use it to spot problems with partner deliveries and inbound processing and to jump straight to the record that needs work.

tasks.title: Check EDI health for a time window
steps: Open [Overview](/edi/overview).
Pick a window from the range buttons at the top right: **4h**, **24h**, **7d**, **30d** or **All**. The page opens on **24h**.

Read the **Needs attention** tiles (**Dead-lettered messages**, **Quarantined files**, **Stuck transfers**, **Overdue acknowledgments**) and the **Pipeline state** tiles (**Failed deliveries**, **Partially processed files**, **Pending approval**, **Rejected acknowledgments**).

Select a tile to open the matching list: message tiles open [Messages](/edi/messages), file tiles open [Inbound files](/edi/inbound-files), and transfer tiles open [Inbound transfers](/edi/transfers/inbound).

tasks.title: Compare trading partner performance
steps: Open [Overview](/edi/overview) and choose a time window.
Scroll to **Partner scorecards**. Each row shows **Sent**, **Failed**, **Dead-lettered**, **Received**, **Success rate**, acknowledgment timing (**Ack avg**, **Ack p95**) and **Overdue acks**.
Select a partner name to open [Messages](/edi/messages) filtered to that partner.

tasks.title: Open a recent failure
steps: Open [Overview](/edi/overview).
Scroll to **Recent failures**, which lists dead-lettered messages and quarantined files with the partner and error.
Select a row to open that message or inbound file, or use **View all messages** or **View all inbound files** to see the full lists.

pages.notes: Viewing EDI pages needs read access to EDI. When nothing moved through EDI in the chosen window, the page says so and offers a button that widens the window to all time; with no traffic at all it offers **Set up a trading partner**, which opens [Partners](/edi/partners).

pages.name: Partners
pages.description: The EDI Partners page lists your trading partners: external companies you exchange X12 documents with, and internal connections to other organizations in Trenova.
pages.summary:
The EDI Partners page lists your trading partners: external companies you exchange X12 documents with, and internal connections to other organizations in Trenova. Each partner holds its identifiers, contact, default transport and mapping profiles, and an onboarding readiness checklist. Connection requests from other organizations waiting for your answer appear above the table.

EDI coordinators and implementation teams use it to onboard new partners, keep partner defaults current, and accept or reject connection requests.

tasks.title: Add an external trading partner
steps: Open [Partners](/edi/partners).
Select New EDI connection at the top of the table. The **New EDI partner** panel opens on the **External partner** tab.
Under **Profile**, fill in **Partner code** (the SCAC or ISA ID), **Partner name**, **Status** and **Country**, and optionally **Customer**, **Timezone** and **Description**.
Under **Contact**, add the **Contact name**, **Contact email** and **Contact phone**.
Under **Defaults**, turn **Inbound enabled** and **Outbound enabled** on or off and pick a **Default transport profile** and **Default mapping profile** if they already exist.
Select **Create partner**.

tasks.title: Request a connection with another Trenova organization
steps: Open [Partners](/edi/partners) and select New EDI connection.
Switch to the **Internal connection** tab.
Under **Organization pairing**, pick the **Target organization**. The partner code and name for both sides fill in from the two organizations; review them and the contact fields.
Select **Request connection**. The other organization sees the request at the top of its Partners page.

tasks.title: Accept or reject a connection request
steps: Open [Partners](/edi/partners). Requests waiting on your organization are listed under **Pending EDI connection requests**.
Select **Accept** to connect. Accepting creates reciprocal internal partners and communication profiles.
Or select **Reject**, enter a reason (it is shared with the requesting organization), then select **Reject connection**.

tasks.title: Edit a partner and check its readiness
steps: Open [Partners](/edi/partners) and select the partner's row.
On the **Details** tab, change the fields you need, then select **Save partner**.
Open the **Readiness** tab to see which onboarding steps are complete. Missing steps offer shortcuts such as **Create communication profile**, **Open designer** or **Open test cases**.

tasks.title: Map partner values to your records
steps: Open [Partners](/edi/partners), select the partner's row and open the **Mappings** tab.
Choose the tab for the kind of record, such as **Customer**.

Enter the partner's value in **Source value key** (and optionally **Source label**), pick your record in **Select local record** (for failure reasons, type the **Partner X12 code**), then select **Save**.
To remove a mapping, select the delete icon on its row.

pages.notes: Viewing partners needs read access to EDI; creating partners and connections needs create access, and editing, mapping, accepting or rejecting needs update access to EDI. For internal partners, the code and name are controlled by the organization connection and cannot be edited here. Avoid changing a partner code after documents have been exchanged, since it is used in EDI envelopes.

pages.name: Test cases
pages.description: EDI test cases are saved certification scenarios.
pages.summary:
EDI test cases are saved certification scenarios. Each one pairs a stored document payload with a partner document profile and records the warnings and errors the rendered X12 is expected to produce. Running a test case renders the payload through the partner's template and reports whether the result matches.

EDI implementation teams use them to certify a partner's documents and to re-check templates after changes.

tasks.title: Create a test case
steps: Open [Test cases](/edi/test-cases).
Select **New EDI test case**.
Under **Test case**, enter a **Name**, choose the **Document profile** it certifies, and add a **Description**.
Under **Expected outcome**, set **Expected warnings** and **Expected errors**, and optionally list **Expected warning codes** and **Expected error codes**.
Under **Document payload**, paste the source data into **Payload**.
Select **Create test case**.

tasks.title: Run a test case and read the result
steps: Open [Test cases](/edi/test-cases) and select the test case's row.
Save any edits first, then select **Run preview**.
Read the verdict at the top: actual warning and error counts against the expected ones, and any missing or unexpected codes.
Select **Open inspector** to see the rendered X12 and its diagnostics. If the result is wrong, fix the payload or template, or update the expected counts and codes.

tasks.title: Edit or delete a test case
steps: Open [Test cases](/edi/test-cases) and select the row.
Change the fields and select **Save test case**, or select **Delete** to remove it.

pages.notes: Viewing test cases needs read access to EDI; creating needs create access, saving changes needs update access, and deleting needs delete access to EDI. A partner's **Readiness** tab on [Partners](/edi/partners) counts a test case as an onboarding step.

pages.name: Inbound transfers
pages.description: Inbound transfers are load tenders your trading partners have sent you.
pages.summary:
Inbound transfers are load tenders your trading partners have sent you. Each one waits here until someone reviews it: a tender whose partner values are not all mapped shows Mapping required, a ready one shows Pending approval. Approving a tender creates the shipment on your side; rejecting it sends the reason back to the partner on the outbound 990 response.

Customer service and dispatch staff work this queue to accept or decline incoming freight. The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds.

tasks.title: Review and approve a load tender
steps: Open [Inbound transfers](/edi/transfers/inbound) and select the tender's row.
Check the summary, then the **Tender** tab (moves and stops) and the **Freight** tab (commodities and additional charges).
Open the **Mappings** tab. For each unresolved value under **Mapping preview**, choose the matching **Local record**.
Select **Approve**. It becomes available once every required mapping is resolved. Trenova creates the shipment, and **Open shipment** links to it once it exists.

tasks.title: Reject a load tender
steps: Open [Inbound transfers](/edi/transfers/inbound) and select the tender's row.
Select **Reject**.
Enter the reason, which is shared with the submitting partner, then select **Reject transfer**.

tasks.title: Approve or reject several tenders at once
steps: Open [Inbound transfers](/edi/transfers/inbound).
Tick the rows you want. A bar appears at the bottom of the screen.
Select **Approve**, or select **Reject**, enter a reason and select **Reject tenders**. Only tenders still awaiting review are acted on; the rest are skipped.

pages.notes: Viewing transfers needs read access to EDI; approving and rejecting need update access to EDI. A tender can be approved or rejected only while it is Submitted, Mapping required or Pending approval. Saving mappings on [Mapping profiles](/edi/mapping-profiles) ahead of time keeps future tenders from that partner out of Mapping required.

pages.name: Outbound transfers
pages.description: Outbound transfers are load tenders your organization has sent to trading partners, with their current state: submitted, awaiting mappings or approval on the receiving side, approved, rejected, expired or canceled.
pages.summary:
Outbound transfers are load tenders your organization has sent to trading partners, with their current state: submitted, awaiting mappings or approval on the receiving side, approved, rejected, expired or canceled.

Dispatch and brokerage staff use it to follow up on tenders they have sent. The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds.

tasks.title: Send a shipment as a load tender
steps: Open [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) and open the row actions for the shipment.
Select **Send EDI load tender**, then **Send tender**. The action is shown only for shipments in New status whose customer is linked to an EDI partner and that are eligible to be tendered.
The tender then appears on [Outbound transfers](/edi/transfers/outbound).

tasks.title: Check the status of a sent tender
steps: Open [Outbound transfers](/edi/transfers/outbound).
Find the tender by its **Reference** (the BOL) or **Partner**, and read its **Status**.
Select the row to see the **Tender**, **Freight** and **Mappings** tabs. The **Target shipment** column reads Pending until the receiving side approves the tender and its shipment is created.

tasks.title: Cancel a sent tender
steps: Open [Outbound transfers](/edi/transfers/outbound) and select the tender's row.
Select **Cancel transfer**. It is offered only while the tender is Submitted, Mapping required or Pending approval.

pages.notes: Viewing transfers needs read access to EDI; canceling needs update access to EDI, and sending a tender from Shipments needs create access to EDI.

pages.name: Equipment manufacturers
pages.description: Manage and configure equipment manufacturers for your organization
pages.summary: Equipment manufacturers is the list of makers your tractors and trailers can be recorded against, such as Freightliner or Great Dane. Fleet administrators maintain it; every tractor and trailer must name one in its **Equip. manufacturer** field.

tasks.title: Add an equipment manufacturer
steps: Open [Equipment manufacturers](/equipment/configuration-files/equipment-manufacturers).
Select **New equipment manufacturer**.
Fill in **Status** and **Name**, and optionally a **Description**.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** or **Save & add another** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit an equipment manufacturer
steps: Open [Equipment manufacturers](/equipment/configuration-files/equipment-manufacturers).
Find the manufacturer with the search box or **Filter**, then select its row.
Change the fields and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate manufacturers
steps: Open [Equipment manufacturers](/equipment/configuration-files/equipment-manufacturers).
Tick the rows you want to change.
Choose **Update status** in the bar at the bottom of the table and pick the status.

pages.notes: - Viewing the page needs read access to equipment manufacturers; adding needs create access and editing or changing status needs update access.

pages.name: Equipment types
pages.description: Manage and configure equipment types for your organization
pages.summary: Equipment types are the categories your tractors, trailers and containers are sorted into, such as a 53-foot dry van or a reefer. Each type has a code, a class (Tractor, Trailer, Container or Other), an optional colour and an interior length. Fleet administrators maintain the list; every tractor and trailer must point at one.

tasks.title: Add an equipment type
steps: Open [Equipment types](/equipment/configuration-files/equipment-types).
Select **New equipment type**.
Fill in **Status**, **Code** and **Class**. These are required.
Optionally add a **Description**, a **Color** and the **Interior Length (ft)**.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** or **Save & add another** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit an equipment type
steps: Open [Equipment types](/equipment/configuration-files/equipment-types).
Find the type with the search box or **Filter**, then select its row.
Change the fields and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate equipment types
steps: Open [Equipment types](/equipment/configuration-files/equipment-types).
Tick the rows you want to change.
Choose **Update status** in the bar at the bottom of the table and pick the status.

pages.notes: - Viewing the page needs read access to equipment types; adding needs create access and editing or changing status needs update access.

pages.name: Tractors
pages.description: Manage and configure tractors for your organization
pages.summary:
Tractors lists every power unit in your fleet with its code, status, primary worker, equipment type, manufacturer and fleet code. Fleet and operations staff use it to add tractors, keep their registration, fuel and telematics details current, assign the drivers who run them, and mark units available, out of service, at maintenance or sold.

Opening a tractor also shows the documents stored against it and its driver vehicle inspection reports (DVIR) and defect history.

tasks.title: Add a tractor
steps: Open [Tractors](/equipment/tractors).
Select **New tractor**.
Fill in **Status**, **Code**, **Equipment type**, **Equip. manufacturer** and **Primary worker**. These are required.

Optionally add **Model**, **Make**, **Year** and **Fleet code**, the **Registration information** (**VIN**, **Registration number**, **License state**, **Registration expiry**, **License plate number**), a **Secondary worker**, the **Fuel type** and **IFTA qualified** setting, and the **Samsara vehicle ID** under **Telematics**.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** or **Save & add another** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit a tractor
steps: Open [Tractors](/equipment/tractors).
Find the tractor with the search box or **Filter**, then select its row.
Change the fields on the **Details** tab.
Select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Change a tractor's status
steps: Open [Tractors](/equipment/tractors).
Select the status badge in the tractor's **Status** column and pick the new status.
To change several at once, tick the rows, then choose **Update status** in the bar at the bottom of the table and pick the status.

tasks.title: Review a tractor's inspections and documents
steps: Open [Tractors](/equipment/tractors) and select the tractor's row.
Select the **Inspections** tab to see its inspection reports and defects, each marked **Open** or **Resolved**.
Select the **Documents** tab to view the files stored for the tractor, or **Upload** new ones.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to tractors and the asset operations feature. Adding a tractor needs create access; editing and status changes need update access. - **Inspections** come from a connected telematics provider. If none is connected the tab shows **Telematics not connected** with a link to **Open integrations**. - **IFTA qualified** decides whether the unit's miles and fuel count on the quarterly IFTA return.

pages.name: Trailers
pages.description: Manage and configure trailers for your organization
pages.summary: Trailers lists every trailer in your fleet with its code, status, equipment type, manufacturer, fleet code and last known location. Fleet and dispatch staff use it to add trailers, keep their registration and inspection details current, change their status, and record where a trailer actually is.

tasks.title: Add a trailer
steps: Open [Trailers](/equipment/trailers).
Select **New trailer**.
Fill in **Status**, **Code**, **Equipment type**, **Equip. manufacturer**, **Model** and **Make**. These are required.

Optionally add **Year**, **Max load weight**, **Fleet code** and the **Registration information** (**VIN**, **Registration number**, **Samsara asset ID**, **Registration state**, **Registration expiry**, **License plate number**, **Last inspection date**).
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** or **Save & add another** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit a trailer
steps: Open [Trailers](/equipment/trailers).
Find the trailer with the search box or **Filter**, then select its row.
Change the fields on the **Details** tab, or use the **Documents** tab to view and **Upload** files for the trailer.
Select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Record where a trailer is
steps: Open [Trailers](/equipment/trailers).
Right-click the trailer's row and choose **Locate trailer**.
Pick the **New location**, then select **Locate trailer**.

tasks.title: Change a trailer's status
steps: Open [Trailers](/equipment/trailers).
Select the status badge in the trailer's **Status** column and pick the new status.
To change several at once, tick the rows, then choose **Update status** in the bar at the bottom of the table and pick the status.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to trailers and the asset operations feature. Adding a trailer needs create access; editing, locating and status changes need update access. - Locating a trailer creates and completes an empty reposition move to the new location automatically, so the trailer's **Last known location** updates.

pages.name: Fuel cards
pages.description: The cards drivers fuel with — which provider issued each one, who carries it, and which unit it is tied to. Imported statements are matched to purchases through these cards.
pages.summary:
Fuel cards is the register of the cards drivers fuel with: which provider issued each one (Comdata, EFS, WEX or other), who carries it, and which tractor it is tied to. Imported fuel card statements are matched to purchases through these cards, so a card should be registered and assigned before its statement is imported.

Fleet and fuel staff maintain the list. The table shows each card's **Status**, **Label**, **Provider**, **Card** (last four digits), **Worker**, **Tractor**, **Expires** and **Updated**.

tasks.title: Register a fuel card
steps: Open [Fuel cards](/fuel/configuration-files/fuel-cards).
Select **New fuel card**.

Under **Card**, choose the **Provider**, enter the **Last four digits**, a **Label** (how the card is named in pickers and on purchases), the **Status**, and optionally the **Provider card ID** and **Expires** date.
Under **Assignment**, pick the **Driver** who normally carries it and the **Tractor** it lives in, and add any **Notes**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Assign or reassign a card
steps: Open [Fuel cards](/fuel/configuration-files/fuel-cards).
Right-click the card's row and choose **Assign card**.

Pick the **Tractor**, the **Driver**, or both, and select **Assign**. Purchases on the card then match to what it is assigned to. Leaving both empty puts the card back on [Unassigned cards](/fuel/unassigned-cards).

tasks.title: Cancel a lost or retired card
steps: Open [Fuel cards](/fuel/configuration-files/fuel-cards).
Right-click the card's row and choose **Cancel card**.
Enter a **Reason** and select **Cancel card**. The card stays on file for the purchases already made with it.

tasks.title: Find a card
steps: Open [Fuel cards](/fuel/configuration-files/fuel-cards).
Type in the search box, or use **Filter** and **Sort** in the table toolbar.

pages.notes:
This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to fuel cards; **Assign card** and **Cancel card** need permission to update fuel cards, and neither is offered on a card that is already cancelled.

Only the last four digits of a card are stored.

pages.name: IFTA tax rates
pages.description: The per-gallon rates each jurisdiction publishes for a quarter and fuel type, as the IFTA rate matrix lists them. A return cannot be finalized while any of its member lines is missing a rate.
pages.summary:
IFTA tax rates holds the per-gallon rates each jurisdiction publishes for a quarter and fuel type, as the IFTA rate matrix lists them, along with any per-gallon surcharge. The quarterly [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) price every jurisdiction line with these rates, and a return cannot be finalized while any of its member lines is missing one.

Fuel tax and compliance staff enter or import the rates each quarter. The table shows **Year**, **Quarter**, **Jurisdiction**, **Fuel**, **Rate / gal**, **Surcharge / gal**, **Source** and **Updated**.

tasks.title: Add a tax rate
steps: Open [IFTA tax rates](/fuel/configuration-files/ifta-tax-rates).
Select **New IFTA tax rate** (then **New IFTA tax rate** again if a menu opens).
Under **Period & product**, set the **Year**, **Quarter**, **Jurisdiction** and **Fuel type**.
Enter the **Rate per gallon** in USD per US gallon as printed in the matrix, and the **Surcharge per gallon** if the jurisdiction publishes one.
Record where it came from in **Source URL** and **Source note**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Import a quarter's rate matrix
steps: Open [IFTA tax rates](/fuel/configuration-files/ifta-tax-rates).
Select **New IFTA tax rate** and choose **Import rates**.
Pick the **Year** and **Quarter** every row is published for, then choose the CSV file. Use **Download template** if you are unsure of the layout.
Check the preview: rows marked **Ready** will be published and rows that need attention will be left out, with the **Problem** shown for each.
Confirm with the publish button to publish the rows that checked out.

tasks.title: Correct or delete a rate
steps: Open [IFTA tax rates](/fuel/configuration-files/ifta-tax-rates).
Select the rate's row, correct it and select **Save**.
To delete it, right-click the row, choose **Delete**, then **Delete rate**.

pages.notes:
This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to IFTA tax rates; importing needs permission to create them and **Delete** needs permission to delete them.

Rates are global: every organization is taxed at the rate published here, so a change or deletion moves the figures on every return for that quarter, not only yours. A rate of zero is a published rate, not a missing one. After changing rates, select **Recompute** on the quarter's return in [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns); a deleted rate shows as missing when the return is recomputed.

pages.name: Fuel surcharge
pages.description: DOE diesel prices, fuel surcharge programs, and automatic surcharge application
pages.summary:
Fuel management is where fuel surcharges are set up and applied automatically. It has three tabs: **Price dashboard** shows the latest weekly diesel prices; **Surcharge programs** holds the programs that turn a week's fuel price into a surcharge (per mile, a percentage of the charge, or a flat amount); and **Fuel indices** lists the price series programs read from, including the DOE / EIA prices that are brought in automatically every week and any custom indices you maintain yourself.

Billing and pricing staff create a program here, then assign it to customers through the **Fuel surcharge program** on the customer's billing profile, or to a rate agreement on its **Fuel** tab.

tasks.title: Create a fuel surcharge program
steps: Open [Fuel management](/fuel/configuration-files/surcharge) and go to **Surcharge programs**.
Select **New program**.
Fill in **Name**, **Code** and **Status**, choose the **Method**, the **Fuel index** it reads and the **Accessorial charge** the surcharge line posts against.

For a formula method, set the **Peg price**, **Increment** and **Rate per Increment**, or the **Miles per gallon** divisor. For a custom table method, build the **Price band table**: select **Generate** to fill it from a lowest and highest price and a band width, or **Add band** to enter bands yourself.

Adjust **Week resolution & rounding**, optional **Minimum amount** and **Maximum amount**, and the **Applicability** filters (**Shipment types**, **Service types**, **Tractor types**, **Trailer types**).
Select **Create program**.

tasks.title: Change or retire a program
steps: Open [Fuel management](/fuel/configuration-files/surcharge) and go to **Surcharge programs**.
Select the program's card, make your changes and select **Save changes**. Setting **Status** to inactive stops it applying surcharges immediately.
To remove a program, hover its card, select the delete icon and confirm with **Delete**.

tasks.title: Check this week's fuel price
steps: Open [Fuel management](/fuel/configuration-files/surcharge).
The **Price dashboard** shows each index's latest weekly price and its history. On **Surcharge programs**, each card shows the rate that applies this week.

tasks.title: Add a custom fuel index and its prices
steps: Open [Fuel management](/fuel/configuration-files/surcharge) and go to **Fuel indices**.
Select **New custom index**, fill in **Name**, **Code**, **Fuel type**, **Region** and **Currency**, and select **Create index**.
Open the index's **Price history**, enter the **Week (Monday)** and **Price ($/gal)**, and select **Add**. Record one price per week.

pages.notes:
Opening the page needs read access to fuel surcharge programs.

A program assigned to customer billing profiles cannot be deleted until it is unassigned. DOE / EIA prices are ingested automatically and cannot be deleted; only manually entered prices can be removed. Each program picks the price week from the shipment date it is set to use, and Monday's DOE price applies from the program's **Price effective day**.

pages.name: Feed runs
pages.description: Every time a connected fuel card feed has read your transactions, and what became of the rows. Rows a run could not place wait here until the card they were on is assigned or the unit they name is added.
pages.summary:
Feed runs lists every time a connected fuel card feed read your transactions, and what became of the rows. Once a provider is connected under [Integrations](/admin/integrations), Trenova reads its transactions on an hourly schedule; each read appears here with how many rows it read, how many it posted as fuel purchases and how many it is holding.

Rows are held when the run cannot place them: usually the card has not been assigned to a tractor or driver yet, or the unit number on the receipt does not match a tractor. They wait here until that is fixed. The table shows **Provider**, **Read**, **Rows**, **Posted**, **Held** and **Ran**.

tasks.title: Read a feed now
steps: Open [Feed runs](/fuel/feed-runs).
Select **Sync now** in the page header and pick the provider (Comdata, EFS or WEX).
A message reports how many rows were posted of those read, and how many are waiting on a card assignment or a missing unit.

tasks.title: See what a run held back
steps: Open [Feed runs](/fuel/feed-runs).
Select the run's row (or right-click it and choose **Review rows**). The rows it could not place are shown first.
Read the note on each held row to see why it was held.

tasks.title: Post held rows after fixing them
steps: Assign the card on [Unassigned cards](/fuel/unassigned-cards), or add the missing tractor.
Open [Feed runs](/fuel/feed-runs) and select the run.
Select **Work rows out again**. Rows that can now be placed are posted as fuel purchases without fetching the statement again; any still waiting stay held.

pages.notes: This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to fuel purchase imports. Runs are started by the schedule or **Sync now**, so there is no create button. Rows a run posts appear on [Fuel purchases](/fuel/purchases).

pages.name: IFTA returns
pages.description: The quarterly fuel tax worksheet: every jurisdiction's miles and tax-paid gallons, the fleet MPG they are taxed through, and what the quarter owes or is owed. Draft figures move with the data until the return is finalized.
pages.summary:
IFTA returns is the quarterly fuel tax worksheet. For each quarter it lists every jurisdiction's miles and tax-paid gallons, works out the fleet MPG they are taxed through, and totals what the quarter owes or is owed. Miles come from completed shipment moves plus the manual entries on [Jurisdiction mileage](/fuel/jurisdiction-mileage); gallons come from [Fuel purchases](/fuel/purchases); rates come from [IFTA tax rates](/fuel/configuration-files/ifta-tax-rates).

Fuel tax and compliance staff use it to generate the return, check it, lock it, record that it was filed and amend it later. The page shows the **Total miles**, **Tax-paid gallons**, **Fleet MPG** and **Status**, then the **Jurisdiction lines** with each line's **Taxable miles**, **Net taxable gal**, **Rate**, **Tax due**, **Surcharge** and **Line total**, and a section on **What the figures leave out**.

tasks.title: Generate a quarter's return
steps: Open [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns). It opens on the most recently completed quarter.
Pick the **Year** and **Quarter** at the top of the page.
If the quarter shows **Not generated**, select **Generate the return**.

tasks.title: Bring a draft return up to date
steps: Open [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) and pick the quarter.
Select **Recompute** to rebuild every line from the miles, fuel and rates on file now. Do this after adding or deleting fuel purchases or manual miles.
Check **What the figures leave out** for moves with no tractor, mileage mismatches and moves that were never broken down by jurisdiction.
A line marked **No rate** is missing its jurisdiction's tax rate; select **Add rate** to enter it on [IFTA tax rates](/fuel/configuration-files/ifta-tax-rates), then recompute.

tasks.title: Finalize and file the return
steps: Open [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) and pick the quarter.
Select **Finalize…**, then **Finalize return**. This recomputes and locks the worksheet.
Select **Export CSV** to download every line, each fuel type's subtotal and the grand total.
After filing with your base jurisdiction, select **Mark filed…**, enter the **Filed on** date and optional **Filing reference**, then select **Mark filed**.

tasks.title: Reopen or amend a return
steps: Open [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) and pick the quarter.
For a finalized return that has not been filed, select **Reopen…**, enter a **Reason** and select **Reopen return**.
For a filed return, select **Amend…**, enter a **Reason** and select **Open the amendment**.

tasks.title: Delete a draft return
steps: Open [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) and pick the quarter.
Select **Delete draft…**, then **Delete draft**. Only a draft can be deleted.

pages.notes:
This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to IFTA returns. Each action needs its own permission: generating or amending needs create, **Recompute** needs update, finalizing needs approve, reopening needs reopen, marking filed needs submit, **Export CSV** needs export and deleting needs delete.

Draft figures move with the data until the return is finalized. A return cannot be finalized while any member line is missing a rate. Reopening a finalized return requires a reason, which is audited.

When some moves were never broken down by jurisdiction, people with permission to manage IFTA returns can select **Backfill jurisdiction miles…** under **What the figures leave out** to re-route those moves. Jurisdiction miles are only captured while **Capture jurisdiction miles** is on in [Distance controls](/admin/distance-controls).

pages.name: Jurisdiction mileage
pages.description: Miles by state or province that dispatch did not compute — deadhead, yard moves, and units without telematics. They are added to the miles the quarter's IFTA return works out from shipment moves.
pages.summary:
Jurisdiction mileage holds miles by state or province that dispatch did not compute: deadhead, bobtailing to a shop, yard moves, repositioning between customers, and units without telematics. Routed miles from completed shipment moves are captured automatically; the manual miles entered here are added to them on the quarter's IFTA return at its next recompute.

Fuel tax and compliance staff use it. The table shows **Travelled**, **Tractor**, **Jurisdiction**, **Miles**, **Loaded**, **Source** and **Notes**. Rows written by the distance provider or telematics also appear here, read-only.

tasks.title: Add miles the system did not see
steps: Open [Jurisdiction mileage](/fuel/jurisdiction-mileage).
Select **New jurisdiction mileage**.
Under **Where and when**, pick the **Tractor** and **Jurisdiction**, and set **Travelled on** (the day the miles were run, which fixes the quarter; it cannot be in the future).
Enter the **Miles** and turn on **Under load** if the tractor was loaded.
Add **Notes** explaining why these miles exist, so an auditor can see the reason, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Correct a move's routed miles
steps: Open [Jurisdiction mileage](/fuel/jurisdiction-mileage) and select the system-written row to see which move it came from.
System rows are read-only. Add a manual entry for the same move instead; it replaces those rows on the return.

tasks.title: Change or delete a manual entry
steps: Open [Jurisdiction mileage](/fuel/jurisdiction-mileage).
Select the entry's row, change it and select **Save**.
To delete it, right-click the row, choose **Delete**, then **Delete entry**.

pages.notes:
This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to jurisdiction mileage, and **Delete** needs permission to delete it.

Manual miles are never subtracted from routed miles, so do not enter miles a move already carries unless the entry names that move. After adding, changing or deleting miles, recompute the quarter on [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) to bring the figures up to date.

pages.name: Fuel purchases
pages.description: Every gallon bought for a tractor, keyed by hand or imported from a fuel card statement. Tax-paid gallons credit the jurisdiction they were bought in on the quarterly IFTA return.
pages.summary:
Fuel purchases lists every gallon bought for a tractor, whether keyed in by hand from a receipt or imported from a fuel card statement (Comdata, EFS or WEX). Tax-paid gallons credit the jurisdiction they were bought in on the quarterly IFTA return, so this is the fuel side of [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns).

Fleet, fuel and compliance staff use it. The table shows **Purchased**, **Tractor**, **Worker**, **Jurisdiction**, **Vendor**, **Fuel**, **Gallons**, **Amount**, **Tax**, **Source**, **Reference** and **Updated**.

tasks.title: Record a fuel purchase from a receipt
steps: Open [Fuel purchases](/fuel/purchases).
Select **New fuel purchase** (then **New fuel purchase** again if a menu opens).

Under **Unit, driver & place**, pick the **Tractor**, optionally the **Driver** (filled from the tractor's primary driver when left empty), the **Purchased at** date and time, the **Jurisdiction**, and the **Vendor** and **City**.
Under **Fuel**, choose the **Fuel type** and **Unit**, and enter the **Quantity**, **Total paid**, **Currency** and **Odometer**.
Under **Card & tax**, pick the **Fuel card** (or enter the card's last four digits), the **Transaction reference**, and whether **Fuel tax paid at the pump** applies. Add any **Notes**.
Select **Save**. Attach the receipt on the purchase's **Documents** tab.

tasks.title: Import a fuel card statement
steps: Open [Fuel purchases](/fuel/purchases).
Select **New fuel purchase** and choose **Import card statement**.
Pick the **Provider**, and optionally a **Default card**, **Default fuel type** and **Currency**, then upload the statement. Use **Download template** if you are unsure of the layout.
Review the rows: new rows, **Duplicates in file**, rows **Already on file** and **Errors**. Nothing is recorded until you confirm.
Confirm the import, or select **Discard** to drop it.

tasks.title: Correct or delete a purchase
steps: Open [Fuel purchases](/fuel/purchases).
Select the purchase's row to change it and select **Save**.
To delete it, right-click the row, choose **Delete**, then **Delete purchase**.

tasks.title: Find purchases
steps: Open [Fuel purchases](/fuel/purchases).
Type in the search box, or use **Filter** in the table toolbar, for example on **Purchased** date, **Jurisdiction** or **Fuel**.

pages.notes:
This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to fuel purchases; importing statements needs permission to create fuel purchase imports, and **Delete** needs permission to delete fuel purchases.

DEF, reefer and other non-IFTA products are tracked as spend only. Litres are converted to US gallons for the return. After deleting a purchase, recompute the quarter's return on [IFTA returns](/fuel/ifta-returns) to take it out of the figures; importing the same statement again records the row afresh.

pages.name: Unassigned cards
pages.description: Cards a connected fuel card feed saw a transaction on before anybody had registered them. Until a card is tied to a tractor or driver, its purchases can only be matched by the unit number on the receipt.
pages.summary:
Unassigned cards lists the fuel cards a connected fuel card feed saw a transaction on before anybody had registered them. Until such a card is tied to a tractor or driver, its purchases can only be matched by the unit number on the receipt, and rows that cannot be matched wait on [Feed runs](/fuel/feed-runs).

Fuel and fleet staff work this list down by assigning each card. It shows the same columns as [Fuel cards](/fuel/configuration-files/fuel-cards): **Status**, **Label**, **Provider**, **Card**, **Worker**, **Tractor**, **Expires** and **Updated**. There is no create button here; cards appear on their own.

tasks.title: Assign a card the feed found
steps: Open [Unassigned cards](/fuel/unassigned-cards).
Right-click the card's row and choose **Assign card**.
Pick the **Tractor**, the **Driver**, or both, and select **Assign**. The card leaves this list and its purchases start matching on their own.

tasks.title: Fill in a card's details
steps: Open [Unassigned cards](/fuel/unassigned-cards) and select the card's row.
Give it a **Label**, check the **Provider** and **Last four digits**, set the **Driver** and **Tractor** under **Assignment**, and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Cancel a card you don't recognise
steps: Open [Unassigned cards](/fuel/unassigned-cards).
Right-click the card's row and choose **Cancel card**, enter a **Reason** and select **Cancel card**.

pages.notes: This page is only available when your organization runs its own trucks (asset operations). Viewing it needs read access to fuel cards; assigning and cancelling need permission to update them.

pages.name: Benefits
pages.description: What the carrier offers and who is on it. An employee contribution is taken through an ordinary settlement deduction, so it caps, pauses and reverses exactly like every other one.
pages.summary:
Benefits lists the plans the company offers for each plan year, grouped by type (medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability, retirement and other), and who is on each one. Each plan shows how many people it covers and how many declined, and what the **Employee** and **Employer** pay per settlement period. Figures at the top give **People covered**, **Plans on offer**, **Employer puts in** and **Off settlements** (the employees' share, taken from their settlements). The side panels list cover **Starting soon**, **Ending soon** and **Recently declined**.

HR and benefits administrators use it to set up and reprice plans. An employee's contribution is taken through an ordinary settlement deduction.

tasks.title: Add a benefit plan
steps: Open [Benefits](/hr/benefits).
Select **Add a plan**.
Fill in **Code**, **Name**, **Type**, **Plan year** and **Pay code** (the pay code the contribution is recorded under on settlements), and set **Status**.
Enter the **Employee cost per period** and **Employer cost per period**, and optionally the **Carrier**, **Policy number**, **Waiting period (days)** and **Description**.
Select **Add**.

tasks.title: Change or archive a plan
steps: Open [Benefits](/hr/benefits) and pick the plan year if there is more than one.
Select the pencil button on the plan.
Change the fields, or set **Status** to **Archived** to stop offering it, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: See who is on a plan
steps: Open [Benefits](/hr/benefits).
Select **Who is on it** on the plan.
Search the list by name or terminal.

tasks.title: Enroll a worker or record that they declined
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers), select the worker and go to the **Pay** tab.
Under **Benefits**, select **Enroll or decline**.
Pick the **Plan**, the **Coverage** tier and **Effective from** date. Turn on **They declined the cover** to record a waiver instead, with the reason in **Why**.
Select **Enroll** (or **Record** for a waiver).
To stop someone's cover later, select **End cover** beside the plan on the same tab.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to benefit plans. Adding a plan needs create access, editing needs update access, and enrolling workers needs permission to assign benefit plans. - Each plan year is priced separately, so repricing next year's plan never changes what someone was charged this year. To offer a plan in a new year, add a plan for that year. - Ending a worker's cover stops their contribution; the record of the cover stays.

pages.name: Checklist templates
pages.description: Onboarding and offboarding checklists that start automatically from a hire, rehire or termination — with who owns each step and when it is due.
pages.summary: Checklist templates define the onboarding, offboarding and custom checklists run for workers. Each template says which employment event starts it (when hired, rehired or terminated, or started by hand), and lists the items to get done, with the team that owns each one and how many days after the start it is due. HR administrators maintain the templates; the checklists themselves are worked on each worker's **Checklist** tab.

tasks.title: Create a checklist template
steps: Open [Checklist templates](/hr/checklist-templates).
Select **New checklist template**.
Under **General**, fill in **Code**, **Name**, **Kind**, **Starts** and **Status**, and optionally a **Description**.
Turn on **Default for this trigger** if this checklist should start automatically when the matching employment event is recorded.

Under **Items**, select **Add item** for each step and fill in its **Label**, **Kind**, **Owner**, **Due** (days after start) and **Required**. A document or credential item also asks for the **Document type** or **Credential type** that completes it.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit a checklist template
steps: Open [Checklist templates](/hr/checklist-templates).
Select the template's row.
Change the fields or items and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Deactivate or restore templates
steps: Open [Checklist templates](/hr/checklist-templates).
Tick the templates, then choose **Deactivate** or **Restore** in the bar at the bottom of the table. You can also right-click a single template.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to checklist templates and the asset operations feature. Creating and editing need create and update access; **Deactivate** and **Restore** only appear for people allowed to archive and restore templates. - Items are copied when a checklist starts, so editing a template does not change checklists already running. - A template needs at least one item. A template started by hand cannot be the default; it is started from the worker's **Checklist** tab. - Document and credential items complete themselves once the matching document or valid credential is on file.

pages.name: Credential types
pages.description: The licences, cards, endorsements and certificates workers can hold — which are required, for whom, and how far ahead renewals are flagged.
pages.summary: Credential types is the list of licences, cards, endorsements and certificates workers can hold, such as a CDL, a medical card or a TWIC card. Each type says whether it is required and for which driver types, how far ahead of expiry it is flagged, its typical validity, and whether a number or a scanned document is needed. HR and safety administrators maintain the list; the credentials themselves are recorded on each worker's **Credentials** tab.

tasks.title: Add a credential type
steps: Open [Credential types](/hr/credential-types).
Select **New credential type**.
Under **General**, fill in **Code**, **Name**, **Category** and **Status**, and optionally a **Description**.
Under **Compliance**, turn on **Required** if workers must hold it to be compliant, pick the **Required for driver types**, and set the **Renewal alert window** and **Typical validity**.
Turn on **Requires a number** or **Requires a document** if the credential cannot be saved without a number or verified without a scan.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit a credential type
steps: Open [Credential types](/hr/credential-types).
Select the type's row, change the fields, and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Deactivate or restore credential types
steps: Open [Credential types](/hr/credential-types).
Tick the types, then choose **Deactivate** or **Restore** in the bar at the bottom of the table. You can also right-click a single type.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to credential types and the asset operations feature. **Deactivate** and **Restore** only appear for people allowed to archive and restore types. - Required types appear on every matching worker; a missing or expired one makes the worker non-compliant. Leave every **Required for driver types** box unchecked to require it for every worker. - A worker holds one active credential of each type; renewing replaces the earlier one. - System types ship with Trenova and their code cannot be changed. Types that mirror a worker-profile field cannot be deactivated.

pages.name: Fleet safety
pages.description: The fleet read the way a safety director thinks: the seven CSA BASICs, the trend behind them, and which terminals and drivers are carrying the weight.
pages.summary:
Fleet safety reads the fleet the way a safety director does. The **Fleet** tab shows **Drivers** by rating, **Average score**, **Events in window** and **Out of service** orders, then the seven **CSA BASICs** with their weighted scores, **Events by month** with the trend, a breakdown **By terminal**, and two driver lists: **Needs attention** (most active points first) and **Best records**. The **My DOT** tab shows your own carrier's DOT profile as pulled from a connected carrier intelligence provider.

Safety managers use the page to see where risk sits and which terminals and drivers to work with. The figures are built from the safety events recorded on each worker.

tasks.title: Review fleet safety
steps: Open [Fleet safety](/hr/fleet-safety) on the **Fleet** tab.
Choose the counting window: **3 months**, **6 months**, **12 months** or **24 months**.
Read the **CSA BASICs** card (select **How the score is made** for the method) and the **Events by month** trend.

tasks.title: Narrow to one terminal
steps: Open [Fleet safety](/hr/fleet-safety).
Select a terminal under **By terminal**. The whole page narrows to it.
Select the terminal chip beside the window selector to go back to every terminal.

tasks.title: Look at a driver's safety record
steps: Open [Fleet safety](/hr/fleet-safety).
Select a driver under **Needs attention** or **Best records**. Their worker record opens on the safety tab.

tasks.title: Check or refresh your DOT profile
steps: Open [Fleet safety](/hr/fleet-safety) and select the **My DOT** tab.
Select **Refresh** to pull a new copy, or **Pull profile** if it has never been pulled.

If the tab says **Your organization has no DOT number**, select **Open organization settings** and add it. If **No carrier intelligence provider is connected**, select **Open integrations** to connect one.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations). The **Fleet** tab needs read access to worker safety events; the **My DOT** tab needs read access to carrier intelligence, and refreshing needs update access. - Points roll off two years after the event.

pages.name: Holiday calendar
pages.description: Company holidays PTO policies skip when counting days, and blackout dates no one can request off.
pages.summary: The holiday calendar shows the year month by month with your company holidays and blackout dates marked, and lists every date below the calendar. HR administrators keep it up to date. Holidays are not charged against a time-off request under a PTO policy that skips weekends; blackout dates cannot be requested off at all.

tasks.title: Add a holiday or blackout date
steps: Open [Holiday calendar](/hr/holidays).
Select **Add date**, or select an empty day on the calendar to start with that date filled in.
Fill in **Name** and **Date**, and choose the **Kind**: a holiday, or a blackout that no one can request off.
Turn on **Repeats every year** for dates that recur annually, and optionally add a **Note**.
Select **Add date**.

tasks.title: Change or remove a date
steps: Open [Holiday calendar](/hr/holidays).
Select the marked day on the calendar, or the edit button beside the date in the list below.
Change the fields and select **Save changes**.
To delete it, select the remove button beside the date in the list, then **Remove** to confirm, or **Keep** to leave it.

tasks.title: Look at another year
steps: Open [Holiday calendar](/hr/holidays).
Use the arrows beside the year to step back or forward, or **This year** to come back.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to the holiday calendar and the asset operations feature. Adding, editing and removing dates each need their own create, update and delete access. - A time-off request that crosses a blackout is refused. A policy that charges every calendar day charges holidays too; only policies that skip weekends leave holidays out of the count. - Removing a blackout lets workers request that date off again.

pages.name: Leave settings
pages.description: How family and medical leave is measured, and what an employee must do to qualify
pages.summary: Leave settings is where HR sets how family and medical leave (FMLA) is measured for the whole organization: which twelve-month period entitlements are counted against, how many weeks of leave an eligible employee gets, how long a week is in hours, and what an employee needs to qualify. The leave cases themselves are opened and tracked on each worker's **Leave** tab.

tasks.title: Choose how the leave year is measured
steps: Open [Leave settings](/hr/leave-settings).

Under **The twelve-month period**, pick **How the year is measured**: calendar year, twelve months from the hire anniversary, twelve months forward from first use, or rolling twelve months looking back.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set the leave entitlement
steps: Open [Leave settings](/hr/leave-settings).
Under **What the entitlement is worth**, set **Weeks of leave**, **Military caregiver weeks** and **Hours in a workweek**.
Select **Save changes**.

tasks.title: Set eligibility and certification rules
steps: Open [Leave settings](/hr/leave-settings).
Under **Eligibility and certification**, set **Months of service**, **Hours worked in the prior year** and **Days to return a certification**.
Select **Save changes**.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to worker leave and the asset operations feature. - The measurement method must be applied to every employee alike. Changing it is a change of policy: employees are entitled to sixty days' notice, and until then whichever method gives the greater benefit applies. - Months of service is checked against the hire date. Hours worked cannot be counted automatically, so they are recorded by hand on each leave case. - The statute's twelve weeks is a floor; you can set a more generous figure.

pages.name: My team
pages.description: Everyone you answer for: your own reports, the terminals you run, and anybody whose approvals have been handed to you.
pages.summary: My team is a manager's view of everyone they answer for: their own direct reports, the people at the terminals they run, and anyone whose approvals have been handed to them. It shows how many are in good standing (compliant, trained and rated Good or better), who needs attention, average tenure, upcoming work anniversaries, a count by terminal, and any approval cover you currently hold.

tasks.title: See who needs attention
steps: Open [My team](/hr/my-team).
Check **Needs your attention** for the people with problems, or select **Needs attention** above the **Roster** to show only them.
Select a person to open their worker record.

tasks.title: Find someone on your team
steps: Open [My team](/hr/my-team).
Type a name, title or terminal in the search box above the **Roster**.
Use **Everyone**, **Direct**, **Terminal** or **Covering** to narrow the list by how the person reaches you, and **Clear filters** to start again.
Turn on **Include people who have left** to see former team members too.

tasks.title: Check whose approvals you are covering
steps: Open [My team](/hr/my-team).
Look at **Approval cover** for the managers whose approvals are in your hands and until when.
Select **Manage** to go to [Org structure](/hr/org-structure) and change delegations.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to workers and the asset operations feature. **Approval cover** only shows for people who can read approval delegations. - A delegation never widens what you could approve on your own. - If nobody reports to you, the page says **Nobody reports to you yet**.

pages.name: Org structure
pages.description: The shape of the organisation: the positions the roster is counted by, the headcount in each, and who is approving in whose place.
pages.summary:
Org structure shows the shape of the organization: the job positions the roster is counted by, how they report to each other, how many people hold each, and who is approving in whose place. Figures at the top give **People**, **Positions**, **Terminals** and **Cover in force**. The **Org chart** lists positions as a tree with each one's headcount; the side panels break the roster down **By terminal** and **By department** and list **Titles nobody holds yet**.

**Approval cover** lists approval delegations you have handed out or are covering for. HR and managers use the page to set up positions, place people in them, and arrange cover while they are away.

tasks.title: Add a position
steps: Open [Org structure](/hr/org-structure).
Select **Add a position**, or the add button on a position's row to add one reporting to it.
Fill in **Code**, **Title**, **Department** and **Status**, and pick who it **Reports to**.
Turn on **Driving position** or **Exempt from overtime** where they apply, and add a **Description** if useful.
Select **Add**.

tasks.title: Edit or move a position
steps: Open [Org structure](/hr/org-structure).
Open the menu on the position's row and choose **Edit**, change the fields, and select **Save**. Set **Status** to **Archived** to retire it; this is refused while anybody still holds it.
To change its reporting line, choose a position under **Move under** in the same menu, or **Nothing (top level)**. You can also drag the position onto another one.

tasks.title: Put people in a position
steps: Open [Org structure](/hr/org-structure).
Select the position's headcount, or choose **Who holds it** from its menu.
Find the worker (or, for office positions, the user) and select **Add**.
To take someone off the position, use the remove button beside their name.

tasks.title: Hand your approvals to a colleague
steps: Open [Org structure](/hr/org-structure) and find **Approval cover**.
Select **Arrange cover**.
Pick **Who is covering** and **What they can approve**, set **From** and **Until**, and give the reason in **Why**.
Select **Arrange**. To end it early, select **Call back** beside the cover.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to job positions. Adding positions needs create access; editing, moving and changing who holds a position need update access. **Approval cover** needs read access to approval delegations, and arranging cover needs create access. - A delegation that is called back stays on the list so approvals made under it can still be explained.

pages.name: OSHA 300 log
pages.description: Recordable injuries and illnesses for the year, and the 300A summary posted over them. The totals are counted from the log every time it is read, so a case corrected years later cannot leave a stale summary behind.
pages.summary:
The OSHA 300 log lists the recordable work-related injuries and illnesses for a year (Form 300) and the year's 300A summary. Figures at the top give **Recordable cases**, the **Incident rate**, the **DART rate** and **Days lost**. The case table shows each case's **Case** number, **Employee**, **Date**, **Where it happened**, **What happened**, log **Column**, days **Away** and **Restricted**, **Type** and **Status**. Privacy cases have the name withheld from the posted log.

The totals are counted from the log every time it is read, so correcting a case later never leaves an out-of-date summary. Safety and HR staff use the page to keep the log and to prepare, certify and post the 300A.

tasks.title: Record a new injury or illness
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers), select the worker and go to the **Safety** tab.
Under **Injuries & illnesses**, select **Record a case**.

Fill in the dates, **What happened**, **Where**, **Body part**, the **Injury or illness** type, **Treatment given**, days away or restricted, and the **OSHA classification**, then save. A recordable case appears on this log for the year it happened.

tasks.title: Find and review a case
steps: Open [OSHA 300 log](/hr/osha-log) and pick the year.
Filter the cases or search by name, injury or place.
Open the row's actions menu and choose **Open case** to see the full case, including any workers' compensation claim, or **Open worker** to go to the worker's safety tab.

tasks.title: Correct or delete a case
steps: Open [OSHA 300 log](/hr/osha-log) and find the case.
From the row's actions menu choose **Edit case**, change the details and save.
Or choose **Delete case** and confirm with **Delete case**. The case number is not reused.

tasks.title: Prepare and certify the 300A summary
steps: Open [OSHA 300 log](/hr/osha-log) and pick the year.

On the summary card, select **Start the summary** (or **Edit figures**) and fill in **Annual average employees**, **Total hours worked**, **NAICS code**, the **Certifying executive** with their **Title** and **Phone**, and, once filed, **Electronically submitted** and the **Submission reference**. Select **Save**.
Select **Certify**. Post the summary where employees can read it, from February 1 to April 30.
To correct a certified summary, select **Reopen**.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to worker injuries. Editing cases and the summary figures needs update access, deleting needs delete access, and certifying or reopening needs manage access. - **Certify** stays unavailable while something the summary needs is missing; the card says what. - The incident and DART rates need the hours worked from the 300A figures.

pages.name: Policies
pages.description: Handbooks and policies people sign from Dash. A signature records the version it was given for, so revising the words means giving them a new version — and everybody bound by it goes back to outstanding.
pages.summary:
Policies holds the handbooks and policies drivers and employees must read, and usually sign, from Dash, the driver app. Each policy card shows its title, version, who it applies to (everyone, employees or owner-operators), whether it needs a signature or is read only, and whether it is retired. Figures at the top count policies **In force**, those that **Need a signature**, and those **Retired**.

HR and safety managers publish policies here and check who still has to sign. A signature is tied to the version it was given for, so publishing a new version asks everyone it applies to to read and sign again.

tasks.title: Publish a policy
steps: Open [Policies](/hr/policies).
Select **Publish a policy**.
Fill in **Code**, **Title** and an optional **One-line summary**.
Under **The text**, choose **Write it here** and type the **Policy text**, or **Attach a document** and drop in a PDF or image.
Under **Who and when**, set the **Version**, **Applies to**, **Effective from** and **Status**, and turn on **Needs a signature** if people must sign it rather than just read it.
Select **Publish**. Everyone it applies to is asked to read (and sign) it from Dash.

tasks.title: See who has signed a policy
steps: Open [Policies](/hr/policies).
Select **Who has signed** on the policy card.
Switch between **Outstanding**, **Signed** and **Everyone**, or find a person by name.

tasks.title: Revise a policy
steps: Open [Policies](/hr/policies).
Hover over the policy card and select **Edit**.
To fix wording without asking for new signatures, change the text and keep the same **Version**. To make everyone sign again, give it a new **Version**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Retire a policy
steps: Open [Policies](/hr/policies), hover over the card and select **Edit**.
Set **Status** to **Retired** and select **Save**.
Use **Everything** at the top of the list to see retired policies alongside those **In force**.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to worker policies. Publishing needs create access; editing needs update access. - Retired policies are kept so older signatures still point at the policy they were given for.

pages.name: PTO policies
pages.description: Accrual rules for paid time off — how days are earned, capped, and carried over, and which drivers each policy governs.
pages.summary:
PTO policies set how paid time off is earned and tracked. Each policy has one accrual rule per PTO type, saying how days are earned, the most a worker can hold, how much carries over into the new year and what happens when employment ends. It also sets whether requests need approval and whether balances are enforced. The table shows **Status**, **Code**, **Name**, **Year**, **Tracked types**, **Workers** on the policy and when it was **Updated**.

HR administrators maintain the policies and then assign each worker to one.

tasks.title: Add a PTO policy
steps: Open [PTO policies](/hr/pto-policies).
Select **New PTO policy**.
Under **General**, fill in **Code**, **Name** and **Status**. Turn on **Default for new hires** to enrol new workers in it from their hire date.
Under **Year & counting**, set the **Policy year**, **Waiting period** and whether to **Count weekends**.

Under **Accrual rules**, set each rule's **PTO type**, **Accrual** method and amount, **Max balance**, **Carryover cap**, **Carryover expires** and **When employment ends**. Select **Add type** for another PTO type, and **Add tier** to give longer-serving workers more.
Under **Enforcement**, choose **Requires approval**, **Enforce balance** and **Allow negative balance** (with a **Negative floor**).
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a PTO policy
steps: Open [PTO policies](/hr/pto-policies) and select the policy's row.
Change the fields and select **Save**. Rule changes apply going forward: days already in a worker's ledger are not recalculated.

tasks.title: Assign a policy to a worker
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers), select the worker and go to the **Time off** tab.
Select **Assign policy** (or **Change policy**).
Pick the **Policy** and the **Effective from** date, and confirm. Accruals start from that date on the next nightly run.

tasks.title: Archive or restore a policy
steps: Open [PTO policies](/hr/pto-policies).
Right-click the policy and choose **Archive**, or **Restore** on an archived one. To do several at once, tick them and use **Archive** or **Restore** in the bar that appears.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to PTO policies. Adding needs create access and editing needs update access; archiving and restoring each need their own permission. - A policy that still has workers on it cannot be archived. - PTO types without a rule can still be requested but are not tracked against a balance. With **Requires approval** off, requests are approved and booked immediately; with **Enforce balance** off, balances are informational and never block a request.

pages.name: Random testing
pages.description: The pools drivers are drawn from and the rounds drawn from them. Each round keeps the seed it was drawn with, so a selection can be re-checked years later.
pages.summary:
Random testing runs the company's DOT random drug and alcohol testing programme. **Pools** lists the groups of drivers selections are drawn from, with each pool's draw period, rounds drawn this year and a warning when it is **Below the DOT minimum**. **Rounds** lists every draw with its **Round**, **Pool**, **Status**, how many were picked for **Drug** and **Alcohol** against the target, how many were **In the hat**, and when it was **Drawn**. Figures at the top show **Owed now**, **Rounds this year**, **Selected this year** and **In the hat**.

Each round keeps the seed it was drawn with, so a selection can be re-checked years later. Safety and compliance staff use the page to run draws on schedule and track who has been tested.

tasks.title: Set up a testing pool
steps: Open [Random testing](/hr/random-testing).
Select **New pool** in the **Pools** panel.
Fill in **Code**, **Name**, an optional **Description**, **Status**, how often to **Draw every**, the **Drug rate (% a year)** and **Alcohol rate (% a year)**.
Tick the **Driver types** to include, or leave them all clear to include every safety-sensitive driver. Turn on **Default pool** if it should be the main one.
Select **Create**. To change it later, select **Edit** on the pool.

tasks.title: Run a random draw
steps: Open [Random testing](/hr/random-testing).
On the pool, select the draw button. It reads **Run draw**, or names the period that is owed.
The new round opens as a draft showing who was selected for drug and alcohol testing.

tasks.title: Finalise or void a round
steps: Open [Random testing](/hr/random-testing) and find the draft round under **Rounds**.
Select **Finalise** and confirm to make the names the record for that period, or **Void** and **Void the round** to discard the selection so the period can be drawn again.

tasks.title: Track the selected drivers
steps: Open [Random testing](/hr/random-testing) and select **Open** on the round.
For each selected driver, select **Mark notified** once told, or **Excuse** or **Missed** as appropriate.
To see only one pool's rounds, select **Rounds** on the pool; filter by status with **All**, **Draft**, **Final** or **Voided**.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to DOT random pools. Creating pools needs create access, editing needs update access, and drawing, finalising, voiding and updating selections need manage access. - Once a round is final, correcting a name means voiding the whole round. A voided round stays on file with its seed so the audit trail shows it happened.

pages.name: Review templates
pages.description: What a performance review rates and how much each item counts. Items are copied onto every review, so editing a template never rewrites history.
pages.summary: Review templates define what a performance review rates and how much each item counts toward the overall score. HR administrators set them up; managers pick a template when they start a review from a worker's **Reviews** tab. A template can repeat on a schedule, so closing a review schedules the next one.

tasks.title: Create a review template
steps: Open [Review templates](/hr/review-templates).
Select **New review template**.
Under **General**, fill in **Code**, **Name** and **Status**, and optionally **Repeat every** (in months), **Default template** and a **Description**.
Under **Rating items**, select **Add item** for each thing to score and fill in its **Key**, **Label**, **Weight** and optional **Hint**.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit a review template
steps: Open [Review templates](/hr/review-templates).
Select the template's row, change the fields or rating items, and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Deactivate or restore templates
steps: Open [Review templates](/hr/review-templates).
Tick the templates, then choose **Deactivate** or **Restore** in the bar at the bottom of the table. You can also right-click a single template.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to performance review templates and the asset operations feature. **Deactivate** and **Restore** only appear for people allowed to archive and restore templates. - Rating items are copied onto every review when it starts. Changing a template only affects reviews started after you save; reviews in progress keep their items and weights. - Only active templates with no open reviews can be deactivated. - The overall score is the weighted average of the items, using each item's **Weight**. Leave **Repeat every** empty for one-off reviews.

pages.name: Scheduling
pages.description: Who is expected on which days. The board is composed on every read from the pattern, approved time off, open leave and the work dispatch has already assigned — so it cannot go stale.
pages.summary:
Scheduling shows who is expected to work on which days. The **Rota** board has a row per worker and a cell per day, built fresh every time from their shift pattern, approved time off, open leave and the loads dispatch has already assigned, so it never goes stale. Figures at the top show **On the board**, **Cover today**, **Conflicts** (people rostered on a day they cannot work) and **Swaps waiting on you**, and **Needs a look** lists the rows that need attention.

The **Shifts** tab holds the shift patterns (days, start time, length and rotation), and the **Swaps** tab holds shift swaps drivers have asked for. Operations managers and HR use the page to plan cover and settle swaps.

tasks.title: Check who is working
steps: Open [Scheduling](/hr/scheduling) on the **Rota** tab.
Use the arrows or **Today** to move between weeks, and choose **Week**, **2 weeks** or **4 weeks** to see more at once.
Search by name, shift or terminal, pick a fleet (**All fleets** by default), or turn on **My team** to see only the people you answer for.
Point at a day to see details such as loads already assigned.

tasks.title: Add or change a shift pattern
steps: Open [Scheduling](/hr/scheduling) and select the **Shifts** tab.
Select **Add a shift**, or **Edit** on an existing shift.
