Fill in **Code** and **Name**, tick the **Working days**, and set **Starts at**, **Length (hours)** and **Rotation (weeks)**. Optionally set a **Colour** and **Description**.
Select **Add shift** (or **Save**). Set **Status** to **Retired** to stop using a shift.

tasks.title: Put a worker on a shift
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers), select the worker and go to the **Schedule** tab.
Select **Put on a shift** (or **Move to another shift**).
Pick the **Shift**, the **Effective from** date and, for rotating shifts, the **Rotation offset (weeks)**; add **Notes** if useful.
Select **Assign**. Their row appears on the board.

tasks.title: Approve or reject a shift swap
steps: Open [Scheduling](/hr/scheduling) and select the **Swaps** tab.
Keep **Waiting** selected to see swaps that need a decision, or choose **Everything**.
On a swap the colleague has accepted, select **Approve** or **Reject**. Swaps still **Waiting on the colleague** cannot be decided yet.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to worker schedules. The **Shifts** and **Swaps** tabs need read access to shift templates and shift swaps; adding, editing, approving and rejecting each need their own access. - The board cannot be edited directly: change a worker's shift, time off or leave and the board follows.

pages.name: Time & attendance
pages.description: Hours worked by staff paid by the clock. A week's totals are frozen when it is handed over, so what a manager approves is what payroll is run from.
pages.summary:
Time & attendance records the hours of staff paid by the clock. People clock in and out, each week's punches build a timesheet, and a manager approves the week before payroll runs from it. Once a week is handed over its totals are frozen, so what the manager approves is exactly what payroll is paid from. Figures at the top show **Awaiting approval**, **On the clock now**, **This week so far** and, for people who run payroll, **Approved, not paid**.

The page has three tabs: **Clock** (punching in and out and correcting entries), **Timesheets** (the approval queue) and **Payroll** (sending approved weeks to payroll). Supervisors, HR and payroll staff use it.

tasks.title: Clock a worker in or out
steps: Open [Time & attendance](/hr/time-attendance) on the **Clock** tab.
Pick the **Worker**. Their card shows whether they are on the clock and their hours this week.
Select **Clock in** or **Clock out**.
Anyone still punched in is listed under **On the clock now**; select **Clock out** beside a name to punch them out from there. Turn on **My team** to list only your own team.

tasks.title: Record or correct hours by hand
steps: Open [Time & attendance](/hr/time-attendance) on the **Clock** tab and pick the **Worker**.
Select **Record hours**, or the edit button beside an entry under **Last two weeks** to correct it.
Set **Started**, **Finished** and any **Unpaid break (minutes)**, give the reason, and add a **Note** if useful.
Select **Record** (or **Save correction**). To delete a wrong punch, use the remove button beside it, give the reason in **Why** and select **Remove**.

tasks.title: Approve or send back a week
steps: Open [Time & attendance](/hr/time-attendance) and select the **Timesheets** tab.
Choose **Awaiting approval**, **Open**, **Approved** or **Paid**, and optionally pick a worker or turn on **My team**.
On a handed-over week, select **Approve**, or **Send back** to return it for another look.
On an open week, select **Hand over** to submit it for approval.

tasks.title: Run payroll from approved weeks
steps: Open [Time & attendance](/hr/time-attendance) and select the **Payroll** tab.
Under **Run payroll**, choose the period length (**Weekly**, **Fortnightly** or **Four weeks**) and step to the right period with the arrows.
Select the run button, which reads **Nothing to run** when no approved weeks are waiting. The weeks in the run lock to it, so the same period cannot be sent twice.
Under **Runs**, select **CSV** to download a run's file, or **Void** and then **Void run** to undo it; its weeks go back to approved.

pages.notes: - The page appears only for organizations that run their own assets (asset operations) and needs read access to timesheets. Clocking in and out needs create access; recording, correcting and removing hours needs update access; approving, handing over and the **Payroll** tab each need their own timesheet permission. - Every hand-entered or corrected entry keeps its reason, which shows on the timesheet.

pages.name: Training courses
pages.description: The courses workers can be put through — which are required for each driver type, how they are delivered, what passes, and how long a completion stays valid.
pages.summary: Training courses is the catalog of courses workers can be put through. Each course records how it is delivered and what passes, whether it is required and for which driver types, how long a worker has to finish it, and how long a completion stays valid before a renewal is assigned. Safety and HR administrators maintain the catalog; courses are assigned and completed on each worker's **Training** tab.

tasks.title: Add a training course
steps: Open [Training courses](/hr/training-courses).
Select **New training course**.
Under **General**, fill in **Code**, **Name**, **Category** and **Status**, and optionally a **Description**.
Under **Delivery**, choose the **Delivery** method and set **Duration**, **Link**, **Passing score** and **Driver acknowledges** as needed.

Under **Requirement & validity**, turn on **Required** if every matching worker must take it, pick the **Required for driver types**, and set **Due after**, **Valid for** and **Renewal alert window**.
Select **Save**, or choose **Save & close** from the save button's menu.

tasks.title: Edit a training course
steps: Open [Training courses](/hr/training-courses).
Select the course's row, change the fields, and select **Save** or **Save & close**.

tasks.title: Deactivate or restore courses
steps: Open [Training courses](/hr/training-courses).
Tick the courses, then choose **Deactivate** or **Restore** in the bar at the bottom of the table. You can also right-click a single course.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to training courses and the asset operations feature. **Deactivate** and **Restore** only appear for people allowed to archive and restore courses. - Required courses are assigned automatically on hire, rehire and driver-type change. An overdue, failed or lapsed required course leaves the worker unqualified. - Leave every **Required for driver types** box unchecked to require the course for every worker. A **Due after** of 0 means no due date; leave **Valid for** empty for one-time courses. - Only active courses with no open assignments can be deactivated.

pages.name: Workers
pages.description: Manage and track workers along with their compliance and paid time off
pages.summary:
Workers is the roster of every driver and employee, with their status, tenure, worker type, driver type, fleet code and at-a-glance compliance, training, safety and drug and alcohol standing. HR, safety and operations staff use it to add people, keep their records current and manage paid time off. The **Paid time off** tab lists every time-off request so managers can approve, reject or cancel them, above a chart of approved time off and a list of requested PTO.

Selecting a worker opens their record on the **Overview** tab. The other tabs hold the rest of their file: **General information**, **Employment information** (with its **History** of employment events), **Compliance status**, **Credentials**, **Checklist**, **Training**, **Safety**, **Testing** (drug and alcohol tests and Clearinghouse queries), **DQ file**, **Reviews**, **HOS**, **Pay**, **Time off**, **Schedule**, **Leave**, **Documents** and **Portal** (their Dash sign-in).

tasks.title: Add a worker
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers).
Select **New worker**.
On **General information**, fill in **Status**, **Worker type**, **First name**, **Last name**, **Driver type**, the address and **Phone number**.
On **Employment information**, enter the **Date of birth**, **Hire date**, **License number** and **License expiry**, plus any CDL and medical details.
On **Compliance status**, set the compliance and availability fields if you know them.
Select **Create worker**.

tasks.title: Update a worker's record
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers).
Find the worker with the search box or **Filter**, then select their row.
Go to **General information**, **Employment information** or **Compliance status** and change the fields.
Select **Save** or **Save & close**.
To change several workers at once, tick their rows and use **Update status**, **Update type** or **Update driver type** in the bar at the bottom of the table.

tasks.title: Add or renew a credential
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers) and select the worker's row.
Go to the **Credentials** tab.
Select **Add credential**, or open the actions menu on an existing credential and choose its renew, edit, verify or archive option.
Pick the **Credential type**, fill in **Number**, **Issuing authority**, **Issued** and **Expires**, and attach a scan of the document.
Select **Add credential** (or **Renew credential** when renewing).

tasks.title: Assign training
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers).
Tick the workers who need the training and choose **Assign training** in the bar at the bottom of the table.
Pick the **Courses**, optionally a **Due date** and **Notes**, then confirm.
For one worker, open their row, go to **Training**, and use **Assign course** or **Assign required**. Use **Record result** or **Waive** on a course to close it out.

tasks.title: Request time off for a worker
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers) and select the **Paid time off** tab.
Select the New worker PTO button above the table. You can also open the worker's row, go to **Time off** and select **Request PTO**.
Pick the **Worker** and **Type**, set the **First day** and **Last day**, and add a **Reason**.
Select **Request PTO**. The request waits for approval.

tasks.title: Approve or reject time off
steps: Open [Workers](/hr/workers) and select the **Paid time off** tab.
Tick the requests, then choose **Approve**, **Reject** or **Cancel** in the bar at the bottom of the table. You can also right-click a single request.
Confirm the action, adding a reason where asked.

pages.notes: - The page needs read access to workers and the asset operations feature. Adding a worker needs create access to workers. - Each tab has its own permissions: verifying and archiving credentials, assigning training, recording safety events, and approving, rejecting or cancelling time off are only offered to people allowed to do them. - The **HOS** tab and hours-of-service data come from Samsara; if it is not connected the tab says **Samsara telematics is not connected**. - On the **Safety** tab, **Record event** logs an accident, citation or inspection, **Issue action** adds a step on the **Discipline ladder**, and **Add recognition** records kudos that can be shared to the driver's Dash.

pages.name: Inbox
pages.description: Mail that arrived on a monitored address, what the desk made of each message, and what is still waiting on a person
pages.summary:
The inbox shows mail that arrived on your organization's monitored addresses and what the desk (the AI assistant) made of each message: what kind of mail it is (tender, rate confirmation, proof of delivery, invoice, status request, detention dispute or other), which shipment or customer it is about, how sure it was, and a suggested next step. Customer service, dispatch and billing staff use it to work through the mail the desk could not settle on its own.

It reads like a mail client: folders on the left (**Waiting on you**, **Handled**, **Ignored**, **Everything**, then **By kind** and **Mailboxes**), the message list in the middle, and the open message on the right with its attachments, **What the desk made of it**, and **How it got here**.

tasks.title: Work through mail waiting on you
steps: Open [Inbox](/inbox) and select **Waiting on you**.
Select a message, or press j to open the first one and keep pressing j to go down the list (k goes back).
Read **What the desk made of it** and follow the **Suggested next** step if it fits, such as attaching a document to the shipment it names or opening that shipment.
Optionally note what you did in the box at the bottom, then select **Mark handled** (e) or **Ignore** (#). The next waiting message opens.

tasks.title: Link a message to the right shipment or customer
steps: Open the message in [Inbox](/inbox).
Select **Link by hand** (or press l).
Choose the **Shipment** or **Customer**, fill in **Why this is the right record**, and select **Link**.

tasks.title: Ask the desk to handle a message
steps: Open the message in [Inbox](/inbox).

Select **Ask the desk** (or press a), or the suggested **Ask the desk to answer** / **Ask the desk to build it** button. A desk conversation opens about that message, where you can review what it drafts.

tasks.title: Find a message
steps: Open [Inbox](/inbox) and pick a folder, a kind under **By kind**, or a mailbox under **Mailboxes**.
Type in **Search sender or subject** (or press / to jump there). Search looks at the sender's name and address and the subject.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to inbound messages. Messages the desk could not make sense of are held back and also land in **Waiting on you**.

Monitored addresses are set up under [Inbound mailboxes](/admin/inbound-mailboxes); people who can manage them see a **Manage** link beside **Mailboxes**.

The folder, search and open message are kept in the page address, so a link to a message opens exactly that message.

pages.name: Insights
pages.description: Findings computed from your own records. The figures come from your data; where an explanation was written by AI, the card says so.
pages.summary: Insights lists findings Trenova computes from your own records when service, cash, cost or compliance moves in the wrong direction, such as on-time performance slipping, money earned but not yet collected, or cost the operation is losing quietly. Each card shows its urgency, its area, the figures that triggered it, and a recommendation. The figures always come from your data; where an explanation was written by AI, the card says so. Operations, billing and management staff use it to spot problems and jump to the records behind them.

tasks.title: Review open findings
steps: Open [Insights](/insights). **Open** findings show by default.
Narrow the list with the **Area** chips (**Service**, **Cash**, **Cost**, **Compliance**) and the **Urgency** chips (Critical, Warning, Info).

Select a finding's headline to open its details: **What was measured**, the **Explanation**, **Since last time** (whether it is getting worse, improving or holding steady), and **Why you are seeing this**.

tasks.title: Go to the records behind a finding
steps: Open [Insights](/insights) and select the finding's headline.
Under **The records behind this**, select a link to open the matching records on their own page.

tasks.title: Dismiss a finding
steps: Open [Insights](/insights).
Select **Dismiss** on the card, or open the finding, optionally say why under **Not worth acting on?**, and select **Dismiss for 30 days**.

tasks.title: Bring back a dismissed finding
steps: Open [Insights](/insights) and select the **Dismissed** status chip.
Select **Restore** on the card, or open it and select **Restore this finding**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to insights.

A dismissed finding comes back if its condition is still there after 30 days. **Closed** holds findings a later refresh no longer makes. A card marked **Numbers may be out of date** has not been refreshed recently.

pages.name: Data retention
pages.description: Configure how long audit entries and raw EDI payloads are kept before the nightly purge jobs remove them.
pages.summary:
Data retention sets how long the organization keeps audit entries and raw EDI payloads before the nightly purge jobs remove them. The page is one form, **Retention windows**, with three values in days: **Audit Retention (days)**, **EDI Inbound File Retention (days)** and **EDI Message Retention (days)**.

Administrators use it to balance storage and privacy against how far back people need to look at audit history or replay EDI traffic.

tasks.title: Change how long audit entries are kept
steps: Open [Data retention](/organization/data-retention).
Enter the number of days in **Audit Retention (days)**. It must be at least 1.
Select **Save settings**.

tasks.title: Limit how long raw EDI payloads are kept
steps: Open [Data retention](/organization/data-retention).

Enter the number of days in **EDI Inbound File Retention (days)** for raw inbound EDI file contents, and in **EDI Message Retention (days)** for raw X12 and payload snapshots of delivered and inbound messages.
Enter 0 in either field to keep those raw payloads forever.
Select **Save settings**.

pages.notes:
Opening the page needs read access to the organization; **Save settings** appears only for people with update access to the organization.

Audit entries older than the audit window are deleted by the nightly purge. For EDI, the purge blanks the raw contents but keeps the file and message records and their metadata. A purged EDI message can no longer be replayed from [EDI messages](/edi/messages).

pages.name: Email logs
pages.description: Transactional email send and delivery history.
pages.summary:
Email logs show the organization's transactional email send and delivery history, newest first. Each row lists the **Subject**, the **Purpose** (such as Billing or Notifications), the **Recipients**, the **Status**, the number of send **Attempts** and when it was **Created**. When a send has failed, the last error appears in red under the subject.

Administrators use it to confirm an email went out and to find out why one did not arrive. The page is read-only.

tasks.title: Check whether an email was delivered
steps: Open [Email logs](/organization/email-logs).
Find the message by its **Subject** and **Recipients**.
Read its **Status**: statuses include Queued, Sending, Sent, Delivered, Opened, Clicked, Failed, Bounced, Complained and Suppressed.

tasks.title: Find out why an email failed
steps: Open [Email logs](/organization/email-logs).
Look for rows with a Failed or Bounced **Status**.
Read the error shown under the **Subject**, and check **Attempts** to see how many times the send was tried.
If the problem is the sender, review the profile on [Email profiles](/organization/email-profiles).

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to email logs. The page shows the most recent messages; it has no search or filters.

pages.name: Email Profile(s)
pages.description: Manage verified sender identities and route email purposes to the right provider profile.
pages.summary:
Email profiles are the sender identities the organization sends email from. Each profile names an email provider (Resend or Postmark), the sender name and verified sender email recipients see, and an optional reply-to address.

The **Purpose assignments** panel at the top of the page routes each kind of email to a profile: General, Billing, Reporting, Operations, Authentication and Notifications. Below it, the table lists every profile with its **Profile**, **Sender**, **Provider**, **Status**, **Reply-To** and **Updated** columns. Administrators use the page to set up and maintain outgoing email.

tasks.title: Add an email profile
steps: Open [Email profiles](/organization/email-profiles).
Select **New email profile**.
Enter a **Profile name**, choose the **Status** and **Provider**, and enter the **Sender name** and **Sender email**.
Optionally enter a **Reply-to email** (blank uses the sender email) and a **Description**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Choose which profile sends each kind of email
steps: Open [Email profiles](/organization/email-profiles).
In **Purpose assignments**, pick an active profile for each purpose, such as **Billing**.
Clear a purpose to remove its assignment.
Select **Save assignments**.

tasks.title: Send a test email from a profile
steps: Open [Email profiles](/organization/email-profiles).
Right-click an active profile and choose **Send test**.
Enter the **Recipient email** and select **Send test**.
Check the result on [Email logs](/organization/email-logs).

tasks.title: Edit or delete a profile
steps: Open [Email profiles](/organization/email-profiles).
Select a row to edit it, change the fields and select **Save**.
To delete one, right-click the row, choose **Delete** and confirm with **Delete**. The profile is also removed from any purpose it was assigned to. This cannot be undone.

pages.notes: Viewing the page needs read access to email profiles. Creating, editing, deleting, sending a test and saving purpose assignments each need the matching create, update or delete access. Inactive profiles cannot be assigned to purposes, and **Send test** is only available for active profiles.

pages.name: Pay advances
pages.description: Cash and money-code advances that are automatically recovered from the driver's next settlement.
pages.summary:
Pay advances records cash and money-code advances given to drivers on the road, such as an EFS or Comdata money code, cash or a fuel card advance. The outstanding balance of each advance is recovered automatically from the driver's next settlements, and this page tracks how much has been recovered and how much is still owed.

The table shows each advance's **Status** (outstanding, partially recovered, recovered or written off), **Driver**, **Source**, **Reference**, **Issued** date, **Amount**, **Recovered** and **Outstanding**.

tasks.title: Record an advance
steps: Open [Pay advances](/payroll/advances).
Select **New pay advance**.
Choose the **Driver** and the **Source**, and enter the **Reference** (the money code or check number).
Enter the **Issued date** (the day the driver received the funds) and the **Amount**, and add **Notes** on what it covered.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Check what a driver still owes
steps: Open [Pay advances](/payroll/advances).
Search or use **Filter** to find the driver's advances.
Select an advance to see its **Amount**, **Recovered** and **Outstanding** balance.

tasks.title: Write off an advance
steps: Open [Pay advances](/payroll/advances) and select the advance.
Select **Write off remaining balance**, enter the reason, and confirm with **Write off**.
To write off several at once, tick them and select **Write off** in the bar that appears, then enter one reason and confirm.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to pay advances to open the page; recording and writing off need the matching permissions. The page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Only outstanding or partially recovered advances can be written off. A written-off balance is no longer recovered from future settlements, and the reason is shown on the advance.

A driver's outstanding advances also appear in the right rail of the [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).

pages.name: Recurring deductions
pages.description: Standing per-settlement deductions: insurance, lease payments, escrow contributions, and loan repayments with caps.
pages.summary:
Recurring deductions are standing amounts withheld from a driver's settlements, such as insurance, lease payments, escrow contributions and loan repayments. Each one belongs to one driver, uses a deduction pay code, and is withheld automatically every settlement or once a month until it is paused, reaches its end date, or hits its total cap.

The table shows each deduction's **Status**, **Driver**, **Code**, **Description**, **Frequency**, **Amount** and **Deducted / cap**.

tasks.title: Add a recurring deduction
steps: Open [Recurring deductions](/payroll/deductions).
Select **New recurring deduction**.
Choose the **Driver**, the **Pay code** and the **Frequency** (every settlement, or monthly on the first settlement of each month).
Enter a **Description** and the **Amount per application**. Optionally set a **Total cap**, after which the deduction stops on its own.
Set the **Start date** and, if it should end, an **End date**.
To send the withheld amount into the driver's escrow account, turn on **Contribute to escrow account**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a deduction
steps: Open [Recurring deductions](/payroll/deductions) and select the deduction.
Change the fields, including **Status**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Pause or resume deductions
steps: Open [Recurring deductions](/payroll/deductions) and tick the deductions.
Select **Update status**, then **Pause** or **Resume**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to recurring deductions to open the page; creating and editing need the matching permissions. The page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Paused deductions are skipped on future settlements and keep their history. A completed deduction has reached its cap and has stopped permanently.

An escrow contribution links to the driver's active escrow account when saved, so open an escrow account for the driver in [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts) first. It stops automatically at the account's funding target, and the escrow setting cannot be changed after the deduction is created.

Deductions can also be paused from the right rail of the [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).

pages.name: Disputes
pages.description: Driver-submitted questions and challenges against issued settlements — review, resolve with a correcting adjustment, or deny with an explanation.
pages.summary:
Disputes lists the questions and challenges drivers submit against their issued settlements from the driver portal (Dash). Payroll staff review each one, then either resolve it in the driver's favor, optionally with a correcting adjustment, or deny it with an explanation the driver can read.

The table shows each dispute's **Status** (Open, In review, Resolved, Denied or Withdrawn), **Driver**, **Category**, **Settlement**, **Description**, **Submitted** date and **Resolved** date. Disputes are raised by drivers, so there is no create button on this page.

tasks.title: Start reviewing a dispute
steps: Open [Disputes](/payroll/disputes).
Select an open dispute to see what the driver wrote, the settlement it is about and, when they picked one, the disputed line.
Select **Start review** to move it to In review.
To move several at once, tick the open disputes and select **Start review** in the bar that appears.

tasks.title: Resolve a dispute in the driver's favor
steps: Open [Disputes](/payroll/disputes) and select the dispute.
Under **Resolve this dispute**, select **Resolve in driver's favor**.
Enter a **Resolution note**. The driver sees it word for word in Dash.
To correct the pay, turn on **Apply a correcting adjustment**, enter a description and an amount in dollars (positive adds pay, negative deducts), and optionally choose a **Pay code (optional)**.
Select **Resolve dispute**.

tasks.title: Deny a dispute
steps: Open [Disputes](/payroll/disputes) and select the dispute.
Select **Deny**, enter a **Resolution note** explaining why, and select **Deny dispute**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to settlement disputes to open the page, and the page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

A correcting adjustment is added as a line on the driver's open settlement; if the driver has none, an off-cycle draft settlement is created for it. Choosing a pay code routes the adjustment to that code's GL account when the settlement is posted.

Resolved, denied and withdrawn disputes are final: the panel shows the resolution note, who resolved it and when, and whether a correcting adjustment was applied.

pages.name: Recurring earnings
pages.description: Standing per-settlement earnings: per diem, safety and performance bonuses, stipends, and equipment rental payments with caps.
pages.summary:
Recurring earnings are standing amounts added to a driver's settlements, such as per diem, safety and performance bonuses, stipends and equipment rental payments. Each one belongs to one driver, uses an earning pay code, and is added automatically every settlement or once a month until it is paused, reaches its end date, or hits its total cap.

The table shows each earning's **Status**, **Driver**, **Code**, **Description**, **Frequency**, **Amount** and **Paid / cap**.

tasks.title: Add a recurring earning
steps: Open [Recurring earnings](/payroll/earnings).
Select **New recurring earning**.
Choose the **Driver**, the **Pay code** and the **Frequency** (every settlement, or monthly on the first settlement of each month).
Enter a **Description** and the **Amount per application**. Optionally set a **Total cap**, after which the earning stops on its own.
Set the **Start date** and, if it should end, an **End date**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit an earning
steps: Open [Recurring earnings](/payroll/earnings) and select the earning.
Change the fields, including **Status**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Pause or resume earnings
steps: Open [Recurring earnings](/payroll/earnings) and tick the earnings.
Select **Update status**, then **Pause** or **Resume**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to recurring earnings to open the page; creating and editing need the matching permissions. The page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Paused earnings are skipped on future settlements and keep their history. A completed earning has reached its cap and has stopped permanently.

Earnings can also be paused or resumed from the right rail of the [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).

pages.name: Escrow accounts
pages.description: Owner-operator maintenance escrow with a full transaction ledger and quarterly interest per 49 CFR 376.12(k).
pages.summary:
Escrow accounts holds owner-operator maintenance escrow. Each owner-operator has at most one active account with a funding target and an annual interest rate. Contributions flow in from settlements through a recurring deduction, interest accrues at least quarterly, and every movement is kept on a transaction ledger, as 49 CFR 376.12(k) requires.

The table shows each account's **Status**, **Driver**, **Balance**, **Target**, how far it is **Funded**, **Interest**, the **Opened** date and the **Last interest** date.

tasks.title: Open an escrow account
steps: Open [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts).
Select **New escrow account**.
Choose the **Driver**. Only owner-operators are listed.
Enter the **Funding target** (contributions stop once the balance reaches it) and the **Annual interest rate**, which defaults to your settlement control rate.
Select **Save**.
To start contributions, add a recurring deduction for the driver in [Recurring deductions](/payroll/deductions) with **Contribute to escrow account** turned on.

tasks.title: Review an account's ledger
steps: Open [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts) and select the account.
See the **Balance**, **Target** and **Interest rate**, and every entry in the **Transaction ledger** with its **Date**, **Type**, **Description**, **Amount** and running **Balance**.

tasks.title: Record an escrow adjustment
steps: Open [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts) and select an active account.
Select **Record adjustment**.
Enter the amount in dollars (positive deposits into escrow, negative applies funds out, for example a repair paid from escrow) and a description.
Select **Record**.

tasks.title: Close an escrow account
steps: Open [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts) and select the active account.
Select **Close account** and confirm with **Close account**. The remaining balance is refunded to the driver as a ledger entry.
To close several at once, tick them and select **Close accounts**. From the bulk action, accounts that still hold a balance fail to close until their funds are refunded or applied.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to escrow accounts to open the page; the other actions need the matching permissions. The page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Closing cannot be undone. Closed accounts stop accepting contributions and accruing interest. Adjustment descriptions are recorded permanently on the ledger.

A driver's escrow balance also appears in the right rail of the [Workspace](/payroll/workspace), where **View ledger** opens this page.

pages.name: Driver expenses
pages.description: Driver-submitted out-of-pocket expenses — review receipts, approve to reimburse on the driver's open settlement, or reject with an explanation.
pages.summary:
Driver expenses lists the out-of-pocket expenses drivers submit from the driver portal (Dash). Payroll staff check each receipt, then approve the expense to reimburse it on the driver's open settlement, or reject it with an explanation.

The table shows **Status** (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Reimbursed or Cancelled), **Driver**, **Amount**, **Description**, **Incurred** date, whether a **Receipt** is attached, and the **Submitted** and **Reviewed** dates. Expenses are submitted by drivers, so there is no create button on this page.

tasks.title: Review an expense and its receipt
steps: Open [Driver expenses](/payroll/expenses).
Use the search box, or **Filter** on **Status**, to find pending expenses.
Select the expense to see the amount, what the driver wrote, the pay code and the receipt. Select **View receipt** to open it.

tasks.title: Approve and reimburse an expense
steps: Open [Driver expenses](/payroll/expenses) and select a pending expense.
Under **Review this expense**, keep **Approve & reimburse** selected.
Optionally add a **Note (optional)**, then select **Approve expense**.

tasks.title: Reject an expense
steps: Open [Driver expenses](/payroll/expenses) and select a pending expense.
Select **Reject**, enter the **Rejection reason**, and select **Reject expense**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to driver expenses to open the page, and the page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Approving immediately adds a reimbursement line to the driver's open settlement; if the driver has none, an off-cycle draft settlement is created. The rejection reason is shown to the driver word for word.

Only pending expenses can be reviewed. Once reviewed, the panel shows the note, who reviewed it and when, and whether the reimbursement was applied to a settlement.

pages.name: Pay codes
pages.description: Your carrier's catalog of earning and deduction codes — behavior flags and GL account mappings drive how each code settles and posts.
pages.summary:
Pay codes are your catalog of earning and deduction codes. Every recurring earning, recurring deduction and manual settlement adjustment can carry a code, and the code decides whether it adds or withholds pay, which GL account its settlement lines post to, whether it is taxable, and whether it counts toward a driver's guaranteed minimum. Payroll and accounting managers maintain it.

The table shows each code's **Status**, **Direction**, **Code**, **Name**, **Behavior**, **GL account** and **Default amount**.

tasks.title: Add a pay code
steps: Open [Pay codes](/payroll/pay-codes).
Select **New pay code**.
Choose the **Direction**: earning codes add pay and deduction codes withhold it.
Enter the **Code** (uppercase letters, digits, dashes or underscores, shown on statements) and the **Name**, and optionally a **Description**.
Optionally choose a **GL account** and a **Default amount**, which prefills recurring earnings and deductions that use the code.
For an earning code, set **Taxable** and **Counts toward guaranteed minimum**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a pay code
keywords: change GL account for pay code
steps: Open [Pay codes](/payroll/pay-codes) and select the code.
Change the fields, including **Status**, then select **Save**. The direction cannot be changed after the code is created.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate pay codes
steps: Open [Pay codes](/payroll/pay-codes) and tick the codes.
Select **Update status**, then **Activate** or **Deactivate**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to pay codes to open the page; creating and editing need the matching permissions. The page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

A code with no GL account posts to the accounting control defaults. Taxable amounts post as earnings; non-taxable ones, such as per diem and stipends, post as reimbursements.

Inactive codes stay on historical records but no longer appear in the dropdowns for new entries.

pages.name: Pay events
pages.description: Real-time driver earnings accrued as shipments deliver — the source ledger behind every settlement.
pages.summary:
Pay events are the driver earnings recorded automatically as shipments deliver. Each one is the pay a driver earned on one shipment, worked out from their pay profile, and it is the source every settlement is built from. Payroll staff use this page to check what a driver has earned, see how a load's pay was calculated, and hold pay that should not settle yet.

The table shows **Status** (Accrued, Settled or Voided), **Driver**, **Pro #**, **Earned** date, **Miles**, **Breakdown** and **Gross pay**. Pay events are created by the system, not by hand.

tasks.title: See how a load's pay was calculated
steps: Open [Pay events](/payroll/pay-events).
Search for the pro number or driver, or use **Filter** and **Sort**.
Select the pay event to see each pay **Component** with its **Qty × rate**, **Amount** and the **Total**.

tasks.title: Hold pay so it does not settle yet
steps: Open [Pay events](/payroll/pay-events).
Tick the accrued pay events to hold and select **Hold** in the bar that appears. For a single event you can also hover its status and select the hold icon.
Enter the reason and select **Hold pay**. Held events show **Held** and are skipped by settlement generation until released.

tasks.title: Release held pay
steps: Open [Pay events](/payroll/pay-events).
Select **Held** on the event's status to release it, or tick several held events and select **Release holds**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to driver settlements, and the page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Only accrued pay events that are not already on hold can be held. One reason is recorded on every event held together. Released events settle normally on the next settlement generation.

pages.name: Pay profiles
pages.description: Reusable driver pay packages: mileage rates and bands, revenue percentages, accessorial pay, and guarantees.
pages.summary:
Pay profiles are reusable driver pay packages. A profile holds the pay components a driver earns on each completed move (for example linehaul per mile with optional mileage bands, a percent of revenue, stop pay or detention), plus an optional guaranteed minimum per period and a per diem daily cap. Payroll managers set them up once and assign them to drivers, adding driver-specific rate overrides where one driver's rate differs.

The table shows each profile's **Status**, **Name**, **Type**, **Pay components**, **Guarantee** and number of **Drivers**.

tasks.title: Create a pay profile
steps: Open [Pay profiles](/payroll/pay-profiles).
Select **New pay profile**.
Choose the **Status** and **Classification** (it decides W-2 or 1099 treatment and the GL expense account), and enter a **Name** and **Description**.
Optionally set a **Guaranteed minimum / period** and a **Per diem daily cap**.

Under **Pay components**, select **Add component**, then choose the **Component** and **Method** and enter the rate. For a percent-of-revenue method, also choose the **Revenue basis**. Optionally set a **Label**, **Minimum per move** and **Maximum per move**.
For per-mile pay, select **Add band** to add **Mileage bands** that pay a different rate by length of haul.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a pay profile
steps: Open [Pay profiles](/payroll/pay-profiles) and select the profile.
On the **Profile** tab, change the fields or components, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Assign a pay profile to a driver
steps: Open [Pay profiles](/payroll/pay-profiles) and select the profile.
Open the **Assigned drivers** tab and select **Assign driver**.
Choose the **Driver**, the **Effective From** date and the **Split percent** (100 for a solo driver, 50 each for an even team split), and add **Notes** if needed.
Under **Driver-specific rate overrides**, enter any rate that differs for this driver, then select **Assign profile**.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate profiles
steps: Open [Pay profiles](/payroll/pay-profiles) and tick the profiles.
Select **Update status**, then **Activate** or **Deactivate**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to driver pay profiles to open the page; creating and editing need the matching permissions. The page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

A deactivated profile can no longer be assigned, but drivers already on it keep being paid under it. Drivers can also be assigned from the Pay tab on the worker in [Workers](/hr/workers).

pages.name: Settlement batches
pages.description: Generate pay-period batches, monitor exceptions, and export payroll files.
pages.summary:
Settlement batches are driver payroll runs. Each batch groups the settlements generated for one pay period, and this page is where payroll staff generate a batch for the current period, check how many settlements it holds and how many have exceptions, and download the payroll file.

The table shows each batch's **Status**, **Batch** name, **Period**, **Pay date**, number of **Settlements**, number of **Exceptions**, **Total gross** and **Total net**.

tasks.title: Generate a settlement batch for the current period
steps: Open [Settlement batches](/payroll/settlement-batches).
Select **New settlement batch**. The panel shows the **Current pay period** and its pay date.
Optionally enter a **Batch name** (left blank, it is named after the period end date) and **Notes** for reviewers.
Select **Save**. A draft settlement is created for every driver with accrued pay in the current period.

tasks.title: Review a batch and its exceptions
steps: Open [Settlement batches](/payroll/settlement-batches).
Select a batch to see its period and pay date, its **Settlements**, **Exceptions**, **Total gross** and **Total net**, and every settlement in it with driver, status, gross and net.
Settlements flagged with exceptions are marked with a warning icon. Work them in the [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).

tasks.title: Export the payroll file
steps: Open [Settlement batches](/payroll/settlement-batches) and select the batch.
Select **Export payroll CSV** to download the batch as a CSV file.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to driver settlements to open the page, and the page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Clean settlements can be approved automatically, depending on your settlement control policy; anything with exceptions stays in review.

pages.name: Settlement history
pages.description: Read-only record of every driver and owner-operator settlement across pay periods — process active settlements in the workspace.
pages.summary:
Settlement history is the read-only record of every driver and owner-operator settlement across all pay periods. Payroll and accounting staff use it to look up a past settlement, see its earnings, deductions, net pay and history, and find settlements from earlier periods that are no longer in the workspace queue.

The table shows **Status**, **Settlement #**, **Driver**, **Type**, **Period end**, **Pay date**, **Loads**, **Gross**, **Deductions** and **Net pay**. Settlements are created in the workspace, not here.

tasks.title: Look up a settlement
steps: Open [Settlement history](/payroll/settlements).
Use the search box, or **Filter** and **Sort**, to narrow the list by driver, status, period or pay date.

Select a row to open the settlement. It shows the gross earnings, deductions, miles and loads, net pay, every line item and a **History** of when it was created, submitted, approved, posted, paid or voided.

tasks.title: Work on a settlement that is still open
steps: Open [Settlement history](/payroll/settlements) and select the settlement.
Select **Open in workspace** to process, adjust or pay it in the [Workspace](/payroll/workspace). Paid and voided settlements are final and have no workspace link.

tasks.title: Move several settlements forward at once
steps: Open [Settlement history](/payroll/settlements).
Tick the settlements to act on.
In the bar that appears, choose **Lifecycle action** and pick **Submit for approval**, **Approve** or **Post to GL**; settlements not in an eligible status are skipped.
To record payment, select **Mark paid**, choose the **Payment method**, optionally enter a **Batch reference**, and confirm with **Mark paid**. Only posted settlements can be marked paid.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to driver settlements, and the page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

The first time you open the page, a four-step explainer at the top describes how pay accrues, settlements build, exceptions are reviewed and settlements are posted and paid. Dismiss it with the close button; it stays hidden in that browser.

pages.name: Workspace
pages.description: Everything needed to run a pay period from one screen — review the queue, transfer pay, manage deductions, and process settlements one at a time or in bulk.
pages.summary:
The settlement workspace is where payroll staff run the current driver pay period from one screen. The top strip shows the pay period and pay date and counts what is **In pipeline**, what **Needs review**, what is **Posted / paid**, the **Period net pay**, **Unsettled pay** not yet on a settlement, and pay events **On hold**.

Below it, the queue on the left lists every settlement in the period, the middle pane shows the selected settlement's earnings, deductions and history with the actions for its current status, and the right rail shows the selected driver's unsettled pay, recurring earnings, recurring deductions, advances and escrow.

tasks.title: Generate the period's settlements
steps: Open [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).
Select **Generate settlements**. It builds one draft settlement per driver from the unsettled pay events, pulling in recurring earnings, recurring deductions, advance recoveries and escrow.
Run it again after more pay accrues. Drivers who already have a settlement for the period are skipped, and their new accruals attach to their open draft automatically.

tasks.title: Review and approve a settlement
steps: Open [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).
Find the driver in the queue with **Search driver or number**, or narrow it with the chips (**All**, **Needs review**, **Draft**, **Pending**, **Approved**, **Posted**, **Paid**).
Select the settlement. If it shows **Review required before approval**, read the listed exceptions first.
On a draft, select **Add adjustment** to add or deduct pay, **Recalculate** to rebuild it from current pay events, or remove a pay event line to return it to the unsettled pool.
Select **Submit for approval**, then **Approve** (or **Reject** with a reason to send it back to draft).
Select **Post to GL**, then **Mark paid** and choose the **Payment method** and an optional **Reference**.

tasks.title: Act on several settlements at once
steps: Open [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).
Tick the settlements in the queue, or tick the box above the list to select all visible ones.
Use **Submit**, **Approve**, **Post** or Mark Paid in the bar at the bottom of the queue. Each button shows how many selected settlements are in a status it applies to; the rest are skipped.

tasks.title: Pay a driver off-cycle
steps: Open [Workspace](/payroll/workspace).
Select **Pay now**, choose the **Driver**, and tick the loads to pay.
Decide whether to **Apply recurring deductions, escrow, and advance recovery**, choose the **Payment method**, and optionally enter a **Payment reference**.
Select **Pay now** to build, approve, post and mark the settlement paid in one pass.
To create an off-cycle draft instead, select the **Unsettled pay** tile and use **Settle now** next to the driver, or the generate-for-all button at the bottom of that dialog for everyone listed.

tasks.title: Hold or attach a driver's unsettled pay
steps: Open [Workspace](/payroll/workspace) and select a settlement for the driver.
In the **Unsettled pay** section of the right rail, select **Add to settlement** to attach a pay event to the selected draft.
Select **Hold** to defer a pay event, enter the reason, and select **Hold pay**. Held pay is skipped by settlement generation until you select **Release hold**.

tasks.title: Void a settlement
steps: Open [Workspace](/payroll/workspace) and select the settlement.
Select **Void**, enter the reason, and confirm with **Void**.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to driver settlements, and the page is only available when the organization has the Asset operations capability.

Voiding releases the settlement's pay events back to the unsettled pool and reverses any GL postings. Paid and voided settlements cannot be voided.

**Add adjustment** takes dollars, not cents: a positive amount adds pay and a negative amount deducts it.

To create or edit recurring earnings, recurring deductions or advances, use **Manage** in the right rail, which opens [Recurring earnings](/payroll/earnings), [Recurring deductions](/payroll/deductions) or [Pay advances](/payroll/advances). **View ledger** in the **Escrow** section opens [Escrow accounts](/payroll/escrow-accounts).

pages.name: Report library
pages.description: Build, run, and share reports over your organization's data
pages.summary: The report library is where people find, run, schedule and share reports over the organization's data. **My reports** holds the reports you and your teammates have saved, **Gallery** holds ready-made reports that come with Trenova, and **Dashboards** holds boards of report tiles. Managers, analysts and back-office staff use it to answer questions about shipments, billing and operations and to send results out on a schedule.

tasks.title: Run a report and get the file
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and find the report on **My reports** or **Gallery** (search, **Sort By**, or filter by category or status).
Select **Run** on its card.
Fill in any values the report asks for, choose the **Format** (CSV, Excel (XLSX), PDF or JSON), and select **Run report**.
When it finishes, download the file from [Run history](/reports/runs).

tasks.title: Start from a gallery report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and select **Gallery**.
Select **Explore** to look at the results, **Run** to export them, or **Customize** to copy the report into your own reports and open it in the builder.

tasks.title: Create a report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and select **New report**. The [report builder](/reports/builder) opens.

tasks.title: Schedule a report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and open the report card's actions menu on **My reports**.
Select **Schedules**, then **Add schedule**.

Set the **Cadence** and **Timezone**, the **Formats**, and under **Delivery** the **Email recipients** and **In-app recipients**. Choose whether to **Show the results in the email** and **Attach the report file**.
Optionally, under **Alert**, turn on **Only send when there is something to report** and set the condition.
Leave **Enabled** on and select **Create schedule**.

tasks.title: Manage a saved report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and open the report card's actions menu.
Choose **Explore results**, **Edit in builder**, **Duplicate**, **Schedules**, **Reset to default** (for a report customized from the gallery) or **Delete**.

tasks.title: Build a dashboard
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports), select **Dashboards**, then **New dashboard**. An untitled dashboard opens.

Select **Edit**, enter the **Dashboard name**, and select **Tile** to add a tile: choose what it **Shows**, the **Report**, and the **Chart** or **Measure**, give it a **Title**, and select **Save tile**.
Use **Filters** to add dashboard-wide filters, then select **Save**.
Later, open the dashboard from **Dashboards** and select **Edit** to change it or **Export** to export it.

pages.notes: Needs read access to reports. **New report**, **New dashboard**, **Duplicate** and customizing a gallery report need create permission; **Schedules** needs export permission on reports. Each card shows whether the report is **Shared** or **Private**, set by its **Visibility** when saved.

pages.name: Report builder
pages.description: The report builder is where a custom report is designed.
pages.summary: The report builder is where a custom report is designed. You pick what the report is about (shipments, customers, invoices and so on), add fields from the catalog on the left as columns, and see a **Live preview** of the first rows update as you build. The inspector on the right sets **Columns**, **Filters**, **Charts**, **Options** (sorting, row limit, totals and pivot) and **Params** (values people fill in when they run it). Analysts, managers and back-office staff use it to build the reports the rest of the team runs.

tasks.title: Build a new report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and select **New report**, or open the [report builder](/reports/builder) directly.
Under **What is this report about?**, pick the entity.

Search the field catalog (**Search fields...**) and add fields. On **Columns**, set each column's **Kind** (**Dimension** or **Measure**), its **Aggregation** for measures, a **Bucket** for dates, and a **Column name**. Select **Calculation** to add a computed column.
On **Filters**, add **Row filters** and **Measure filters**; use **Condition** and **Group** with **Match all** or **Match any**.
On **Options**, set the **Sort**, **Row limit** and **Total row**, and a **Pivot** if needed.
Select **Save**, then enter the **Name**, **Description**, **Category**, **Default format**, **Visibility**, **Status** and **Tags**, and select **Save report**.

tasks.title: Add a chart
steps: Open the report in the [report builder](/reports/builder) and add at least one measure column.
On **Charts**, select **Chart**, choose its **Type**, set the **Horizontal axis** or **Group by** column and the **Measures**, and adjust options such as **Stacked**, **Show values** and **Legend**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Let people choose values when they run it
steps: Open the report in the [report builder](/reports/builder) and go to **Params**.
Select **Parameter**, set its **Label**, **Type**, **Default**, whether it is **Required** or **Multiple**, and any **Allowed values**.
On **Filters**, point a condition at the parameter instead of a **Fixed value**, then select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit an existing report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports), open the report card's actions menu, and select **Edit in builder**.
Make the changes and select **Save**, then **Save report** to keep them. Saving creates a new revision.
Select **Run** to run the saved report.

pages.notes: Needs create permission for reports. **Save** stays disabled until the report has at least one column, and **Run** works only for a report whose status is **Active**. A report flagged **Needs attention** has a problem (for example a field that no longer exists) described at the top of the builder.

pages.name: Explore report
pages.description: Explore opens a saved report or a gallery report as a live result you can read on screen before exporting it.
pages.summary: Explore opens a saved report or a gallery report as a live result you can read on screen before exporting it. It shows the report's rows in a **Table** view and one view per chart the report defines, lets you filter the rows and choose which **Columns** show, and lets you drill into an aggregated number to see the records behind it. If the report takes values (such as a date range or customer), you fill them in at the top.

tasks.title: Explore a report
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and select a report card (or **Explore** on a **Gallery** card).
Fill in any values the report asks for across the top.
Switch between **Table** and the report's charts. Type in **Filter these rows...** to narrow what shows, and use **Columns** to hide or show columns.

tasks.title: See the records behind a number
keywords: which records make up this total
steps: Explore the report from the [Report library](/reports).
Select an aggregated value in the results. **Records behind this number** opens with the individual records that value was built from.

tasks.title: Export what you are looking at
steps: Explore the report from the [Report library](/reports).
Select **Export**, choose the **Format**, and select **Run report**. The file is ready in [Run history](/reports/runs).

tasks.title: Change the report
steps: Explore a saved report from the [Report library](/reports) and select **Edit** to open it in the [report builder](/reports/builder).

pages.notes: Needs read access to reports. Gallery reports cannot be edited directly; customize them from the **Gallery** tab first. When the results show "row limit reached", the report returned more rows than it displays; export it to get them all.

pages.name: Run history
pages.description: Track report generation, download artifacts, and cancel active runs
pages.summary: Run history lists every report run in your organization: which report, its **Status**, **Format**, **Trigger** (for example run by hand or by a schedule), how many **Rows** it returned, its **Size** and **Duration**, when it was requested (**Requested At**) and when its file **Expires**. Anyone who runs or schedules reports uses it to download finished files and to cancel runs that are still in progress.

tasks.title: Download a finished report
steps: Open [Run history](/reports/runs).
Find the run (filter or sort by **Status**, **Format** or **Requested At** if needed).
Select the row, or right-click it and choose **Download**. Only finished runs whose file has not expired can be downloaded.

tasks.title: Cancel a running report
steps: Open [Run history](/reports/runs).
Right-click the queued or running run and choose **Cancel run**.

tasks.title: Run a report again
steps: Open the [Report library](/reports) and find the report.
Select **Run**, choose the **Format**, and select **Run report**. The new run appears in [Run history](/reports/runs).

pages.notes: Needs read access to reports. Downloading needs export permission on reports. Report files are kept for a limited time; after the time in **Expires**, the file can no longer be downloaded and the report has to be run again. A row marked **(truncated)** returned more rows than the run could hold.

pages.name: Commodities
pages.description: Manage and configure commodities for your organization
pages.summary: Commodities describe the goods your organization hauls: name and description, NMFC freight class, a linked hazardous material if the goods are hazmat, weight and linear feet per unit, maximum quantity per shipment, temperature range, and handling notes such as stackable, fragile and loading instructions. Shipments list the commodities they carry, so these records feed weight, hazmat and temperature handling on the load.

tasks.title: Add a commodity
steps: Open [Commodities](/shipment-management/configuration-files/commodities).
Select **New commodity**.
Fill in **Status**, **Name** and **Description**.

Optionally set **Freight class** and link a **Hazardous material**, then fill in **Weight per unit**, **Linear feet per unit**, **Max qty per shipment**, **Min temperature**, **Max temperature**, **Stackable**, **Fragile** and **Loading instructions**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a commodity
steps: Open [Commodities](/shipment-management/configuration-files/commodities).
Select the row, or right-click it and choose **Edit**.
Change the fields and select **Save**.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate several commodities
steps: Open [Commodities](/shipment-management/configuration-files/commodities).
Tick the rows to change.
Select **Update status** in the bar that appears and choose **Active** or **Inactive**.

pages.notes:
The hazardous material you link must already exist on [Hazardous materials](/shipment-management/configuration-files/hazardous-materials).

Adding needs create permission for commodities; editing needs update permission.

pages.name: Hazardous materials
pages.description: Manage and configure hazardous materials for your organization
pages.summary: The hazardous materials list holds the hazmat records your organization ships: name, DOT hazard class, UN number, packing group, proper shipping name, emergency contact and compliance flags such as placards and marine pollutants. A commodity can be linked to one of these records. Safety, compliance and operations staff maintain it.

tasks.title: Add a hazardous material from the DOT reference
steps: Open [Hazardous materials](/shipment-management/configuration-files/hazardous-materials).
Select **New hazardous material**.

Type at least two characters of the material name in **Name** and pick a match from the list. The match fills **Name**, **Proper shipping name**, **Description**, **UN number**, **Class** and, where the reference has them, **Subsidiary hazard class**, **Special provisions** and **ERG guide number**.

Check the filled values and complete the rest: **Status**, **Packing group**, **Emergency contact**, **Emergency contact phone**, **Handling instructions** and the compliance switches (**Placard required**, **Marine pollutant**, **Inhalation hazard**, **Reportable quantity**).
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Edit a hazardous material
steps: Open [Hazardous materials](/shipment-management/configuration-files/hazardous-materials).
Select the row, or right-click it and choose **Edit**.
Change the fields and select **Save**. The **Code** is generated by the system and cannot be edited.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate several hazardous materials
steps: Open [Hazardous materials](/shipment-management/configuration-files/hazardous-materials).
Tick the rows to change.
Select **Update status** in the bar that appears and choose **Active** or **Inactive**.

pages.notes:
**Name**, **Status**, **Description** and **Class** are required. When **Reportable quantity** is on, **Reportable quantity threshold** is required too.

Adding needs create permission for hazardous materials; editing needs update permission.

pages.name: Service types
pages.description: Manage and configure service types for your organization
pages.summary: Service types are the levels of service your organization offers on a shipment. Each service type has a **Code**, a **Description**, an optional **Color** and a **Status**, and shipments pick one. Administrators and operations leads maintain the list.

tasks.title: Add a service type
steps: Open [Service types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/service-types).
Select **New service type**.
Choose a **Status**, fill in **Code**, and optionally a **Description** and **Color**.
Select **Save**, or pick **Save & close** or **Save & add another** from the arrow on the save button.

tasks.title: Edit a service type
steps: Open [Service types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/service-types).
Select the row to open it in the side panel, or right-click it and choose **Edit**.
Change the fields and select **Save**.
To change only the **Code** or **Description**, hover the cell in the table and select its pencil icon to edit it in place.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate several service types
steps: Open [Service types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/service-types).
Tick the rows to change.
Select **Update status** in the bar that appears and choose **Active** or **Inactive**.

pages.notes: Adding a service type needs create permission for service types, and editing needs update permission.

pages.name: Shipment types
pages.description: Manage and configure shipment types for your organization
pages.summary: Shipment types are the categories your organization puts shipments into, such as a kind of freight or load. Each type has a **Code**, a **Description**, an optional **Color** and a **Status**. Shipments pick a shipment type, so this list is set up by an administrator or operations lead and kept short.

tasks.title: Add a shipment type
steps: Open [Shipment types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/shipment-types).
Select **New shipment type**.
Choose a **Status**, fill in **Code**, and optionally a **Description** and **Color**.
Select **Save**. Use the arrow on the save button to pick **Save & close** or **Save & add another** instead.

tasks.title: Edit a shipment type
steps: Open [Shipment types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/shipment-types).
Select the row to open it in the side panel, or right-click the row and choose **Edit**.
Change the fields and select **Save**.
To change only the **Code** or **Description**, hover the cell in the table and select its pencil icon to edit it in place.

tasks.title: Activate or deactivate several shipment types
steps: Open [Shipment types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/shipment-types).
Tick the rows to change.
In the bar that appears, select **Update status** and choose **Active** or **Inactive**.

tasks.title: Find a shipment type
steps: Open [Shipment types](/shipment-management/configuration-files/shipment-types).
Type in the search box, or select **Filter** to add conditions on columns such as **Status**.

pages.notes: Adding a shipment type needs create permission for shipment types, and editing needs update permission; without update permission the row opens read-only.

pages.name: Orders
pages.description: Manage and track orders for your organization
pages.summary: An order is the customer's commercial request that one or more shipments carry out. Each shipment attached to an order is a leg. The order holds the customer, owner, PO number and BOL, the quoted price and currency, order-level charges (such as customs brokerage or order-wide fuel), and an accounts receivable rollup across every leg. Customer service and billing staff use it to track multi-leg work and invoice the legs together.

tasks.title: Create an order
steps: Open [Orders](/shipment-management/orders).
Select **New order**.
Under **General information**, choose the **Status**, **Customer** and **Owner**, and enter the **PO number** and **BOL**. The **Order number** is generated for you.
Under **Commercial**, choose the **Currency** and enter the **Quoted amount** and **Base amount**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Attach shipments to an order
steps: Open [Orders](/shipment-management/orders) and select the order.
Under **Legs**, select **Add legs** (or **Add first leg**).
Pick the shipments to attach and select **Add leg** (the button counts the legs when you pick several).
To take a shipment off the order, select **Detach leg** on its row and confirm. The shipment moves onto its own order.

tasks.title: Invoice an order's legs
steps: Open the order from [Orders](/shipment-management/orders).
Under **Legs**, tick the legs to bill (legs in a status that cannot be invoiced cannot be ticked).
Select the create-invoice button. Billing a single leg on its own asks you to confirm with **Create invoice**.

tasks.title: Add an order-level charge
steps: Open the order from [Orders](/shipment-management/orders).
Under **Order charges**, select **Add charge** (or **Add first charge**).
Enter the **Description** and **Amount**, then select **Add charge**. Use **Edit charge** or **Remove charge** on a row to change it later; invoiced charges are marked **Invoiced**.

tasks.title: Close or cancel an order
steps: Open the order from [Orders](/shipment-management/orders).
Under **Accounts receivable**, select **Close order** once the order is billed, or **Cancel order**, enter the reason for cancellation, and confirm with **Cancel order**.

pages.notes: Needs read access to orders; creating and editing need create and update permission. The **Accounts receivable**, **Legs** and **Order charges** sections appear only on an existing order. Canceling an order cancels every remaining leg. **Close order** is offered only when the order's status is Billed.

pages.name: Recurring shipments
pages.description: Automatically generate shipments for repeating lanes on a schedule you control
pages.summary: A recurring shipment is a series that copies a source shipment on a schedule, so a lane that repeats (a weekly run for the same customer, for example) is booked without re-entering it. Each series sets when pickups happen, in which timezone, how many days ahead the shipment is created, when the series starts and ends, which days are blocked, and whether shipments are created automatically or only on demand. Dispatch and customer service staff set these up for their repeating freight.

tasks.title: Set up a recurring shipment
steps: Open [Recurring shipments](/shipment-management/recurring-shipments).
Select **New recurring shipment**.
Under **Series**, enter a **Name**, choose the **Status**, pick the **Source shipment** to copy (search by Pro number or BOL), and add a **Description** if useful.

Under **Schedule**, set how often pickups happen (every day, week, month or a custom schedule) and at what time, the **Timezone**, and the **Lead time** in days before pickup that the shipment is created.
Under **Series window**, optionally set a **Start date**, an **End date** and **Max occurrences**.

Under **Blocked days**, turn on **Skip weekends** if needed, add **Blackout dates** (or **Add US federal holidays** from **Holidays**), and choose the **Exception policy** for a pickup that lands on a blocked day.
Under **Generation**, leave **Generate shipments automatically** on, or turn it off to keep the series as an on-demand template.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Create the next shipment now
steps: Open [Recurring shipments](/shipment-management/recurring-shipments).
Open the series' row menu and select **Generate now**. Expired series cannot generate.

tasks.title: Pause or resume a series
steps: Open [Recurring shipments](/shipment-management/recurring-shipments).
Open the series' row menu and select **Pause / resume**.

tasks.title: See what a series has generated
steps: Open [Recurring shipments](/shipment-management/recurring-shipments).
Open the series' row menu and select **View history** to see its **Generation history**, including any occurrence the exception policy moved.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to recurring shipments; creating and editing need create and update permission.

The **Exception policy** either skips the occurrence (**Skip the occurrence**) or pulls the pickup earlier (**Move to previous business day**). Changing the schedule recalculates the next pickup; shipments already generated are never changed. A series expires once it reaches its end date or its occurrence cap.

When you enter a shipment on [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) that looks like a repeating lane, the shipment form may suggest **Set up recurring shipment**, or offer **Generate from series** when a series already covers the lane.

pages.name: Service failures
pages.description: Review unresolved pickup and delivery service failures
pages.summary:
Service failures lists every late or missed pickup and delivery: late pickup, late delivery, missed pickup, missed delivery, appointment missed or other. Most are detected automatically from stop times; others come in manually, over EDI or from an integration (the **Source** column says which). Each row shows the shipment and stop, how late it was, the reason, notes and when it was detected. Operations and customer service staff use it to assign a reason to each failure, review it and close it out, and to report the failure to the customer by EDI 214.

A failure moves through Open, Reviewed and Resolved, or is Voided when it should not count.

tasks.title: Work the open service failures
steps: Open [Service failures](/shipment-management/service-failures).
Filter the **Status** column to Open, and by **Type** or **Source** if needed.
Select a failure to open it, choose the **Reason code**, and add **Operations notes** (customer-facing) and **Internal notes**.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Review, resolve or void a failure
steps: Open [Service failures](/shipment-management/service-failures).
Right-click the failure and choose **Review**, **Resolve** or **Void**. **Review** and **Resolve** need a reason code on the failure first; **Void** asks for a reason.

tasks.title: Override the EDI codes for one failure
steps: Open the failure from [Service failures](/shipment-management/service-failures).
Under **EDI overrides**, set the **Status code**, **Reason code** or **Exception code** to send for this failure only.
Select **Save**.

tasks.title: Build the EDI 214 payload
steps: Open [Service failures](/shipment-management/service-failures).
Right-click the failure and choose **Build EDI 214 payload**. The payload is copied to your clipboard, with any diagnostics listed in the confirmation.

tasks.title: Check one shipment's failures
steps: Open the shipment from [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) and go to its service failures tab.
Select **Evaluate** to check its stops for new failures, and review, resolve or void them there.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to service failures. **Review** needs approve permission, **Resolve** and editing need update permission, **Void** needs archive permission, and **Build EDI 214 payload** needs export permission. Failures cannot be created from this page.

Reason codes are maintained under [Service failure reason codes](/admin/service-failure-reason-codes).

pages.name: Shipments
pages.description: Operations command center for shipments, assignments, and exceptions.
pages.summary:
Shipments is the operations command center. The top rail shows shipment KPIs, the map shows where loads are, and the side panels (**Unassigned**, **Exceptions** and other watch lists) surface work that needs a person. The table below lists every shipment with its status, customer, stops and coverage; selecting a row expands it to show the route timeline, financials, documents and quick actions. Dispatchers, customer service and billing staff work loads from here.

Opening a shipment shows its full record in a side panel: **Details** (general information, service and classification, billing and rating, commodities and moves), plus service failures, **Documents**, **Comments** and **History**.

tasks.title: Create a shipment
steps: Open [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) and select **New shipment**.
Under **General information**, enter the **BOL** and other reference details.
Under **Service & classification**, choose the **Service type** and **Shipment type**, and the **Tractor type** and **Trailer type** if needed.
Under **Billing & rating**, choose the **Customer**, check **Bill To**, and set the **Rating method** and **Base rate**.
Under **Move details**, select **Add first move** and add at least one pickup and one delivery stop.
Select **Save** (or **Save & close**).

tasks.title: Find a shipment
steps: Open [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments).
Type in **Search shipments...**, or pick a view such as **All shipments**, **In transit**, **At risk**, **Unassigned** or **Delivering today**.
Narrow further with the **At risk**, **Reefer** and **Today** chips or with **Filter**, and switch between **Table** and **Timeline**.
Select a row to expand it, or choose **Edit** from its row menu to open the full shipment.

tasks.title: Assign a driver or carrier to a move
steps: Open the shipment from [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) (**Edit**) and go to **Move details**. The shipment must be saved first.
Open the move's menu and select **Assign** (or **Reassign**).
Choose **Driver** to set the **Tractor**, **Trailer**, **Primary worker** and **Secondary worker**, or **Carrier** to broker the move to an outside carrier with its rate and reference details.
Save the assignment. To take it back, use **Unassign** or **Cancel carrier assignment** from the same menu.

tasks.title: Send a shipment to billing
steps: Open [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) and open the shipment's row menu (or expand the row).
Select **Mark ready to bill**, **Transfer to billing**, or **Mark ready & transfer to billing**. Only the actions that fit the shipment's current state are shown.

tasks.title: Duplicate, transfer or cancel a shipment
steps: Open [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) and open the shipment's row menu.
Select **Duplicate**, set the **Number of copies** and whether to **Override dates**, then **Duplicate**. Copies are made in the background.
Or select **Transfer ownership**, choose the **New owner**, and confirm.
Or select **Cancel**, optionally enter a **Cancel reason**, and select **Cancel shipment**. A canceled shipment can be restored with **Uncancel**.

tasks.title: Send an EDI load tender
steps: Open [Shipments](/shipment-management/shipments) and open the row menu of a shipment in New status whose customer has an EDI partner.
Select **Send EDI load tender** and confirm.

pages.notes:
Needs read access to shipments; **New shipment** appears only with create permission. **Send EDI load tender** needs create access to EDI. An invoiced shipment is locked and cannot be edited.

To create a shipment from a rate confirmation document instead of typing it, use [Import from rate confirmation](/shipment-management/shipments/import).

pages.name: Import from rate confirmation
pages.description: This page creates a shipment from a customer's rate confirmation document.
pages.summary: This page creates a shipment from a customer's rate confirmation document. You upload a PDF or image, Trenova extracts the shipment details (customer, stops, dates, rates and references), and you review each extracted field beside a preview of the document before creating the shipment. An AI assistant panel helps fill in or correct fields and says when the draft is ready. Customer service and dispatch staff use it to enter tendered loads without retyping them.

tasks.title: Create a shipment from a rate confirmation
steps: Open [Import from rate confirmation](/shipment-management/shipments/import).
Under **Upload rate confirmation**, drop or choose a PDF, JPG, PNG or WEBP file. Extraction starts automatically and usually takes a few seconds.

Review the fields next to the document preview. Select **Accept confident** to accept every field the extraction is sure of, and use **Issues only** to see just the fields that need review, are missing or conflict.
Complete **Required details**: **Customer**, **Service type**, **Shipment type** and **Rating method** (plus **Tractor type** and **Trailer type** if needed).
Check **Stops**, match each stop to a location, and correct any names, addresses, dates or windows.
Select **Create shipment**. The source document is attached to the new shipment.
Select **Open shipments** to go to the shipment list, or **Done**.

tasks.title: Recover from a failed extraction
steps: On [Import from rate confirmation](/shipment-management/shipments/import), if extraction fails, select **Retry** to run it again.
Or select **Replace file** to start over with a different document.

pages.notes: Needs create permission for shipments. If the shipment is created but the document could not be attached, the success screen says so; attach the document from the shipment's **Documents** tab.
